86// Stamp the producing thread id into every entry, for the %t pattern flag.
87// Turning this off drops the per-call capture (one thread-local read) and
88// leaves every entry carrying thread id 0. The LogEntry layout stays the same:
89// the field is always reserved, so processes sharing a segment stay
90// attach-compatible whatever each of them chose here.
91#ifndef SLICK_LOGGER_ENABLE_THREAD_ID
92#define SLICK_LOGGER_ENABLE_THREAD_ID 1
93#endif
94
95// Count entries a producer overwrote before the writer thread read them, reported as
96// LogStats::entry_loss_count. Off by default. Costs the writer thread a compare per read
97// and an atomic add per lossy read; producers pay nothing. See the note below.
98#ifndef SLICK_LOGGER_ENABLE_LOSS_DETECTION
99#define SLICK_LOGGER_ENABLE_LOSS_DETECTION 0
100#endif
101
102// Producers claim queue slots with a CAS on one shared reservation counter. When two
103// threads log at the same instant only one CAS succeeds, and the loser retries. On by
104// default, the loser first executes a pause/yield instruction. Off retries immediately,
105// which can shave latency with few producers per core but hammers the contended cache
106// line with many. A single producer thread never loses the race and never pays for it.
107//
108// Both switches change the queue type Logger holds, so every translation unit and every
109// shared library sharing a Logger (Logger::set_instance) must agree on them. Processes
110// sharing a segment need not: neither changes the shared-memory layout.
111#ifndef SLICK_LOGGER_ENABLE_CPU_RELAX
112#define SLICK_LOGGER_ENABLE_CPU_RELAX 1
113#endif
114
115// The OS thread id, for entries (%t) and for thread rings. Debuggers, `top -H`
116// and ETW all show it, which is worth a little platform code over hashing
117// std::thread::id. These are declared here instead of coming from <windows.h>,
118// which this header keeps out of every translation unit that logs. The
119// declarations are identical to the SDK's, so including <windows.h> before or
120// after this is fine. FlushProcessWriteBuffers is the writer's side of the
121// thread-ring park handshake; see detail::writer_barrier().
122#if defined(_WIN32)
123extern "C" __declspec(dllimport) unsigned long __stdcall GetCurrentThreadId(void);
124extern "C" __declspec(dllimport) void __stdcall FlushProcessWriteBuffers(void);
125// Process liveness for shared-memory mode; see detail::process_running().
126struct _FILETIME;
127extern "C" __declspec(dllimport) void* __stdcall OpenProcess(unsigned long, int, unsigned long);
128extern "C" __declspec(dllimport) int __stdcall CloseHandle(void*);
129extern "C" __declspec(dllimport) unsigned long __stdcall WaitForSingleObject(void*, unsigned long);
130extern "C" __declspec(dllimport) int __stdcall GetProcessTimes(void*, _FILETIME*, _FILETIME*, _FILETIME*, _FILETIME*);
131extern "C" __declspec(dllimport) unsigned long __stdcall GetLastError(void);
132#elif defined(__linux__)
133# include <sys/syscall.h> // SYS_gettid, __NR_membarrier
134# include <signal.h> // kill(pid, 0)
135# include <cerrno>
136#elif defined(__APPLE__)
137# include <pthread.h>
138# include <signal.h>
139# include <cerrno>
140# include <libproc.h> // proc_pidinfo
141#elif !defined(_WIN32)
142# include <signal.h>
143# include <cerrno>
144#endif

215inline constexpr const char* file_name_from_path(const char* path) noexcept {
216 if (!path) {
217 return nullptr;
218 }
219 const char* file_name = path;
220 for (const char* current = path; *current != '\0'; ++current) {
221 if (*current == '/' || *current == '\\') {
222 file_name = current + 1;
223 }
224 }
225 return file_name;
226}

238inline void write_2_digits(char* out, uint32_t value) noexcept {
239 out[0] = kDigitPairs[value * 2];
240 out[1] = kDigitPairs[value * 2 + 1];
241}
242
246inline void write_6_digits(char* out, uint32_t value) noexcept {
247 write_2_digits(out, value / 10000);
248 write_2_digits(out + 2, (value / 100) % 100);
249 write_2_digits(out + 4, value % 100);
250}
251
255inline void write_3_digits(char* out, uint32_t value) noexcept {
256 out[0] = static_cast<char>('0' + value / 100);
257 write_2_digits(out + 1, value % 100);
258}
259
263inline void write_9_digits(char* out, uint32_t value) noexcept {
264 out[0] = static_cast<char>('0' + value / 100000000);
265 write_2_digits(out + 1, (value / 1000000) % 100);
266 write_2_digits(out + 3, (value / 10000) % 100);
267 write_2_digits(out + 5, (value / 100) % 100);
268 write_2_digits(out + 7, value % 100);
269}
270
275SLICK_LOGGER_FORCE_INLINE void write_subsecond(char* out, uint32_t subsecond_ns, uint32_t digits) noexcept {
276 switch (digits) {
277 case 3: write_3_digits(out, subsecond_ns / 1000000u); break;
278 case 6: write_6_digits(out, subsecond_ns / 1000u); break;
279 default: write_9_digits(out, subsecond_ns); break;
280 }
281}

284inline constexpr size_t kMaxUint32Digits = 10;
286inline constexpr size_t kMaxUint64Digits = 20;
287
289template <typename UInt>
290inline char* write_uint_backward_as(char* end, UInt value) noexcept {
291 char* p = end;
292 while (value >= 100) {
293 const UInt quotient = value / 100;
294 p -= 2;
295 write_2_digits(p, static_cast<uint32_t>(value - quotient * 100));
296 value = quotient;
297 }
298 if (value >= 10) {
299 p -= 2;
300 write_2_digits(p, static_cast<uint32_t>(value));
301 } else {
302 *--p = static_cast<char>('0' + value);
303 }
304 return p;
305}
306
308SLICK_LOGGER_NOINLINE inline char* write_uint64_backward(char* end, uint64_t value) noexcept {
309 return write_uint_backward_as(end, value);
310}
311
320inline char* write_uint_backward(char* end, uint64_t value) noexcept {
321 if (value > UINT32_MAX) [[unlikely]] {
322 return write_uint64_backward(end, value);
323 }
324 return write_uint_backward_as(end, static_cast<uint32_t>(value));
325}
326
333inline void append_uint(std::string& out, uint64_t value) {
334 char buf[kMaxUint64Digits];
335 char* const end = buf + sizeof(buf);
336 const char* begin = write_uint_backward(end, value);
337 out.append(begin, static_cast<size_t>(end - begin));
338}

357template <typename String>
358void grow_uninitialized(String& s, size_t size) {
359 constexpr auto keep_all = [](char*, size_t n) noexcept { return n; };
360 if constexpr (requires { s.resize_and_overwrite(size, keep_all); }) {
361 s.resize_and_overwrite(size, keep_all);
362 } else if constexpr (requires { s._Resize_and_overwrite(size, keep_all); }) {
363 s._Resize_and_overwrite(size, keep_all);
364 } else if constexpr (requires { s.__resize_and_overwrite(size, keep_all); }) {
365 s.__resize_and_overwrite(size, keep_all);
366 } else {
367 s.resize(size);
368 }
369}

384class line_writer {
385public:
386 line_writer(std::string& out, size_t bound) : out_(out) { reserve_tail(out.size(), bound); }
387 line_writer(const line_writer&) = delete;
388 line_writer& operator=(const line_writer&) = delete;
389
390 // Forced inline: every piece of every line comes through here, and most are
391 // short enough that the call would cost more than the copy.
392 SLICK_LOGGER_FORCE_INLINE void put(const char* data, size_t size) noexcept {
393 assert(size <= static_cast<size_t>(end_ - cursor_));
394 copy_bytes(cursor_, data, size);
395 cursor_ += size;
396 }
397 SLICK_LOGGER_FORCE_INLINE void put(std::string_view text) noexcept { put(text.data(), text.size()); }
398 void put(char c) noexcept {
399 assert(cursor_ < end_);
400 *cursor_++ = c;
401 }
402 void put_uint(uint64_t value) noexcept {
403 char buf[kMaxUint64Digits];
404 char* const end = buf + sizeof(buf);
405 const char* begin = write_uint_backward(end, value);
406 put(begin, static_cast<size_t>(end - begin));
407 }
408
410 char* cursor() noexcept { return cursor_; }
411 void advance(size_t size) noexcept {
412 assert(size <= static_cast<size_t>(end_ - cursor_));
413 cursor_ += size;
414 }
415
418 size_t offset() const noexcept { return static_cast<size_t>(cursor_ - out_.data()); }
419
426 void pad_from(size_t start, size_t width, bool left_align) noexcept {
427 const size_t written = offset() - start;
428 if (written >= width) {
429 return;
430 }
431 const size_t pad = width - written;
432 assert(pad <= static_cast<size_t>(end_ - cursor_));
433 if (!left_align) {
434 // The field is already at the tail, so this shifts only its own
435 // bytes, not the line before it.
436 char* field = out_.data() + start;
437 std::memmove(field + pad, field, written);
438 std::memset(field, ' ', pad);
439 } else {
440 std::memset(cursor_, ' ', pad);
441 }
442 cursor_ += pad;
443 }
444
452 template <typename Append>
453 void append_unbounded(Append&& append) {
454 const size_t remaining = static_cast<size_t>(end_ - cursor_);
455 finish();
456 append(out_);
457 reserve_tail(out_.size(), remaining);
458 }
459
461 void finish() { out_.resize(offset()); }
462
463private:
472 static SLICK_LOGGER_FORCE_INLINE void copy_bytes(char* dst, const char* src, size_t size) noexcept {
473 if (size > 16) {
474 std::memcpy(dst, src, size);
475 } else if (size >= 8) {
476 uint64_t head, tail;
477 std::memcpy(&head, src, 8);
478 std::memcpy(&tail, src + size - 8, 8);
479 std::memcpy(dst, &head, 8);
480 std::memcpy(dst + size - 8, &tail, 8);
481 } else if (size >= 4) {
482 uint32_t head, tail;
483 std::memcpy(&head, src, 4);
484 std::memcpy(&tail, src + size - 4, 4);
485 std::memcpy(dst, &head, 4);
486 std::memcpy(dst + size - 4, &tail, 4);
487 } else if (size != 0) {
488 // 1 to 3 bytes: first, middle and last cover every case.
489 dst[0] = src[0];
490 dst[size / 2] = src[size / 2];
491 dst[size - 1] = src[size - 1];
492 }
493 }
494
495 void reserve_tail(size_t used, size_t bound) {
496 grow_uninitialized(out_, used + bound);
497 cursor_ = out_.data() + used;
498 end_ = cursor_ + bound;
499 }
500
501 std::string& out_;
502 char* cursor_ = nullptr;
503 char* end_ = nullptr;
504};

538inline constexpr size_t kDateTimeLen = 19;
539inline constexpr size_t kTimeOffset = 11; // index of "HH" within the prefix
540inline constexpr size_t kTimeLen = 8; // "HH:MM:SS"
541
550struct second_cache {
551 int64_t seconds = INT64_MIN; // whole seconds since epoch, or INT64_MIN if empty
552 char date_time[kDateTimeLen] = {}; // "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"
553 std::tm tm = {}; // for CUSTOM formats, which still need put_time
554};
555
557inline bool to_local_tm(time_t time_val, std::tm& tm) noexcept {
558#if defined(_WIN32)
559 return localtime_s(&tm, &time_val) == 0;
560#else
561 return localtime_r(&time_val, &tm) != nullptr;
562#endif
563}
564
568inline const second_cache* cached_second(int64_t seconds) noexcept {
569 thread_local second_cache cache;
570 if (cache.seconds != seconds) [[unlikely]] {
571 std::tm tm;
572 if (!to_local_tm(static_cast<time_t>(seconds), tm)) {
573 return nullptr;
574 }
575 char* out = cache.date_time;
576 const uint32_t year = static_cast<uint32_t>(tm.tm_year + 1900);
577 write_2_digits(out, year / 100);
578 write_2_digits(out + 2, year % 100);
579 out[4] = '-';
580 write_2_digits(out + 5, static_cast<uint32_t>(tm.tm_mon + 1));
581 out[7] = '-';
582 write_2_digits(out + 8, static_cast<uint32_t>(tm.tm_mday));
583 out[10] = ' ';
584 write_2_digits(out + 11, static_cast<uint32_t>(tm.tm_hour));
585 out[13] = ':';
586 write_2_digits(out + 14, static_cast<uint32_t>(tm.tm_min));
587 out[16] = ':';
588 write_2_digits(out + 17, static_cast<uint32_t>(tm.tm_sec));
589 cache.tm = tm;
590 cache.seconds = seconds;
591 }
592 return &cache;
593}

597inline uint64_t os_thread_id() noexcept {
598#if defined(_WIN32)
599 return ::GetCurrentThreadId();
600#elif defined(__linux__)
601 return static_cast<uint64_t>(::syscall(SYS_gettid));
602#elif defined(__APPLE__)
603 uint64_t tid = 0;
604 ::pthread_threadid_np(nullptr, &tid);
605 return tid;
606#else
607 // No portable OS thread id: a hash is still stable and unique among live
608 // threads, it just will not match what a debugger shows.
609 return std::hash<std::thread::id>{}(std::this_thread::get_id());
610#endif
611}

643#if defined(_WIN32)
644inline void* open_process(uint32_t pid, bool& denied) noexcept {
645 void* const process = ::OpenProcess(0x1000 /* PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION */ | 0x00100000 /* SYNCHRONIZE */,
646 0, pid);
647 denied = !process && ::GetLastError() == 5; // ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED: it exists
648 return process;
649}
650
651inline uint64_t process_creation_time(void* process) noexcept {
652 uint64_t times[4] = {}; // FILETIMEs: creation, exit, kernel, user
653 return ::GetProcessTimes(process, reinterpret_cast<_FILETIME*>(&times[0]), reinterpret_cast<_FILETIME*>(&times[1]),
654 reinterpret_cast<_FILETIME*>(&times[2]), reinterpret_cast<_FILETIME*>(&times[3]))
655 ? times[0]
656 : 0;
657}
658#elif defined(__linux__)
660inline bool read_proc_stat(uint32_t pid, char& state, uint64_t& start_time) noexcept {
661 char path[32];
662 std::snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "/proc/%u/stat", pid);
663 std::FILE* const file = std::fopen(path, "r");
664 if (!file) {
665 return false;
666 }
667 char text[1024];
668 const size_t size = std::fread(text, 1, sizeof(text) - 1, file);
669 std::fclose(file);
670 text[size] = '\0';
671 // The command (field 2) may hold spaces and parentheses: count from the last ')'.
672 const char* at = std::strrchr(text, ')');
673 if (!at) {
674 return false;
675 }
676 ++at;
677 for (int field = 3; field <= 22; ++field) {
678 while (*at == ' ') {
679 ++at;
680 }
681 if (field == 3) {
682 state = *at;
683 } else if (field == 22) {
684 start_time = std::strtoull(at, nullptr, 10); // clock ticks since boot
685 return true;
686 }
687 while (*at && *at != ' ') {
688 ++at;
689 }
690 }
691 return false;
692}
693#endif

700inline uint64_t process_start_time(uint32_t pid) noexcept {
701#if defined(_WIN32)
702 bool denied;
703 void* const process = open_process(pid, denied);
704 if (!process) {
705 return 0;
706 }
707 const uint64_t start = process_creation_time(process);
708 ::CloseHandle(process);
709 return start;
710#elif defined(__linux__)
711 char state = 0;
712 uint64_t start = 0;
713 return read_proc_stat(pid, state, start) ? start : 0;
714#elif defined(__APPLE__)
715 proc_bsdinfo info{};
716 if (::proc_pidinfo(static_cast<int>(pid), PROC_PIDTBSDINFO, 0, &info, sizeof(info)) != sizeof(info)) {
717 return 0;
718 }
719 return uint64_t{info.pbi_start_tvsec} * 1000000 + info.pbi_start_tvusec;
720#else
721 (void)pid;
722 return 0;
723#endif
724}

728inline bool process_running(uint32_t pid, uint64_t start_time) noexcept {
729 if (pid == 0) {
730 return false;
731 }
732#if defined(_WIN32)
733 bool denied;
734 void* const process = open_process(pid, denied);
735 if (!process) {
736 return denied;
737 }
738 bool running = ::WaitForSingleObject(process, 0) == 0x102; // WAIT_TIMEOUT: not signaled, so not exited
739 if (running && start_time != 0) {
740 const uint64_t start = process_creation_time(process);
741 running = start == 0 || start == start_time;
742 }
743 ::CloseHandle(process);
744 return running;
745#else
746 if (::kill(static_cast<pid_t>(pid), 0) != 0 && errno != EPERM) {
747 return false;
748 }
749# if defined(__linux__)
750 char state = 0;
751 uint64_t start = 0;
752 if (read_proc_stat(pid, state, start)) {
753 if (state == 'Z' || state == 'X') {
754 return false; // exited, not yet reaped
755 }
756 return start_time == 0 || start == start_time;
757 }
758 return true;
759# else
760 const uint64_t start = start_time ? process_start_time(pid) : 0;
761 return start == 0 || start == start_time;
762# endif
763#endif
764}

778 cache.seconds = 0;

804// P0718's std::atomic<std::shared_ptr<T>>. Availability has to be tested before
805// the type is ever named: libc++ ships no specialization, and naming it there
806// instantiates the primary std::atomic template, which hard-errors on its
807// is_trivially_copyable mandate rather than degrading into something usable.
808#ifndef SLICK_LOGGER_HAS_ATOMIC_SHARED_PTR
809# if defined(__cpp_lib_atomic_shared_ptr) && __cpp_lib_atomic_shared_ptr >= 201711L
810# define SLICK_LOGGER_HAS_ATOMIC_SHARED_PTR 1
811# else
812# define SLICK_LOGGER_HAS_ATOMIC_SHARED_PTR 0
813# endif
814#endif
815
816// The shared_ptr atomic free functions are deprecated in C++20. Silenced at the
817// one place they are named rather than in the build of every project that
818// includes this header. The pragma wraps the template definition, which is where
819// the diagnostic is anchored even though it fires on instantiation.
820#if !SLICK_LOGGER_HAS_ATOMIC_SHARED_PTR
821# if defined(__clang__) || defined(__GNUC__)
822# pragma GCC diagnostic push
823# pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Wdeprecated-declarations"
824# elif defined(_MSC_VER)
825# pragma warning(push)
826# pragma warning(disable : 4996)
827# endif
828#endif
829
846template <typename T>
847class atomic_shared_ptr {
848public:
849 atomic_shared_ptr() noexcept = default;
850 atomic_shared_ptr(const atomic_shared_ptr&) = delete;
851 atomic_shared_ptr& operator=(const atomic_shared_ptr&) = delete;
852
853 std::shared_ptr<T> load(std::memory_order order) const noexcept {
854#if SLICK_LOGGER_HAS_ATOMIC_SHARED_PTR
855 return value_.load(order);
856#else
857 return std::atomic_load_explicit(&value_, order);
858#endif
859 }
860
861 void store(std::shared_ptr<T> desired, std::memory_order order) noexcept {
862#if SLICK_LOGGER_HAS_ATOMIC_SHARED_PTR
863 value_.store(std::move(desired), order);
864#else
865 std::atomic_store_explicit(&value_, std::move(desired), order);
866#endif
867 }
868
869private:
870#if SLICK_LOGGER_HAS_ATOMIC_SHARED_PTR
871 std::atomic<std::shared_ptr<T>> value_;
872#else
873 std::shared_ptr<T> value_;
874#endif
875};
876
877#if !SLICK_LOGGER_HAS_ATOMIC_SHARED_PTR
878# if defined(__clang__) || defined(__GNUC__)
879# pragma GCC diagnostic pop
880# elif defined(_MSC_VER)
881# pragma warning(pop)
882# endif
883#endif

948class TimestampFormatter {
949public:
950 enum class Format {
951 DEFAULT, // 2024-08-26 15:30:45
952 WITH_MICROSECONDS, // 2024-08-26 15:30:45.123456
953 WITH_MILLISECONDS, // 2024-08-26 15:30:45.123
954 ISO8601, // 2024-08-26T15:30:45.123456Z
955 TIME_ONLY, // 15:30:45.123456
956 CUSTOM // User-defined format
957 };
958
959 TimestampFormatter(Format fmt = Format::WITH_MICROSECONDS) : format_(fmt) {}
960
961 TimestampFormatter(const std::string& custom_format)
962 : format_(Format::CUSTOM), custom_format_(custom_format),
963 custom_segments_(split_custom_format(custom_format)) {}
964
972 void append_timestamp(std::string& out, uint64_t timestamp_ns) const {
973 if (is_unbounded()) {
974 append_unbounded(out, timestamp_ns);
975 return;
976 }
977 char buf[kMaxBoundedLength];
978 out.append(buf, write_bounded(buf, timestamp_ns));
979 }
980
987 void write(detail::line_writer& out, uint64_t timestamp_ns) const {
988 if (is_unbounded()) {
989 out.append_unbounded([&](std::string& s) { append_unbounded(s, timestamp_ns); });
990 return;
991 }
992 out.advance(write_bounded(out.cursor(), timestamp_ns));
993 }
994
996 size_t write_bound() const noexcept { return is_unbounded() ? 0 : kMaxBoundedLength; }
997
999 std::string format_timestamp(uint64_t timestamp_ns) const {
1000 std::string out;
1001 append_timestamp(out, timestamp_ns);
1002 return out;
1003 }
1004
1012 size_t max_length() const noexcept {
1013 return format_ == Format::CUSTOM ? custom_format_.size() + 32 : kMaxBoundedLength;
1014 }
1015
1016private:
1018 static constexpr size_t kMaxBoundedLength = 27;
1019 static constexpr std::string_view kFallback = "1970-01-01 00:00:00.000000";
1020
1022 bool is_unbounded() const noexcept { return !custom_segments_.empty(); }
1023
1029 size_t write_bounded(char* out, uint64_t timestamp_ns) const noexcept {
1030 using namespace detail;
1031
1032 // Whole seconds select the cached "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" prefix; only the
1033 // sub-second digits have to be written per call.
1034 const int64_t seconds = static_cast<int64_t>(timestamp_ns / 1000000000ULL);
1035 const uint32_t us = static_cast<uint32_t>((timestamp_ns / 1000ULL) % 1000000ULL);
1036
1037 const second_cache* cache = cached_second(seconds);
1038 if (!cache) [[unlikely]] {
1039 std::memcpy(out, kFallback.data(), kFallback.size());
1040 return kFallback.size();
1041 }
1042
1043 switch (format_) {
1044 case Format::WITH_MICROSECONDS:
1045 std::memcpy(out, cache->date_time, kDateTimeLen);
1046 out[19] = '.';
1047 write_6_digits(out + 20, us);
1048 return 26;
1049
1050 case Format::WITH_MILLISECONDS:
1051 std::memcpy(out, cache->date_time, kDateTimeLen);
1052 out[19] = '.';
1053 write_2_digits(out + 20, us / 10000);
1054 out[22] = static_cast<char>('0' + (us / 1000) % 10);
1055 return 23;
1056
1057 case Format::ISO8601:
1058 std::memcpy(out, cache->date_time, kDateTimeLen);
1059 out[10] = 'T';
1060 out[19] = '.';
1061 write_6_digits(out + 20, us);
1062 out[26] = 'Z';
1063 return 27;
1064
1065 case Format::TIME_ONLY:
1066 std::memcpy(out, cache->date_time + kTimeOffset, kTimeLen);
1067 out[8] = '.';
1068 write_6_digits(out + 9, us);
1069 return 15;
1070
1071 case Format::DEFAULT:
1072 case Format::CUSTOM: // only an empty one gets here
1073 break;
1074 }
1075 std::memcpy(out, cache->date_time, kDateTimeLen);
1076 return kDateTimeLen;
1077 }
1078
1079 void append_unbounded(std::string& out, uint64_t timestamp_ns) const {
1080 const detail::second_cache* cache =
1081 detail::cached_second(static_cast<int64_t>(timestamp_ns / 1000000000ULL));
1082 if (!cache) [[unlikely]] {
1083 out += kFallback;
1084 return;
1085 }
1086 append_custom(out, cache->tm, static_cast<uint32_t>((timestamp_ns / 1000ULL) % 1000000ULL));
1087 }
1088
1097 void append_custom(std::string& out, const std::tm& tm, uint32_t us) const {
1098 bool first = true;
1099 for (const std::string& segment : custom_segments_) {
1100 if (!first) {
1101 detail::append_uint(out, us);
1102 }
1103 first = false;
1104 append_strftime(out, segment, tm);
1105 }
1106 }
1107
1117 static void append_strftime(std::string& out, const std::string& format, const std::tm& tm) {
1118 if (format.empty()) {
1119 return;
1120 }
1121 // Wide enough that no realistic timestamp format reaches the growing path.
1122 char buf[256];
1123 if (const size_t written = std::strftime(buf, sizeof(buf), format.c_str(), &tm)) {
1124 out.append(buf, written);
1125 return;
1126 }
1127 grow_strftime(out, format, tm);
1128 }
1129
1145 static void grow_strftime(std::string& out, const std::string& format, const std::tm& tm) {
1146 // 1 MiB of expanded timestamp is a mistake in the format, not a timestamp.
1147 constexpr size_t kMaxExpansion = size_t{1} << 20;
1148 std::string probe;
1149 probe.reserve(format.size() + 1);
1150 probe += '\x01';
1151 probe += format;
1152
1153 std::vector<char> spacious;
1154 for (size_t capacity = 512; capacity <= kMaxExpansion; capacity *= 2) {
1155 spacious.assign(capacity, '\0');
1156 const size_t written = std::strftime(spacious.data(), capacity, probe.c_str(), &tm);
1157 if (written) {
1158 // written counts the sentinel, which is not part of the timestamp.
1159 out.append(spacious.data() + 1, written - 1);
1160 return;
1161 }
1162 }
1163 }
1164
1173 static std::vector<std::string> split_custom_format(const std::string& format) {
1174 std::vector<std::string> segments;
1175 if (format.empty()) {
1176 return segments;
1177 }
1178 size_t start = 0;
1179 for (size_t i = 0; i + 1 < format.size(); ) {
1180 if (format[i] != '%') {
1181 ++i;
1182 } else if (format[i + 1] == 'f') {
1183 segments.push_back(format.substr(start, i - start));
1184 i += 2;
1185 start = i;
1186 } else {
1187 i += 2; // "%%", or a conversion strftime handles itself
1188 }
1189 }
1190 segments.push_back(format.substr(start));
1191 return segments;
1192 }
1193
1194 Format format_;
1195 std::string custom_format_;
1196 // custom_format_ split at every %f, once, when it was set. Rendering walks the
1197 // segments and writes the microseconds between them, so a CUSTOM line does
1198 // not allocate. An ostringstream would allocate twice per line, once for a
1199 // copy of the format string and once for the result.
1200 std::vector<std::string> custom_segments_;
1201};

1305// Whether `_Float128` is usable as a type name in C++.
1306//
1307// It is a distinct type from `__float128` on GCC, and libstdc++ can hand it to a
1308// format-arg visitor, so it cannot simply be dropped. It needs its own feature
1309// test though: `__SIZEOF_FLOAT128__` says the target has a 128-bit float, not
1310// that this spelling exists. Clang defines that macro on x86-64 yet has no
1311// `_Float128` in C++ mode, and GCC only accepts it in C++ from version 13.
1312#ifndef SLICK_LOGGER_HAS_FLOAT128_T
1313# if defined(__STDCPP_FLOAT128_T__) || \
1314 (defined(__GNUC__) && !defined(__clang__) && !defined(__INTEL_COMPILER) && __GNUC__ >= 13)
1315# define SLICK_LOGGER_HAS_FLOAT128_T 1
1316# else
1317# define SLICK_LOGGER_HAS_FLOAT128_T 0
1318# endif
1319#endif
1320
1321// True for the target's 128-bit binary floating point types, and false (rather
1322// than ill-formed) wherever they do not exist. Keeping the preprocessor here
1323// instead of inside the if-constexpr chain matters: an ill-formed condition
1324// there stops the chain from discarding later branches, which is what made the
1325// `_Float128` spelling break every translation unit under clang.
1326template<typename T>
1327inline constexpr bool is_float128_v =
1328#if defined(__SIZEOF_FLOAT128__)
1329 std::is_same_v<T, __float128>
1330# if SLICK_LOGGER_HAS_FLOAT128_T
1331 || std::is_same_v<T, _Float128>
1332# endif
1333 ;
1334#else
1335 false;
1336#endif
1337
1338// True when Args... is exactly one type convertible to std::format_args, which
1339// is how log_to_sink detects the pre-built format_args overload.
1340// std::make_format_args() returns an implementation-defined store type
1341// (e.g. std::_Format_arg_store on MSVC) that converts to std::format_args,
1342// so we check convertibility rather than exact type identity.
1343template<typename... Args>
1344inline constexpr bool is_single_format_args_v =
1345 sizeof...(Args) == 1 &&
1346 (std::is_convertible_v<std::decay_t<Args>, std::format_args> || ...);
1347
1358enum class QueueMode : uint8_t {
1359 Local,
1360 SharedProducer,
1361 SharedCollector
1362};
1363
1367// String references in this entry are ring-buffer indices, not addresses.
1368// Set by producers whose queues live in shared memory, because the segment maps
1369// at a different base address in every process.
1370inline constexpr uint8_t kEntryOffsets = 0x01;
1371// The entry carries a valid source file/line. Needed as an explicit flag because
1372// ring index 0 is a legitimate string reference and cannot double as a null sentinel.
1373inline constexpr uint8_t kEntryHasSourceLocation = 0x02;
1374// The format is a string literal referenced in place: fixed text at a fixed
1375// address, so a parse of it holds for every entry that carries it. Never set
1376// alongside kEntryOffsets, because a format copied into a ring has no fixed
1377// address.
1378inline constexpr uint8_t kEntryStaticFormat = 0x04;
1379// Spilled from a full thread ring into the shared queue. Sinks never see this
1380// flag. The entry carries a route to the ring it waits for until the writer
1381// thread takes the route out. Local mode keeps the route in pid, which it sets
1382// to 0 anyway. In shared memory pid stays the producer's, so a replay still
1383// names the producer after its registry slot is freed or reused. There the
1384// route goes in the high halves of format.length and file.length, which a
1385// string in the shared string ring never uses (see kMaxPayloadBytes).
1386inline constexpr uint8_t kEntrySpilled = 0x08;
1387
1388#pragma pack(push, 1)
1397struct StringRef {
1398 union {
1399 const char* ptr; // Pointer to string data (entry without kEntryOffsets)
1400 uint64_t offset; // String ring reserve index (entry with kEntryOffsets)
1401 };
1402 uint32_t length; // String length; 0 means "NUL-terminated, length unknown"
1403
1404 // Deliberately left as an aggregate with no user-provided constructors:
1405 // LogArgument stores a StringRef inside a union, and any non-trivial default
1406 // constructor here would delete that union's (and therefore LogEntry's)
1407 // default constructor. Build one with braces, e.g. StringRef{"text"}.
1408};
1409
1410struct LogArgument {
1411 ArgType type;
1412 union {
1413 bool b;
1414 char c;
1415 unsigned char uc;
1416 wchar_t wc;
1417 int8_t i8;
1418 int16_t i16;
1419 int32_t i32;
1420 int64_t i64;
1421 uint8_t u8;
1422 uint16_t u16;
1423 uint32_t u32;
1424 uint64_t u64;
1425 float f;
1426 double d;
1427 void* ptr; // For pointer types
1428 const char* literal_ptr; // For string literals
1429 StringRef dynamic_str; // For dynamic strings
1430 } value;
1431};
1432
1433struct LogEntry {
1434 StringRef format; // Format string
1435 uint64_t timestamp; // nanoseconds since epoch
1436 StringRef file{}; // Source file name captured by LOG_* macros
1437 uint32_t pid = 0; // Producing process id; 0 in single-process (Local) mode
1438 // Always present, even where SLICK_LOGGER_ENABLE_THREAD_ID is off and it stays
1439 // 0: the layout is the shared-memory contract, so the option must not move it.
1440 uint32_t thread_id = 0; // Producing thread id; see detail::current_thread_id()
1441 uint32_t line = 0; // Source line captured by LOG_* macros
1442 int sink_index = -1; // Optional sink index, logged by that sink only
1443 LogLevel level;
1444 uint8_t flags = 0; // kEntryOffsets / kEntryHasSourceLocation / kEntryStaticFormat / kEntrySpilled
1445 uint8_t arg_count = 0; // Number of arguments
1446 char tag[SLICK_LOGGER_TAG_SIZE] = {}; // NUL-padded producer tag; empty in Local mode
1447 LogArgument args[SLICK_LOGGER_MAX_ARGS];
1448
1449 // Sinks always receive entries whose string references have been resolved to
1450 // addresses, so these accessors are safe from any sink implementation.
1451 const char* format_ptr() const noexcept { return format.ptr; }
1452 const char* file_name() const noexcept { return file.ptr; }
1453};
1454#pragma pack(pop)
1455
1456inline constexpr bool has_source_location(const LogEntry& entry) noexcept {
1457 return (entry.flags & kEntryHasSourceLocation) != 0;
1458}

1473inline size_t tag_length(const char* tag) noexcept {
1474 constexpr size_t kSize = SLICK_LOGGER_TAG_SIZE;
1475 size_t offset = 0;
1476 if constexpr (std::endian::native == std::endian::little) {
1477 for (; offset + 8 <= kSize; offset += 8) {
1478 uint64_t word;
1479 std::memcpy(&word, tag + offset, 8);
1480 const uint64_t zero_bytes = (word - 0x0101010101010101ull) & ~word & 0x8080808080808080ull;
1481 if (zero_bytes != 0) {
1482 return offset + static_cast<size_t>(std::countr_zero(zero_bytes)) / 8;
1483 }
1484 }
1485 }
1486 while (offset < kSize && tag[offset] != '\0') {
1487 ++offset;
1488 }
1489 return offset;
1490}

1639private:
1640 enum class Flag : uint8_t {
1641 // A run of date/time flags and their separators that turned out to be one
1642 // contiguous slice of the cached "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" text, fused by
1643 // compile() into a single memcpy. literal_off/literal_len index that text
1644 // rather than literals_. May carry a fraction; see Op::frac_digits.
1645 kCachedSlice,
1646 kLiteral, kMessage, kLevel, kLevelShort, kThreadId, kProcessId, kTag, kSinkName,
1647 kSourceFile, kSourceLine, kSourceLoc,
1648 kYear4, kYear2, kMonth, kDay, kHour24, kHour12, kAmPm, kMinute, kSecond,
1649 kMillis, kMicros, kNanos, kTimeHMS, kDateMDY, kDateTimeFull, kEpochSeconds,
1650 kWeekdayShort, kWeekdayLong, kMonthShort, kMonthLong,
1651 kColorBegin, kColorEnd, kDefaultHeader, kConfiguredTimestamp
1652 };
1653
1654 struct Op {
1655 Flag flag = Flag::kLiteral;
1656 bool left_align = false;
1657 uint8_t width = 0; // 0 means "natural width"
1658 // For a kCachedSlice: a one-character separator and 3, 6 or 9 sub-second
1659 // digits written after the slice, fused from "%S.%e"/"%S.%f"/"%S.%F".
1660 // frac_digits is 0 when there is no fraction.
1661 char frac_sep = 0;
1662 uint8_t frac_digits = 0;
1663 uint32_t literal_off = 0; // offset into literals_, for kLiteral
1664 uint32_t literal_len = 0;
1665 // The literal run in front of this op, in literals_, written before it
1666 // (and outside its width) so that it costs no dispatch of its own.
1667 uint32_t prefix_off = 0;
1668 uint32_t prefix_len = 0;
1669 };
1670
1671 void compile(std::string_view pattern);
1673 static Flag flag_for(char c, std::string_view pattern);
1674
1683 static bool flag_needs_cache(Flag flag) noexcept;
1684
1695 void fuse_cached_slices();
1703 void fuse_literal_prefixes();
1705 static bool cached_slice_for(Flag flag, size_t& offset, size_t& length) noexcept;
1707 static constexpr char cached_separator_at(size_t index) noexcept {
1708 switch (index) {
1709 case 4: case 7: return '-';
1710 case 10: return ' ';
1711 case 13: case 16: return ':';
1712 default: return '\0';
1713 }
1714 }
1716 static bool literal_matches_cached(std::string_view literal, size_t offset) noexcept;
1717
1725 static size_t fixed_length(const Op& op) noexcept;
1727 static constexpr uint32_t subsecond_digits(Flag flag) noexcept {
1728 return flag == Flag::kMillis ? 3 : flag == Flag::kMicros ? 6 : flag == Flag::kNanos ? 9 : 0;
1729 }
1731 size_t line_bound(const LogEntry& entry, const Context& ctx) const noexcept;
1733 void write_op(detail::line_writer& out, const Op& op, const LogEntry& entry,
1734 const Context& ctx, const detail::second_cache* cache,
1735 uint32_t subsecond_ns) const;
1736
1737 std::vector<Op> ops_;
1738 std::string literals_; // every literal run, concatenated once at compile time
1739 std::string pattern_; // kept verbatim for pattern() and diagnostics
1740 // What line_bound() starts from: the fixed_length() of every op plus every
1741 // width, which is the most padding a field can take.
1742 size_t fixed_bound_ = 0;
1743 // How many ops render each string the line supplies, so line_bound() is a
1744 // handful of multiply-adds rather than a walk of the ops.
1745 uint32_t message_count_ = 0; // %v
1746 uint32_t level_name_count_ = 0; // %l
1747 uint32_t sink_name_count_ = 0; // %n
1748 uint32_t source_file_count_ = 0; // %s %@
1749 uint32_t color_begin_count_ = 0; // %^
1750 uint32_t color_end_count_ = 0; // %$
1751 uint32_t timestamp_count_ = 0; // %q
1752 uint32_t default_layout_count_ = 0; // %+
1753 bool has_color_range_ = false;
1754 // Kept apart because they cost different things. A calendar field needs the
1755 // per-second localtime() behind cached_second(); %e/%f/%F need one division
1756 // of the entry's own timestamp. A pattern carrying only sub-second digits
1757 // pays for neither the lookup nor the cache line it would touch.
1758 bool needs_cache_ = false; // %Y %y %m %d %H %I %p %M %S %T %D %c %a %A %b %B
1759 bool needs_subsecond_ = false; // %e %f %F
1760 bool needs_message_ = false; // skips the std::format pass entirely when false
1761 // A %^ with no %$ after it. The escape would otherwise stay active past the
1762 // end of the line and tint everything the terminal prints next.
1763 bool color_left_open_ = false;
1764};

1782class pattern_store {
1783public:
1790 const PatternFormatter* get(std::string_view pattern) {
1791 if (pattern.empty()) {
1792 return nullptr;
1793 }
1794 for (const PatternFormatter& owned : owned_) {
1795 if (owned.pattern() == pattern) {
1796 return &owned;
1797 }
1798 }
1799 owned_.emplace_back(pattern);
1800 return &owned_.back();
1801 }
1802
1804 size_t size() const noexcept { return owned_.size(); }
1805
1806private:
1807 std::deque<PatternFormatter> owned_;
1808};

1993 int index_ = -1; // Index assigned by Logger when added
1994 // Atomic because the LOG_SINK_* macros read it from producer threads while
1995 // set_min_level() may run concurrently on another. LogLevel is uint8_t-backed,
1996 // so this stays lock-free.
1997 std::atomic<LogLevel> min_level_{LogLevel::L_TRACE}; // Minimum level for this sink
1998 bool dedicated_ = false; // Whether this sink is dedicated (logs only its own entries)
1999 // Left deliberately default-constructed: TimestampFormatter's own default is
2000 // Format::WITH_MICROSECONDS, which is the documented default timestamp for
2001 // every sink. Do not "tidy" this into an explicit initializer.
2002 TimestampFormatter timestamp_formatter_;
2003 // Writer thread only; reused across entries so a steady-state line allocates
2004 // nothing at all.
2005 std::string format_buffer_;
2006 // Where formatted_message() formats when no dispatch is sharing one. Writer
2007 // thread only, reused like format_buffer_.
2008 std::string message_buffer_;
2009 // This sink's own patterns, from set_pattern(). Grow-only, so a pointer the
2010 // writer thread already loaded stays valid even as set_pattern() publishes a
2011 // replacement.
2012 detail::pattern_store owned_patterns_;
2013 // The logger's store, holding whatever inherited_pattern_ points at. Held by
2014 // shared_ptr rather than trusted to outlive the sink: a caller can keep its
2015 // own shared_ptr to a sink past Logger::reset(), or past the destruction of a
2016 // Logger it installed with set_instance().
2017 std::shared_ptr<detail::pattern_store> inherited_store_;
2018 // The two layouts that compete, kept apart so the override is reversible:
2019 // this sink's own wins while it is set, and clearing it falls back to
2020 // whatever the logger-wide default is by then. Null means "not set".
2021 const PatternFormatter* explicit_pattern_ = nullptr;
2022 const PatternFormatter* inherited_pattern_ = nullptr;
2023 // The winner of those two, which is all the writer thread reads.
2024 std::atomic<const PatternFormatter*> active_pattern_{nullptr};
2025};

2067inline void open_buffered_stream(std::ofstream& stream, std::vector<char>& buffer,
2068 const std::filesystem::path& path,
2069 std::ios::openmode mode, size_t buffer_size) {
2070 const auto parent = path.parent_path();
2071 if (!parent.empty()) {
2072 std::error_code ec;
2073 std::filesystem::create_directories(parent, ec); // no-op when it already exists
2074 }
2075 if (buffer.empty()) {
2076 buffer.resize(buffer_size);
2077 }
2078 stream.rdbuf()->pubsetbuf(buffer.data(), static_cast<std::streamsize>(buffer.size()));
2079 stream.open(path, mode);
2080}

2304// EncodedFileSink's file: records, each a kind byte then its fields, unaligned,
2305// in the writer's byte order (the reader checks the header's 0x01020304).
2306// 'H' "SLICKLOG" u16 version, u16 0, u32 0x01020304 - starts every session
2307// 'T' u32 id, u32 size, bytes - a format string or file name; ids count from 1
2308// 'E' u8 level, u8 bits, u8 arg_count, u64 timestamp, u32 thread_id, u32 format,
2309// [u32 file, u32 line], [u32 pid, u8 tag size, tag], then per argument
2310// u8 ArgType and its value: 1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes (a wchar_t as 4, a pointer
2311// as 8), or u32 size and bytes for a string or BLOB.
2312// A text id of 0 means the text follows inline, as u32 size and bytes.
2313inline constexpr char kEncodedMagic[8] = {'S', 'L', 'I', 'C', 'K', 'L', 'O', 'G'};
2314inline constexpr uint16_t kEncodedVersion = 1;
2315inline constexpr uint32_t kEncodedByteOrder = 0x01020304;
2316inline constexpr char kEncodedHeader = 'H';
2317inline constexpr char kEncodedText = 'T';
2318inline constexpr char kEncodedEntry = 'E';
2319inline constexpr uint8_t kEncodedLocated = 0x01; // file and line follow
2320inline constexpr uint8_t kEncodedProcess = 0x02; // pid and tag follow
2321inline constexpr size_t kEncodedHeaderSize = 1 + sizeof(kEncodedMagic) + 2 + 2 + 4;
2322
2327inline constexpr uint8_t kEncodedArgBytes[] = {1, 1, 1, 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 1, 2, 4, 8, 4, 8,
2328 sizeof(void*) == 8 ? 8 : 0, 0, 0, 0};
2329static_assert(sizeof(kEncodedArgBytes) == static_cast<size_t>(ArgType::BLOB) + 1, "a new ArgType needs its size here");
2330
2331inline uint8_t encoded_arg_bytes(ArgType type) noexcept {
2332 const auto index = static_cast<size_t>(type);
2333 return index < sizeof(kEncodedArgBytes) ? kEncodedArgBytes[index] : 0;
2334}
2335
2346class text_table {
2347public:
2348 static constexpr size_t kDefaultLimit = size_t{16} << 20;
2349
2350 text_table() : hints_(std::make_unique<hint[]>(kHints)) {}
2351
2354 SLICK_LOGGER_FORCE_INLINE uint32_t intern(std::string_view text, bool& added) {
2355 hint& h = hints_[hint_index(text.data())];
2356 if (h.ptr == text.data() && h.size == text.size() && same(h.copy, text)) [[likely]] {
2357 added = false;
2358 return h.id;
2359 }
2360 return intern_slow(text.data(), text.size(), h, added);
2361 }
2362
2364 void set_limit(size_t bytes) noexcept { limit_ = bytes; }
2365
2367 void clear() noexcept {
2368 std::fill_n(hints_.get(), kHints, hint{});
2369 slots_.clear();
2370 blocks_.clear();
2371 block_at_ = nullptr;
2372 block_left_ = 0;
2373 count_ = 0;
2374 used_ = 0;
2375 next_id_ = 1;
2376 }
2377
2378private:
2379 struct hint {
2380 const char* ptr = nullptr; // where the text was last seen
2381 const char* copy = nullptr; // its bytes, kept here
2382 uint32_t size = 0;
2383 uint32_t id = 0;
2384 };
2385 struct slot {
2386 uint64_t hash = 0;
2387 const char* copy = nullptr;
2388 uint32_t size = 0;
2389 uint32_t id = 0; // 0: empty
2390 };
2391 static constexpr size_t kHints = 1024; // power of two
2392 static constexpr size_t kOverheadPerText = 64; // a slot, a hint, the table's slack
2393 static constexpr size_t kBlockSize = 64 * 1024;
2394
2395 static size_t hint_index(const char* ptr) noexcept {
2396 // Fibonacci hashing, as message_formats: literals sit at small aligned strides.
2397 return static_cast<size_t>((static_cast<uint64_t>(reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(ptr)) *
2398 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ull) >> 54);
2399 }
2400 static uint64_t hash(std::string_view text) noexcept;
2401 static uint64_t load8(const char* p) noexcept {
2402 uint64_t word;
2403 std::memcpy(&word, p, 8);
2404 return word;
2405 }
2406 static uint32_t load4(const char* p) noexcept {
2407 uint32_t word;
2408 std::memcpy(&word, p, 4);
2409 return word;
2410 }
2414 static SLICK_LOGGER_FORCE_INLINE bool same(const char* copy, std::string_view text) noexcept {
2415 const char* const b = text.data();
2416 const size_t n = text.size();
2417 if (n >= 8) {
2418 uint64_t diff = load8(copy + n - 8) ^ load8(b + n - 8);
2419 for (size_t i = 0; i + 8 < n; i += 8) {
2420 diff |= load8(copy + i) ^ load8(b + i);
2421 }
2422 return diff == 0;
2423 }
2424 if (n >= 4) {
2425 return ((load4(copy) ^ load4(b)) | (load4(copy + n - 4) ^ load4(b + n - 4))) == 0;
2426 }
2427 for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
2428 if (copy[i] != b[i]) {
2429 return false;
2430 }
2431 }
2432 return true;
2433 }
2436 uint32_t intern_slow(const char* data, size_t size, hint& h, bool& added);
2437 void insert(const slot& s) noexcept;
2439 const char* store(std::string_view text);
2440
2441 std::unique_ptr<hint[]> hints_;
2442 std::vector<slot> slots_; // open addressing, at most half full
2443 std::vector<std::unique_ptr<char[]>> blocks_; // every text, so a hit is checked against its bytes
2444 char* block_at_ = nullptr;
2445 size_t block_left_ = 0;
2446 size_t count_ = 0;
2447 size_t used_ = 0; // text bytes plus kOverheadPerText per text
2448 size_t limit_ = kDefaultLimit;
2449 uint32_t next_id_ = 1;
2450};
2451
2452} // namespace detail

2472class EncodedFileSink : public FileSinkBase {
2473public:
2474 explicit EncodedFileSink(const std::filesystem::path& file_path, std::string&& name = "");
2476 ~EncodedFileSink() override;
2477
2478 void write(const LogEntry& entry) override;
2479 void flush() override;
2480
2484 void set_text_table_limit(size_t bytes) noexcept { texts_.set_limit(bytes); }
2485
2486protected:
2488 size_t file_size() const noexcept { return file_bytes_ + used_; }
2489
2497 template<typename Retire>
2498 void restart_file(Retire&& retire) {
2499 drain();
2500 close_stream();
2501 retire();
2502 open_stream(file_path_, std::ios::binary | std::ios::out | std::ios::trunc);
2503 file_bytes_ = 0;
2504 texts_.clear();
2505 write_header();
2506 }
2507
2508private:
2509 void write_header();
2511 SLICK_LOGGER_FORCE_INLINE uint32_t text_id(std::string_view text) {
2512 bool added = false;
2513 const uint32_t id = texts_.intern(text, added);
2514 if (added) [[unlikely]] {
2515 write_text(id, text.data(), text.size());
2516 }
2517 return id;
2518 }
2521 void write_text(uint32_t id, const char* data, size_t size);
2523 SLICK_LOGGER_FORCE_INLINE char* reserve(size_t size) {
2524 if (used_ + size > buffer_.size()) [[unlikely]] {
2525 grow(size);
2526 }
2527 return buffer_.data() + used_;
2528 }
2529 void grow(size_t size);
2531 void drain();
2532
2533 detail::text_table texts_;
2534 // Records are written through a pointer into this buffer, which goes to the
2535 // file once it holds write_cache_size() bytes. Growing a std::string per
2536 // record, as text sinks do, cost a third of the time an entry takes here.
2537 std::vector<char> buffer_;
2538 size_t used_ = 0;
2539 size_t file_bytes_ = 0; // bytes already written to the current file
2540};

2809inline uint64_t read_cycle_counter() noexcept {
2810#if defined(_MSC_VER) && defined(_M_X64)
2811 return __rdtsc();
2812#elif defined(_MSC_VER) && defined(_M_ARM64)
2813 return static_cast<uint64_t>(_ReadStatusReg(0x5F02)); // CNTVCT_EL0, as winnt.h encodes it
2814#elif defined(__x86_64__)
2815 return __rdtsc();
2816#elif defined(__aarch64__)
2817 uint64_t ticks;
2818 __asm__ volatile("mrs %0, cntvct_el0" : "=r"(ticks));
2819 return ticks;
2820#else
2821 return 0;
2822#endif
2823}
2824
2826inline void cpu_pause() noexcept {
2827#if defined(_MSC_VER) && defined(_M_X64)
2828 _mm_pause();
2829#elif defined(_MSC_VER) && defined(_M_ARM64)
2830 __yield();
2831#elif defined(__x86_64__) || defined(__i386__)
2832 __builtin_ia32_pause();
2833#elif defined(__aarch64__) || defined(__arm__)
2834 __asm__ __volatile__("yield" ::: "memory");
2835#else
2836 std::this_thread::yield();
2837#endif
2838}
2839
2843inline bool cycle_counter_is_steady() noexcept {
2844#if defined(_MSC_VER) && defined(_M_X64)
2845 int regs[4];
2846 __cpuid(regs, static_cast<int>(0x80000000u));
2847 if (static_cast<unsigned>(regs[0]) < 0x80000007u) {
2848 return false;
2849 }
2850 __cpuid(regs, static_cast<int>(0x80000007u));
2851 return (regs[3] >> 8) & 1;
2852#elif defined(__x86_64__)
2853 unsigned eax = 0, ebx = 0, ecx = 0, edx = 0;
2854 if (!__get_cpuid(0x80000000u, &eax, &ebx, &ecx, &edx) || eax < 0x80000007u) {
2855 return false;
2856 }
2857 __get_cpuid(0x80000007u, &eax, &ebx, &ecx, &edx);
2858 return (edx >> 8) & 1;
2859#elif defined(_M_ARM64) || defined(__aarch64__)
2860 return true;
2861#else
2862 return false;
2863#endif
2864}
2865
2868inline uint64_t mul_shift_32(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) noexcept {
2869#if defined(__SIZEOF_INT128__)
2870 return static_cast<uint64_t>((static_cast<unsigned __int128>(a) * b) >> 32);
2871#elif defined(_MSC_VER) && defined(_M_X64)
2872 uint64_t high;
2873 const uint64_t low = _umul128(a, b, &high);
2874 return (high << 32) | (low >> 32);
2875#elif defined(_MSC_VER) && defined(_M_ARM64)
2876 return (__umulh(a, b) << 32) | ((a * b) >> 32);
2877#else
2878 const uint64_t a_hi = a >> 32, a_lo = a & 0xFFFFFFFFu, b_hi = b >> 32, b_lo = b & 0xFFFFFFFFu;
2879 const uint64_t mid = a_lo * b_hi + ((a_lo * b_lo) >> 32); // cannot overflow
2880 return (a_hi * b_hi << 32) + a_hi * b_lo + mid;
2881#endif
2882}
2883
2884} // namespace detail

2921class TscTimestamper final : public ITimestamper {
2922public:
2923 explicit TscTimestamper(std::chrono::nanoseconds calibration = std::chrono::milliseconds(10),
2924 std::chrono::nanoseconds resync_interval = std::chrono::seconds(1));
2925
2926 uint64_t now() noexcept override;
2927
2930 bool uses_cycle_counter() const noexcept { return use_counter_; }
2931
2933 std::chrono::nanoseconds resync_interval() const noexcept {
2934 return std::chrono::nanoseconds(static_cast<int64_t>(resync_interval_ns_));
2935 }
2936
2937private:
2939 static constexpr std::chrono::nanoseconds kMinInterval = std::chrono::milliseconds(1);
2940
2942 struct Anchor {
2943 std::atomic<uint64_t> ticks{0};
2944 std::atomic<uint64_t> ns{0};
2945 std::atomic<uint64_t> ns_per_tick_q32{0};
2946 };
2947
2950 template<typename Clock>
2951 static void sample(uint64_t& ticks, uint64_t& clock_ns) noexcept;
2952
2953 static uint64_t project(uint64_t ticks, uint64_t anchor_ticks, uint64_t anchor_ns, uint64_t rate) noexcept;
2954
2957 bool resync() noexcept;
2958
2959 // Read by every now(): the published anchor pair and what selects between them.
2960 // A re-anchor writes the anchor not in use and then bumps generation_, so a
2961 // reader only ever retries, never waits.
2962 alignas(64) std::atomic<uint64_t> generation_{0};
2963 Anchor anchors_[2];
2964 uint64_t resync_ticks_ = 0;
2965 bool use_counter_ = false;
2966
2967 // Re-anchor state: touched only by the thread holding resyncing_.
2968 alignas(64) std::atomic<bool> resyncing_{false};
2969 uint64_t resync_interval_ns_ = 0;
2970 uint64_t base_ticks_ = 0;
2971 uint64_t base_steady_ns_ = 0;
2972 uint64_t rate_q32_ = 0;
2973};
2974
2975inline TscTimestamper::TscTimestamper(std::chrono::nanoseconds calibration,
2976 std::chrono::nanoseconds resync_interval)
2977 : resync_interval_ns_(static_cast<uint64_t>(std::max(resync_interval, kMinInterval).count())) {
2978 if (!detail::cycle_counter_is_steady()) {
2979 return;
2980 }
2981 sample<std::chrono::steady_clock>(base_ticks_, base_steady_ns_);
2982 std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::max(calibration, kMinInterval));
2983 uint64_t ticks = 0, steady_ns = 0;
2984 sample<std::chrono::steady_clock>(ticks, steady_ns);
2985 if (ticks <= base_ticks_ || steady_ns <= base_steady_ns_) {
2986 return; // a counter that did not advance is no clock
2987 }
2988 rate_q32_ = static_cast<uint64_t>(static_cast<double>(steady_ns - base_steady_ns_) * 4294967296.0 /
2989 static_cast<double>(ticks - base_ticks_));
2990 resync_ticks_ = static_cast<uint64_t>(static_cast<double>(resync_interval_ns_) * 4294967296.0 /
2991 static_cast<double>(std::max<uint64_t>(rate_q32_, 1)));
2992
2993 uint64_t wall_ns = 0;
2994 sample<std::chrono::system_clock>(ticks, wall_ns);
2995 anchors_[0].ticks.store(ticks, std::memory_order_relaxed);
2996 anchors_[0].ns.store(wall_ns, std::memory_order_relaxed);
2997 anchors_[0].ns_per_tick_q32.store(rate_q32_, std::memory_order_relaxed);
2998 use_counter_ = rate_q32_ != 0 && resync_ticks_ != 0;
2999}
3000
3001template<typename Clock>
3002inline void TscTimestamper::sample(uint64_t& ticks, uint64_t& clock_ns) noexcept {
3003 uint64_t best_width = UINT64_MAX;
3004 for (int attempt = 0; attempt < 3; ++attempt) {
3005 const uint64_t before = detail::read_cycle_counter();
3006 const uint64_t ns = detail::clock_timestamp<Clock>();
3007 const uint64_t width = detail::read_cycle_counter() - before;
3008 if (width < best_width) {
3009 best_width = width;
3010 ticks = before + width / 2;
3011 clock_ns = ns;
3012 }
3013 }
3014}
3015
3016inline uint64_t TscTimestamper::project(uint64_t ticks, uint64_t anchor_ticks, uint64_t anchor_ns,
3017 uint64_t rate) noexcept {
3018 // A thread that read the counter just before another re-anchored can land a
3019 // few ticks before the new anchor.
3020 return ticks >= anchor_ticks ? anchor_ns + detail::mul_shift_32(ticks - anchor_ticks, rate)
3021 : anchor_ns - detail::mul_shift_32(anchor_ticks - ticks, rate);
3022}
3023
3024inline uint64_t TscTimestamper::now() noexcept {
3025 if (!use_counter_) [[unlikely]] {
3026 return detail::clock_timestamp<std::chrono::system_clock>();
3027 }
3028 const uint64_t ticks = detail::read_cycle_counter();
3029 for (;;) {
3030 const uint64_t generation = generation_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
3031 const Anchor& anchor = anchors_[generation & 1];
3032 const uint64_t anchor_ticks = anchor.ticks.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
3033 const uint64_t anchor_ns = anchor.ns.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
3034 const uint64_t rate = anchor.ns_per_tick_q32.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
3035 // Pairs with the release fence in resync(): if any of the three loads saw
3036 // a later re-anchor's write, the generation has moved on and this retries.
3037 std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_acquire);
3038 if (generation_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) != generation) [[unlikely]] {
3039 continue;
3040 }
3041 if (ticks - anchor_ticks >= resync_ticks_ && ticks > anchor_ticks) [[unlikely]] {
3042 if (resync()) {
3043 continue; // stamp with the anchor just published
3044 }
3045 }
3046 return project(ticks, anchor_ticks, anchor_ns, rate);
3047 }
3048}
3049
3050inline bool TscTimestamper::resync() noexcept {
3051 if (resyncing_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) ||
3052 resyncing_.exchange(true, std::memory_order_acquire)) {
3053 return false;
3054 }
3055 // Every store below goes to the anchor no reader was handed by the current
3056 // generation. Ordered after that generation was published, so a reader that
3057 // sees one of these stores also sees the generation it has to retry on.
3058 std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_release);
3059 const uint64_t generation = generation_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
3060 const Anchor& current = anchors_[generation & 1];
3061 const uint64_t current_ticks = current.ticks.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
3062 const uint64_t current_ns = current.ns.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
3063 const uint64_t current_rate = current.ns_per_tick_q32.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
3064
3065 uint64_t ticks = 0, steady_ns = 0, wall_ns = 0;
3066 sample<std::chrono::steady_clock>(ticks, steady_ns);
3067 // The rate over everything since construction: steady_clock's own read jitter
3068 // shrinks against an ever longer span. A rate that disagrees with the last by
3069 // over 1% means the counter and steady_clock parted ways (a suspend that one
3070 // of them counted), so measuring starts over from here instead.
3071 if (ticks > base_ticks_ && steady_ns > base_steady_ns_) {
3072 const uint64_t measured = static_cast<uint64_t>(static_cast<double>(steady_ns - base_steady_ns_) *
3073 4294967296.0 / static_cast<double>(ticks - base_ticks_));
3074 if (measured > rate_q32_ - rate_q32_ / 100 && measured < rate_q32_ + rate_q32_ / 100) {
3075 rate_q32_ = measured;
3076 } else {
3077 base_ticks_ = ticks;
3078 base_steady_ns_ = steady_ns;
3079 }
3080 }
3081
3082 sample<std::chrono::system_clock>(ticks, wall_ns);
3083 const uint64_t projected = project(ticks, current_ticks, current_ns, current_rate);
3084 const int64_t error = static_cast<int64_t>(wall_ns - projected);
3085 const int64_t slew_limit = static_cast<int64_t>(resync_interval_ns_ / 1000); // 0.1% of the interval
3086 uint64_t anchor_ns = projected;
3087 uint64_t rate = rate_q32_;
3088 if (error > slew_limit || error < -slew_limit) {
3089 anchor_ns = wall_ns; // the wall clock jumped: follow it, as system_clock would
3090 } else {
3091 // Continuous at the anchor, and back on the wall clock one interval later.
3092 const double correction = static_cast<double>(error) / static_cast<double>(resync_interval_ns_);
3093 rate = static_cast<uint64_t>(static_cast<double>(rate_q32_) * (1.0 + correction));
3094 }
3095
3096 Anchor& next = anchors_[(generation + 1) & 1];
3097 next.ticks.store(ticks, std::memory_order_relaxed);
3098 next.ns.store(anchor_ns, std::memory_order_relaxed);
3099 next.ns_per_tick_q32.store(rate, std::memory_order_relaxed);
3100 generation_.store(generation + 1, std::memory_order_release);
3101 resyncing_.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
3102 return true;
3103}
3104
3105namespace detail {
3106
3128class producer_ring {
3129public:
3130 static constexpr uint32_t kLayoutVersion = 1;
3131 static constexpr uint32_t kRecordAlign = 8;
3132 static constexpr uint32_t kRecordHeader = 8;
3134 static constexpr uint32_t kWrapMarker = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
3135
3136 struct deleter {
3137 void operator()(producer_ring* ring) const noexcept;
3138 };
3139 using pointer = std::unique_ptr<producer_ring, deleter>;
3140
3142 static constexpr size_t block_size(uint64_t capacity) noexcept {
3143 return sizeof(producer_ring) + static_cast<size_t>(capacity);
3144 }
3145
3147 static constexpr bool valid_capacity(uint64_t capacity) noexcept {
3148 return capacity >= 64 && std::has_single_bit(capacity);
3149 }
3150
3156 static producer_ring* create(void* memory, uint64_t capacity) noexcept {
3157 assert(valid_capacity(capacity));
3158 assert(reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(memory) % alignof(producer_ring) == 0);
3159 return ::new (memory) producer_ring(capacity);
3160 }
3161
3166 static pointer allocate(uint64_t capacity, bool prefault = true) {
3167 void* memory = ::operator new(block_size(capacity), std::align_val_t{alignof(producer_ring)});
3168 pointer ring{create(memory, capacity)};
3169 if (prefault) {
3170 ring->prefault();
3171 }
3172 return ring;
3173 }
3174
3177 void prefault() noexcept { std::memset(data(), 0, static_cast<size_t>(capacity_)); }
3178
3179 uint64_t capacity() const noexcept { return capacity_; }
3180 uint32_t layout_version() const noexcept { return layout_version_; }
3181
3184 uint32_t max_payload() const noexcept {
3185 return static_cast<uint32_t>(std::min<uint64_t>(capacity_ / 2, UINT32_MAX - kRecordAlign)) - kRecordHeader;
3186 }
3187
3188 // ---- producer side: one thread ----
3189
3198 uint8_t* try_reserve(uint32_t payload) noexcept {
3199 assert(payload <= max_payload());
3200 const uint64_t size = (uint64_t{kRecordHeader} + payload + (kRecordAlign - 1)) & ~uint64_t{kRecordAlign - 1};
3201 const uint64_t pos = write_pos_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); // only this thread writes it
3202 const uint64_t offset = pos & mask_;
3203 const uint64_t to_end = capacity_ - offset;
3204 const uint64_t skip = size <= to_end ? 0 : to_end;
3205 const uint64_t end = pos + skip + size;
3206 if (end - cached_read_pos_ > capacity_) [[unlikely]] {
3207 // The only load of the reader's line, so in steady state it never leaves the reader's core.
3208 cached_read_pos_ = read_pos_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
3209 if (end - cached_read_pos_ > capacity_) {
3210 return nullptr;
3211 }
3212 }
3213 uint8_t* const base = data();
3214 if (skip != 0) {
3215 store_u32(base + offset, kWrapMarker);
3216 }
3217 const uint64_t start = (pos + skip) & mask_;
3218 store_u32(base + start, static_cast<uint32_t>(size));
3219 pending_end_ = end;
3220 return base + start + kRecordHeader;
3221 }
3222
3224 void publish() noexcept {
3225 records_.store(records_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) + 1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
3226 write_pos_.store(pending_end_, std::memory_order_release);
3227 }
3228
3230 void drop() noexcept { drops_.store(drops_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) + 1, std::memory_order_relaxed); }
3232 uint64_t drops() const noexcept { return drops_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }
3233
3236 void mark_shared_strings(uint64_t end) noexcept { shared_strings_end_.store(end, std::memory_order_relaxed); }
3237 uint64_t shared_strings_end() const noexcept { return shared_strings_end_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }
3239 uint64_t reserved_end() const noexcept { return pending_end_; }
3240
3244 void set_spill_gate(uint64_t position) noexcept { spill_gate_.store(position, std::memory_order_release); }
3245 uint64_t spill_gate() const noexcept { return spill_gate_.load(std::memory_order_acquire); }
3246
3247 // ---- either side ----
3248
3250 uint64_t written() const noexcept { return write_pos_.load(std::memory_order_acquire); }
3252 uint64_t released() const noexcept { return read_pos_.load(std::memory_order_acquire); }
3254 uint64_t records() const noexcept { return records_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }
3256 uint64_t released_records() const noexcept { return released_records_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }
3257
3258private:
3259 friend class ring_reader;
3260
3261 explicit producer_ring(uint64_t capacity) noexcept : capacity_(capacity), mask_(capacity - 1) {}
3262
3263 uint8_t* data() noexcept { return reinterpret_cast<uint8_t*>(this) + sizeof(producer_ring); }
3264 const uint8_t* data() const noexcept { return reinterpret_cast<const uint8_t*>(this) + sizeof(producer_ring); }
3265
3266 static void store_u32(uint8_t* at, uint32_t value) noexcept { std::memcpy(at, &value, sizeof(value)); }
3267 static uint32_t load_u32(const uint8_t* at) noexcept {
3268 uint32_t value;
3269 std::memcpy(&value, at, sizeof(value));
3270 return value;
3271 }
3272
3273 // Read-only once built, but for the rare shared-strings mark.
3274 alignas(64) uint32_t layout_version_ = kLayoutVersion;
3275 uint64_t capacity_;
3276 uint64_t mask_;
3277 std::atomic<uint64_t> shared_strings_end_{0};
3278 // Producer-owned: the reader only ever loads write_pos_.
3279 alignas(64) std::atomic<uint64_t> write_pos_{0};
3280 uint64_t pending_end_ = 0; // what publish() moves write_pos_ to
3281 uint64_t cached_read_pos_ = 0; // the last read_pos_ the producer looked at
3282 std::atomic<uint64_t> drops_{0};
3283 std::atomic<uint64_t> records_{0};
3284 std::atomic<uint64_t> spill_gate_{0};
3285 // Reader-owned: the producer only loads read_pos_, and only when the ring looks full.
3286 alignas(64) std::atomic<uint64_t> read_pos_{0};
3287 std::atomic<uint64_t> released_records_{0};
3288};
3289
3290static_assert(std::atomic<uint64_t>::is_always_lock_free,
3291 "producer_ring must be lock-free: it is meant to be shared between processes");
3292static_assert(std::is_standard_layout_v<producer_ring> && sizeof(producer_ring) % 64 == 0,
3293 "producer_ring is a block layout: its data must start on a cache line");
3294
3295inline void producer_ring::deleter::operator()(producer_ring* ring) const noexcept {
3296 ring->~producer_ring();
3297 ::operator delete(ring, std::align_val_t{alignof(producer_ring)});
3298}
3299
3310class ring_reader {
3311public:
3312 ring_reader() noexcept = default;
3313 explicit ring_reader(producer_ring& ring) noexcept
3314 : ring_(&ring), cursor_(ring.released()), batch_end_(cursor_), popped_(ring.released_records()) {}
3315
3316 producer_ring* ring() const noexcept { return ring_; }
3317
3320 bool refresh() noexcept {
3321 batch_end_ = ring_->write_pos_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
3322 return cursor_ != batch_end_;
3323 }
3324
3334 std::optional<std::span<const uint8_t>> peek() noexcept {
3335 const uint64_t capacity = ring_->capacity_;
3336 const uint8_t* const base = ring_->data();
3337 while (cursor_ != batch_end_) {
3338 const uint64_t offset = cursor_ & ring_->mask_;
3339 const uint64_t left = batch_end_ - cursor_;
3340 const uint32_t size = producer_ring::load_u32(base + offset);
3341 if (size == producer_ring::kWrapMarker) {
3342 const uint64_t to_end = capacity - offset;
3343 if (to_end > left) {
3344 break;
3345 }
3346 cursor_ += to_end;
3347 continue;
3348 }
3349 if (size < producer_ring::kRecordHeader || size % producer_ring::kRecordAlign != 0 ||
3350 size > left || size > capacity - offset) {
3351 break;
3352 }
3353 current_size_ = size;
3354 return std::span<const uint8_t>{base + offset + producer_ring::kRecordHeader,
3355 size - producer_ring::kRecordHeader};
3356 }
3357 if (cursor_ != batch_end_) [[unlikely]] {
3358 ++corrupt_;
3359 cursor_ = batch_end_;
3360 }
3361 return std::nullopt;
3362 }
3363
3365 void pop() noexcept {
3366 assert(current_size_ != 0);
3367 cursor_ += current_size_;
3368 current_size_ = 0;
3369 ++popped_;
3370 }
3371
3373 void release() noexcept {
3374 ring_->released_records_.store(popped_, std::memory_order_relaxed);
3375 ring_->read_pos_.store(cursor_, std::memory_order_release);
3376 }
3377
3379 bool batch_done() const noexcept { return cursor_ == batch_end_; }
3380
3382 void skip() noexcept {
3383 cursor_ = batch_end_ = ring_->written();
3384 popped_ = ring_->records();
3385 current_size_ = 0;
3386 release();
3387 }
3388
3390 uint64_t corrupt() const noexcept { return corrupt_; }
3391
3392private:
3393 producer_ring* ring_ = nullptr;
3394 uint64_t cursor_ = 0;
3395 uint64_t batch_end_ = 0;
3396 uint32_t current_size_ = 0;
3397 uint64_t corrupt_ = 0;
3398 uint64_t popped_ = 0;
3399};

3402template<typename T>
3403using cold_arg_t = std::conditional_t<std::is_scalar_v<std::remove_cvref_t<T>>, std::remove_cvref_t<T>, T&&>;
3404
3407template<typename T>
3408inline constexpr bool is_copied_string_v = [] {
3409 using B = std::remove_cvref_t<T>;
3410 using D = std::decay_t<T>;
3411 return std::is_same_v<D, BinaryView> || std::is_same_v<D, std::string> ||
3412 std::is_same_v<D, std::string_view> || std::is_same_v<D, const char*> ||
3413 std::is_same_v<D, char*> ||
3414 (std::is_array_v<B> && std::is_same_v<std::remove_cv_t<std::remove_extent_t<B>>, char>);
3415}();
3416
3419template<typename T>
3420inline constexpr bool uses_string_ring_v = [] {
3421 using D = std::decay_t<T>;
3422 if constexpr (is_copied_string_v<T> || std::is_same_v<D, bool> || std::is_same_v<D, char> ||
3423 std::is_same_v<D, unsigned char> || std::is_same_v<D, wchar_t> ||
3424 std::is_floating_point_v<D> || std::is_pointer_v<D> ||
3425 std::is_same_v<D, std::chrono::system_clock::time_point>) {
3426 return false;
3427 } else if constexpr (std::is_enum_v<D>) {
3428 return uses_string_ring_v<std::underlying_type_t<D>>;
3429 } else if constexpr (std::is_integral_v<D>) {
3430 return sizeof(D) > sizeof(int64_t);
3431 } else {
3432 return true; // a class converting to an arithmetic type, e.g. std::atomic<int>
3433 }
3434}();

3450struct alignas(64) thread_ring_slot {
3451 static constexpr uint32_t kFree = 0;
3452 static constexpr uint32_t kClaimed = 1;
3453 static constexpr uint32_t kActive = 2;
3454 static constexpr uint32_t kOrphaned = 3;
3455
3456 // Read by the writer and by claiming threads.
3457 std::atomic<uint32_t> state{kFree};
3458 std::atomic<producer_ring*> ring{nullptr};
3459 std::atomic<uint64_t> owner{0}; // os_thread_id() of the thread holding it
3464 std::atomic<uint64_t> ticket{0};
3465 // The owning thread's alone, from whichever module it logs.
3466 alignas(64) uint64_t spill_end = 0; // past its last spilled entry in the shared queue; 0 when none is pending
3467 uint32_t spill_check = 0; // spilled calls left before looking at the writer's progress again
3468 bool prefaulted = false; // every page of the ring touched once (Logger::prepare_thread())
3469
3470 ~thread_ring_slot() {
3471 if (producer_ring* r = ring.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
3472 producer_ring::deleter{}(r);
3473 }
3474 }
3475};

3479struct thread_ring_tls {

3482 producer_ring* ring; // null: the registry was full, log through the shared ring
3483 thread_ring_slot* slot; // ring's registry slot
3484 uint64_t ticket; // slot->ticket when this module attached
3485 uint32_t thread_id;
3486};

3499struct thread_ring_exit {
3500 thread_ring_slot* slot = nullptr;
3501 const std::atomic<uint64_t>* generation_source = nullptr;
3502 uint64_t generation = 0;
3503
3504 ~thread_ring_exit() {
3505 // A changed generation means the registry was torn down: leave it alone.
3506 if (slot && generation_source->load(std::memory_order_acquire) == generation) {
3507 slot->ticket.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed); // before anyone may take it over
3508 slot->state.store(thread_ring_slot::kOrphaned, std::memory_order_release);
3509 }
3510 }
3511};

3515inline constexpr size_t kEntryHeaderBytes = offsetof(LogEntry, args);
3516
3518struct ring_view {
3519 producer_ring* ring = nullptr;
3520 ring_reader reader;
3521 const uint8_t* head = nullptr; // peeked record, not yet dispatched
3522 uint32_t head_size = 0;
3523 uint64_t head_timestamp = 0;
3524 int64_t last_poll_ns = 0; // when refresh() last found records
3525 uintptr_t delta = 0; // remote: this mapping's address minus the producer's
3526 bool gated = false; // wait out the poll interval before the next refresh()
3527 bool remote = false; // a producer process's ring: its addresses need translating
3528
3530 bool hold_next() noexcept {
3531 const auto payload = reader.peek();
3532 if (!payload) {
3533 reader.release(); // a corrupt batch was skipped
3534 return false;
3535 }
3536 head = payload->data();
3537 head_size = static_cast<uint32_t>(payload->size());
3538 // A record too short for an entry is corrupt, and dispatch_ring_head()
3539 // drops it. Don't read its timestamp, since the record can end at the end
3540 // of the ring or of a producer's mapping. Its timestamp stays 0, so it goes first.
3541 head_timestamp = 0;
3542 if (head_size >= kEntryHeaderBytes) [[likely]] {
3543 std::memcpy(&head_timestamp, head + offsetof(LogEntry, timestamp), sizeof(head_timestamp));
3544 }
3545 return true;
3546 }
3547};

3558inline bool writer_barrier_available() noexcept {
3559#if SLICK_LOGGER_TSAN
3560 return false; // TSan cannot see the barrier
3561#elif defined(_WIN32)
3562 return true;
3563#elif defined(__linux__) && defined(__NR_membarrier)
3564 static const bool registered = ::syscall(__NR_membarrier, 1 << 4 /* REGISTER_PRIVATE_EXPEDITED */, 0, 0) == 0;
3565 return registered;
3566#else
3567 return false;
3568#endif

3571inline void writer_barrier() noexcept {
3572#if SLICK_LOGGER_TSAN
3573 std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_seq_cst);
3574#elif defined(_WIN32)
3575 ::FlushProcessWriteBuffers();
3576#elif defined(__linux__) && defined(__NR_membarrier)
3577 ::syscall(__NR_membarrier, 1 << 3 /* PRIVATE_EXPEDITED */, 0, 0);
3578#else
3579 std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_seq_cst);
3580#endif
3581}

3588struct alignas(64) shm_registry_slot {
3589 static constexpr uint32_t kFree = 0;
3590 static constexpr uint32_t kClaiming = 1; // a producer is building its segment
3591 static constexpr uint32_t kActive = 2;
3592 static constexpr uint32_t kClosing = 3; // shut down: the collector drains it, then frees it
3593
3596 std::atomic<uint64_t> control{0};
3597 std::atomic<uint32_t> pid{0};
3598 std::atomic<uint64_t> start_time{0}; // process_start_time(pid)
3599
3600 static constexpr uint32_t state_of(uint64_t control) noexcept { return static_cast<uint32_t>(control); }
3601 static constexpr uint32_t generation_of(uint64_t control) noexcept { return static_cast<uint32_t>(control >> 32); }
3602 static constexpr uint64_t make(uint32_t state, uint32_t generation) noexcept {
3603 return (uint64_t{generation} << 32) | state;
3604 }
3605};

3614struct shm_registry {
3615 static constexpr uint64_t kMagic = 0x4745524C474B4C53ull; // "SLKGLREG"
3616 static constexpr uint32_t kLayoutVersion = 1;
3617 static constexpr uint32_t kSlotCount = 64;
3618
3619 alignas(64) std::atomic<uint32_t> ready;
3620 uint32_t layout_version;
3621 uint64_t magic;
3622 uint32_t slot_count;
3624 std::atomic<uint64_t> changes;
3626 std::atomic<uint64_t> string_epoch;
3628 alignas(64) std::atomic<uint64_t> collector;
3631 alignas(64) std::atomic<uint64_t> read_index;
3632 shm_registry_slot slots[kSlotCount];

3636struct alignas(64) shm_ring_segment {
3637 static constexpr uint64_t kMagic = 0x474E524C474B4C53ull; // "SLKGLRNG"
3638 static constexpr uint32_t kLayoutVersion = 1;
3639 static constexpr uint32_t kMaxRings = 64;
3640
3641 uint64_t magic;
3642 uint32_t layout_version;
3643 uint32_t ring_layout_version; // producer_ring::kLayoutVersion
3644 uint32_t generation; // the registry slot's when this was built
3645 uint32_t ring_count;
3646 uint64_t ring_capacity;
3649 uint64_t producer_base;
3650 uint32_t record_layout; // record_layout_of(): both sides must read a record alike
3651
3653 static constexpr uint32_t record_layout_of() noexcept {
3654 return static_cast<uint32_t>(offsetof(LogEntry, args) << 16 | sizeof(LogArgument));
3655 }
3656 static constexpr size_t bytes(uint32_t count, uint64_t capacity) noexcept {
3657 return sizeof(shm_ring_segment) + size_t{count} * producer_ring::block_size(capacity);
3658 }
3659 producer_ring* ring(uint32_t index) noexcept {
3660 return reinterpret_cast<producer_ring*>(reinterpret_cast<uint8_t*>(this) + sizeof(shm_ring_segment) +
3661 size_t{index} * producer_ring::block_size(ring_capacity));
3662 }
3663};

3666inline uint64_t collector_lease(uint32_t pid) noexcept {
3667 return (uint64_t{pid} << 32) | static_cast<uint32_t>(process_start_time(pid));

3670inline bool collector_lease_running(uint64_t lease) noexcept {
3671 const uint32_t pid = static_cast<uint32_t>(lease >> 32);
3672 if (!process_running(pid, 0)) {
3673 return false;
3674 }
3675 const uint32_t start = static_cast<uint32_t>(process_start_time(pid));
3676 return start == 0 || start == static_cast<uint32_t>(lease);

4803 std::atomic<uint64_t> stats_string_frontier_{0};
4804 // The cursor pair the frontier is promoted from, and the rule behind it.
4805 //
4806 // A producer reserves its string bytes before it reserves an entry slot, so
4807 // string order and slot order are two independent races and neither implies
4808 // the other. Taking the frontier from the string of whichever entry the
4809 // writer happened to drain last is therefore unsound: a producer holding
4810 // earlier string bytes can take a later slot, and the frontier sails past
4811 // bytes still in use, reporting an idle ring while the ring is not.
4812 //
4813 // So the frontier is never read out of an entry at all. The writer instead
4814 // snapshots the entry reservation cursor and then the string reservation
4815 // cursor, and promotes the string half only once its read cursor has passed
4816 // the entry half. At that moment every slot taken before the snapshot has
4817 // been drained, and every one of those strings was reserved before the
4818 // snapshot too, so the whole string ring below it is provably free, whatever
4819 // order the producers published in. Between promotions the frontier simply
4820 // stays put, which is the conservative direction: the span grows and the
4821 // gauge reads fuller, which is what a stalled writer means. A thread ring's
4822 // record with strings here announces them first; see advance_string_frontier().
4823 //
4824 // The one window it cannot see is a producer that has reserved string bytes
4825 // and not yet taken a slot: it is invisible in both orderings, so a producer
4826 // preempted there still hides its bytes until it publishes. Closing that
4827 // needs the producer to announce the reservation, which is not worth what it
4828 // would cost the logging path.
4829 //
4830 // Writer thread only. Relaxed everywhere: these carry positions and order
4831 // nothing else.
4832 uint64_t stats_gen_entry_ = 0;
4833 uint64_t stats_gen_string_ = 0;
4834 bool stats_gen_open_ = false;
4835 // Thread rings with records holding strings in the string ring, and how far
4836 // each must drain; rescanned when *string_epoch_ moves past stats_seen_epoch_.
4837 std::vector<std::pair<const detail::producer_ring*, uint64_t>> stats_gen_rings_;
4838 uint64_t stats_seen_epoch_ = UINT64_MAX;
4839 // Configuration, written by init() before the thread starts and read only by
4840 // it afterwards, so it needs no synchronization.
4841 bool stats_enabled_ = false;
4842 uint32_t stats_interval_ms_ = 0;
4843 uint32_t stats_sample_interval_ms_ = 0;
4844 size_t stats_max_file_size_ = 0;
4845 std::filesystem::path stats_file_;
4846 // Everything below is touched only by the statistics thread, between the
4847 // point start() spawns it and the point shutdown() joins it.
4848 uint64_t stats_depth_max_ = 0;
4849 uint64_t stats_depth_sum_ = 0;
4850 uint32_t stats_sample_count_ = 0;
4851 uint64_t stats_string_inflight_max_ = 0;
4854 uint64_t stats_string_last_ = 0;
4855 bool stats_string_seen_ = false;
4856 // Buffer before stream, so ~ofstream never flushes from a freed buffer.

4858 std::ofstream stats_stream_;
4859 size_t stats_bytes_written_ = 0;
4861 LogStats stats_previous_{};
4862 bool stats_has_previous_ = false;
4863 std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point stats_last_report_{};
4866 bool stats_write_failed_ = false;
4867 // The writer thread's copy of the entry it is dispatching: sinks are handed
4868 // this, never the ring slot, which a producer can rewrite at any moment (see
4869 // snapshot_entry()). Owned by that thread alone, so no synchronization is needed.
4870 LogEntry entry_scratch_{};
4871 // Entries snapshot_entry() discarded because a producer rewrote their slot

4896inline bool ISink::should_log(const Logger& logger, LogLevel level) const noexcept {
4897 // Cheapest checks first; the logger's own check ends in an atomic load.
4898 return index_ >= 0
4899 && level >= min_level_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)
4900 && logger.should_log(level);
4901}
4902
4903inline bool ISink::should_log(LogLevel level) const noexcept {
4904 return should_log(Logger::instance(), level);
4905}
4906
4907template<typename FormatT, typename... Args>
4908inline void ISink::log(LogLevel level, FormatT&& format, Args&&... args) {
4909 // Resolve the logger once and use it for both the check and the call: two
4910 // Logger::instance() calls would be two atomic loads, and a set_instance()
4911 // landing between them would test one logger and log to another.
4912 auto& logger = Logger::instance();
4913 // Same predicate the LOG_SINK_* macros use. Two reasons to check it here:
4914 // below-threshold entries then cost neither a queue slot nor a string-ring
4915 // copy, and a sink that is not attached to a logger has index -1, which
4916 // log_to_sink() would read as "broadcast to every sink". The arguments were
4917 // already evaluated by the caller; use the macros to avoid that too.
4918 if (!should_log(logger, level)) {
4919 return;
4920 }
4921 logger.log_to_sink(index_, level, std::forward<FormatT>(format), std::forward<Args>(args)...);
4922}
