4959inline std::string_view view_string_ref(StringRef ref) noexcept {
4960 if (!ref.ptr) {
4961 return {};
4962 }
4963 return ref.length ? std::string_view{ref.ptr, ref.length} : std::string_view{ref.ptr};
4964}
4965
4972inline std::span<const std::byte> view_binary(StringRef ref) noexcept {
4973 if (!ref.ptr || !ref.length) {
4974 return {};
4975 }
4976 return {reinterpret_cast<const std::byte*>(ref.ptr), ref.length};
4977}
4978
4989inline void append_binary_arg(std::string& out, std::string_view format_spec, StringRef ref) {
4990 constexpr size_t kDefaultPreviewBytes = 64;
4991 static constexpr char kLower[] = "0123456789abcdef";
4992 static constexpr char kUpper[] = "0123456789ABCDEF";
4993
4994 const auto bytes = view_binary(ref);
4995 const char* digits = format_spec.find('X') != std::string_view::npos ? kUpper : kLower;
4996
4997 size_t preview = kDefaultPreviewBytes;
4998 if (const auto dot = format_spec.find('.'); dot != std::string_view::npos) {
4999 preview = 0;
5000 for (size_t i = dot + 1; i < format_spec.size() && format_spec[i] >= '0' && format_spec[i] <= '9'; ++i) {
5001 preview = preview * 10 + static_cast<size_t>(format_spec[i] - '0');
5002 }
5003 }
5004
5005 const size_t shown = std::min(preview, bytes.size());
5006 // Written straight into the caller's buffer: a temporary string here would be
5007 // an allocation and a copy of a few hundred bytes per binary argument.
5008 out.reserve(out.size() + shown * 2 + 24);
5009 for (size_t i = 0; i < shown; ++i) {
5010 const auto byte = static_cast<unsigned char>(bytes[i]);
5011 out += digits[byte >> 4];
5012 out += digits[byte & 0x0F];
5013 }
5014 if (shown < bytes.size()) {
5015 out += "...(";
5016 out += std::to_string(bytes.size());
5017 out += " bytes)";
5018 }
5019}
5020
5022inline std::string format_binary_arg(std::string_view format_spec, StringRef ref) {
5023 std::string result;
5024 append_binary_arg(result, format_spec, ref);
5025 return result;
5026}
5027
5037inline char spec_presentation_type(std::string_view format_spec) noexcept {
5038 // The shortest spec carrying a type is "{:d}".
5039 if (format_spec.size() < 4 || format_spec.find(':') == std::string_view::npos) {
5040 return '\0';
5041 }
5042 const char type = format_spec[format_spec.size() - 2];
5043 switch (type) {
5044 case 'b': case 'B': case 'c': case 'd': case 'o': case 'x': case 'X':
5045 return type;
5046 default:
5047 return '\0';
5048 }
5049}
5050
5058inline size_t encode_utf8(uint32_t code_point, char (&out)[4]) noexcept {
5059 if (code_point < 0x80) {
5060 out[0] = static_cast<char>(code_point);
5061 return 1;
5062 }
5063 if (code_point < 0x800) {
5064 out[0] = static_cast<char>(0xC0 | (code_point >> 6));
5065 out[1] = static_cast<char>(0x80 | (code_point & 0x3F));
5066 return 2;
5067 }
5068 if (code_point < 0x10000) {
5069 if (code_point >= 0xD800 && code_point <= 0xDFFF) {
5070 return 0;
5071 }
5072 out[0] = static_cast<char>(0xE0 | (code_point >> 12));
5073 out[1] = static_cast<char>(0x80 | ((code_point >> 6) & 0x3F));
5074 out[2] = static_cast<char>(0x80 | (code_point & 0x3F));
5075 return 3;
5076 }
5077 if (code_point <= 0x10FFFF) {
5078 out[0] = static_cast<char>(0xF0 | (code_point >> 18));
5079 out[1] = static_cast<char>(0x80 | ((code_point >> 12) & 0x3F));
5080 out[2] = static_cast<char>(0x80 | ((code_point >> 6) & 0x3F));
5081 out[3] = static_cast<char>(0x80 | (code_point & 0x3F));
5082 return 4;
5083 }
5084 return 0;
5085}
5086
5091template<typename T>
5092inline uint64_t checked_spec_value(T value) {
5093 if (value < 0) {
5094 throw std::format_error("dynamic width or precision must not be negative");
5095 }
5096 return static_cast<uint64_t>(value);
5097}
5098
5112inline uint64_t dynamic_spec_value(const LogArgument& arg) {
5113 switch (arg.type) {
5114 case ArgType::INT8_T: return checked_spec_value(arg.value.i8);
5115 case ArgType::INT16_T: return checked_spec_value(arg.value.i16);
5116 case ArgType::INT32_T: return checked_spec_value(arg.value.i32);
5117 case ArgType::INT64_T: return checked_spec_value(arg.value.i64);
5118 case ArgType::UINT8_T: return arg.value.u8;
5119 case ArgType::UINT16_T: return arg.value.u16;
5120 case ArgType::UINT32_T: return arg.value.u32;
5121 case ArgType::UINT64_T: return arg.value.u64;
5122 default:
5123 throw std::format_error("dynamic width or precision must be an integer argument");
5124 }
5125}
5126
5138template<typename T>
5139inline void append_one_arg(std::string& out, std::string_view format_spec, T value) {
5140 std::vformat_to(std::back_inserter(out), format_spec, std::make_format_args(value));
5141}
5142
5147inline void append_log_argument(std::string& out, std::string_view format_spec, const LogArgument& arg) {
5148 // Every case passes the union member by value through append_one_arg:
5149 // these members are packed and may be misaligned, so a reference must
5150 // never be bound directly to one. See append_one_arg.
5151 switch (arg.type) {
5152 case ArgType::BOOL:
5153 append_one_arg(out, format_spec, arg.value.b);
5154 break;
5155 case ArgType::CHAR:
5156 append_one_arg(out, format_spec, arg.value.c);
5157 break;
5158 case ArgType::U_CHAR:
5159 append_one_arg(out, format_spec, arg.value.uc);
5160 break;
5161 case ArgType::WCHAR: {
5162 // std::format has no wchar_t formatter in a narrow (char)
5163 // context on any supported standard library, so a wchar_t
5164 // cannot go through append_one_arg directly. Reproduce what
5165 // std::format does for char instead: render it as text by
5166 // default and as a number under a b/B/d/o/x/X presentation
5167 // type. Dispatching on the spec rather than on the value
5168 // keeps "{}" and "{:5}" producing the same kind of output
5169 // (and the same default alignment) for every code point,
5170 // instead of silently switching to a number above U+007F.
5171 //
5172 // wchar_t is signed on Linux and macOS, so go through the
5173 // unsigned type first: a negative value is a code unit, not
5174 // a number to sign-extend into a huge unsigned one.
5175 const auto code_point = static_cast<uint32_t>(
5176 static_cast<std::make_unsigned_t<wchar_t>>(arg.value.wc));
5177
5178 std::string_view spec{format_spec};
5179 std::string char_spec;
5180 bool as_number = false;
5181 switch (spec_presentation_type(format_spec)) {
5182 case 'b': case 'B': case 'd': case 'o': case 'x': case 'X':
5183 as_number = true;
5184 break;
5185 case 'c':
5186 // "render as a character" is already the default
5187 // here, and std::format's string formatter would
5188 // reject the 'c', so drop it.
5189 char_spec.assign(format_spec, 0, format_spec.size() - 2);
5190 char_spec += '}';
5191 spec = char_spec;
5192 break;
5193 default:
5194 break;
5195 }
5196
5197 char utf8[4];
5198 const size_t utf8_len = as_number ? 0 : encode_utf8(code_point, utf8);
5199 if (utf8_len > 0) {
5200 append_one_arg(out, spec, std::string_view{utf8, utf8_len});
5201 } else {
5202 // Either the spec asked for a number, or the value is
5203 // not a Unicode scalar value and has no character to
5204 // print, so fall back to the numeric code point.
5205 append_one_arg(out, spec, code_point);
5206 }
5207 break;
5208 }
5209 case ArgType::INT8_T:
5210 append_one_arg(out, format_spec, arg.value.i8);
5211 break;
5212 case ArgType::UINT8_T:
5213 append_one_arg(out, format_spec, arg.value.u8);
5214 break;
5215 case ArgType::INT16_T:
5216 append_one_arg(out, format_spec, arg.value.i16);
5217 break;
5218 case ArgType::UINT16_T:
5219 append_one_arg(out, format_spec, arg.value.u16);
5220 break;
5221 case ArgType::INT32_T:
5222 append_one_arg(out, format_spec, arg.value.i32);
5223 break;
5224 case ArgType::UINT32_T:
5225 append_one_arg(out, format_spec, arg.value.u32);
5226 break;
5227 case ArgType::INT64_T:
5228 append_one_arg(out, format_spec, arg.value.i64);
5229 break;
5230 case ArgType::UINT64_T:
5231 append_one_arg(out, format_spec, arg.value.u64);
5232 break;
5233 case ArgType::FLOAT:
5234 append_one_arg(out, format_spec, arg.value.f);
5235 break;
5236 case ArgType::DOUBLE:
5237 append_one_arg(out, format_spec, arg.value.d);
5238 break;
5239 case ArgType::PTR:
5240 append_one_arg(out, format_spec, arg.value.ptr);
5241 break;
5242 case ArgType::STRING_LITERAL:
5243 append_one_arg(out, format_spec, arg.value.literal_ptr);
5244 break;
5245 case ArgType::STRING_DYNAMIC:
5246 append_one_arg(out, format_spec, view_string_ref(arg.value.dynamic_str));
5247 break;
5248 case ArgType::BLOB:
5249 // Rendered here rather than through append_one_arg: std::format
5250 // has no formatter for raw bytes, and the spec flags a payload
5251 // accepts are its own.
5252 append_binary_arg(out, format_spec, arg.value.dynamic_str);
5253 break;
5254 default:
5255 out += "<UNKNOWN>";
5256 break;
5257 }
5258}
5259
5274inline void append_plain_argument(std::string& out, const LogArgument& arg) {
5275 char buf[32]; // a double's shortest form is at most 24 characters
5276 auto append_int = [&](auto value) {
5277 const std::to_chars_result result = std::to_chars(buf, buf + sizeof(buf), value);
5278 out.append(buf, result.ptr);
5279 };
5280 auto append_float = [&](auto value) {
5281 if (!std::isfinite(value)) {
5282 return false;
5283 }
5284 append_int(value);
5285 return true;
5286 };
5287 // Every union member is read by value: they are packed and may be
5288 // misaligned. See append_one_arg.
5289 switch (arg.type) {
5290 case ArgType::BOOL:
5291 out += arg.value.b ? std::string_view{"true"} : std::string_view{"false"};
5292 return;
5293 case ArgType::CHAR:
5294 out += arg.value.c;
5295 return;
5296 // unsigned char and int8_t are integer types to std::format, not characters.
5297 case ArgType::U_CHAR: append_int(arg.value.uc); return;
5298 case ArgType::INT8_T: append_int(arg.value.i8); return;
5299 case ArgType::UINT8_T: append_int(arg.value.u8); return;
5300 case ArgType::INT16_T: append_int(arg.value.i16); return;
5301 case ArgType::UINT16_T: append_int(arg.value.u16); return;
5302 case ArgType::INT32_T: append_int(arg.value.i32); return;
5303 case ArgType::UINT32_T: append_int(arg.value.u32); return;
5304 case ArgType::INT64_T: append_int(arg.value.i64); return;
5305 case ArgType::UINT64_T: append_int(arg.value.u64); return;
5306 case ArgType::FLOAT:
5307 if (append_float(arg.value.f)) {
5308 return;
5309 }
5310 break;
5311 case ArgType::DOUBLE:
5312 if (append_float(arg.value.d)) {
5313 return;
5314 }
5315 break;
5316 case ArgType::PTR: {
5317 const std::to_chars_result result = std::to_chars(
5318 buf, buf + sizeof(buf), reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(arg.value.ptr), 16);
5319 out += "0x";
5320 out.append(buf, result.ptr);
5321 return;
5322 }
5323 case ArgType::WCHAR: {
5324 // As append_log_argument renders it under "{}": the character,
5325 // UTF-8 encoded, or the code point if it is not a scalar value.
5326 const auto code_point = static_cast<uint32_t>(
5327 static_cast<std::make_unsigned_t<wchar_t>>(arg.value.wc));
5328 char utf8[4];
5329 const size_t utf8_len = encode_utf8(code_point, utf8);
5330 if (utf8_len > 0) {
5331 out.append(utf8, utf8_len);
5332 } else {
5333 append_int(code_point);
5334 }
5335 return;
5336 }
5337 case ArgType::STRING_LITERAL: {
5338 const char* const text = arg.value.literal_ptr;
5339 if (text) {
5340 out += text;
5341 return;
5342 }
5343 break;
5344 }
5345 case ArgType::STRING_DYNAMIC:
5346 out += view_string_ref(arg.value.dynamic_str);
5347 return;
5348 default:
5349 break;
5350 }
5351 append_log_argument(out, "{}", arg);
5352}
5353
5354namespace detail {
5355
5363struct format_op {
5364 enum class kind : uint8_t {
5365 literal,
5366 missing,
5367 plain,
5368 arg,
5369 nested,
5370 nested_missing,
5372 unmatched,
5373 };
5374 kind type;
5375 uint8_t index;
5376 uint32_t off;
5377 uint32_t len;
5378};
5379
5382struct spec_piece {
5383 static constexpr uint8_t kNoNested = 0xFF; // arg_count is a uint8_t, so no index reaches it
5384 uint32_t off;
5385 uint32_t len;
5386 uint8_t nested;
5387};
5388
5416class message_formats {
5417public:
5418 static message_formats& local() {
5419 thread_local message_formats formats;
5420 return formats;
5421 }
5422
5428 void append(std::string& out, std::string_view fmt, const LogEntry& entry) {
5429 if ((entry.flags & kEntryStaticFormat) && fmt.data()) {
5430 render(out, fmt, entry, find(fmt, entry.arg_count));
5431 return;
5432 }
5433 const mark scratch = mark_now();
5434 try {
5435 render(out, fmt, entry, parse(fmt, entry.arg_count));
5436 } catch (...) {
5437 rewind(scratch);
5438 throw;
5439 }
5440 rewind(scratch);
5441 }
5442
5443private:
5444 struct op_range {
5445 uint32_t begin;
5446 uint32_t end;
5447 };
5448
5449 struct slot {
5450 const char* ptr = nullptr; // null marks an empty slot
5451 uint32_t len = 0;
5452 uint8_t arg_count = 0;
5453 op_range ops{};
5454 size_t text = 0; // offset of the text's copy in texts_
5455 };
5456
5458 struct mark {
5459 size_t ops;
5460 size_t pieces;
5461 size_t specs;
5462 };
5463
5464 static constexpr size_t kInitialSlots = 256; // power of two
5465
5466 static size_t hash(const char* ptr) noexcept {
5467 // Fibonacci hashing: literals sit at small, aligned strides, which a
5468 // plain mask of the address would pile into a few slots.
5469 return static_cast<size_t>(
5470 (static_cast<uint64_t>(reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(ptr)) * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ull) >> 32);
5471 }
5472
5473 SLICK_LOGGER_FORCE_INLINE op_range find(std::string_view fmt, uint8_t arg_count) {
5474 if (!slots_.empty()) {
5475 const size_t mask = slots_.size() - 1;
5476 for (size_t i = hash(fmt.data()) & mask;; i = (i + 1) & mask) {
5477 slot& s = slots_[i];
5478 if (s.ptr == fmt.data() && s.len == fmt.size() && s.arg_count == arg_count) {
5479 if (std::memcmp(texts_.data() + s.text, fmt.data(), fmt.size()) == 0) [[likely]] {
5480 return s.ops;
5481 }
5482 return reparse(s, fmt);
5483 }
5484 if (!s.ptr) {
5485 break;
5486 }
5487 }
5488 }
5489 return insert(fmt, arg_count);
5490 }
5491
5492 op_range insert(std::string_view fmt, uint8_t arg_count) {
5493 const mark before = mark_now();
5494 const size_t text = texts_.size();
5495 try {
5496 const op_range ops = parse(fmt, arg_count);
5497 texts_.append(fmt);
5498 // Kept at most half full, so a probe stays short.
5499 if ((used_ + 1) * 2 > slots_.size()) {
5500 grow();
5501 }
5502 place(slot{fmt.data(), static_cast<uint32_t>(fmt.size()), arg_count, ops, text});
5503 ++used_;
5504 return ops;
5505 } catch (...) {
5506 rewind(before);
5507 texts_.resize(text);
5508 throw;
5509 }
5510 }
5511
5514 op_range reparse(slot& s, std::string_view fmt) {
5515 const mark before = mark_now();
5516 try {
5517 s.ops = parse(fmt, s.arg_count);
5518 } catch (...) {
5519 rewind(before);
5520 throw;
5521 }
5522 std::memcpy(texts_.data() + s.text, fmt.data(), fmt.size());
5523 return s.ops;
5524 }
5525
5526 void grow() {
5527 std::vector<slot> old(slots_.empty() ? kInitialSlots : slots_.size() * 2);
5528 old.swap(slots_);
5529 for (const slot& s : old) {
5530 if (s.ptr) {
5531 place(s);
5532 }
5533 }
5534 }
5535
5536 void place(const slot& s) noexcept {
5537 const size_t mask = slots_.size() - 1;
5538 size_t i = hash(s.ptr) & mask;
5539 while (slots_[i].ptr) {
5540 i = (i + 1) & mask;
5541 }
5542 slots_[i] = s;
5543 }
5544
5545 mark mark_now() const noexcept { return {ops_.size(), pieces_.size(), specs_.size()}; }
5546
5547 void rewind(const mark& m) noexcept {
5548 ops_.resize(m.ops);
5549 pieces_.resize(m.pieces);
5550 specs_.resize(m.specs);
5551 }
5552
5553 void emit(format_op::kind type, size_t index, size_t off, size_t len) {
5554 ops_.push_back(format_op{type, static_cast<uint8_t>(index),
5555 static_cast<uint32_t>(off), static_cast<uint32_t>(len)});
5556 }
5557
5567 op_range parse(std::string_view fmt, uint8_t arg_count) {
5568 const size_t begin = ops_.size();
5569
5570 // Text runs that turn out adjacent ("a{{b" is "a{" then "b") become one
5571 // op, so an escaped brace costs no extra append.
5572 auto literal = [&](size_t off, size_t len) {
5573 if (len == 0) {
5574 return;
5575 }
5576 if (ops_.size() > begin) {
5577 format_op& last = ops_.back();
5578 if (last.type == format_op::kind::literal && last.off + last.len == off) {
5579 last.len += static_cast<uint32_t>(len);
5580 return;
5581 }
5582 }
5583 emit(format_op::kind::literal, 0, off, len);
5584 };
5585
5586 size_t pos = 0;
5587 uint8_t arg_index = 0;
5588
5589 while (pos < fmt.length()) {
5590 const size_t brace_start = fmt.find_first_of("{}", pos);
5591 if (brace_start == std::string_view::npos) {
5592 literal(pos, fmt.length() - pos);
5593 break;
5594 }
5595
5596 if (fmt[brace_start] == '{' &&
5597 brace_start + 1 < fmt.length() &&
5598 fmt[brace_start + 1] == '{') {
5599 literal(pos, brace_start + 1 - pos); // keeps one of the two
5600 pos = brace_start + 2;
5601 continue;
5602 }
5603
5604 if (fmt[brace_start] == '}') {
5605 if (brace_start + 1 < fmt.length() &&
5606 fmt[brace_start + 1] == '}') {
5607 literal(pos, brace_start + 1 - pos);
5608 pos = brace_start + 2;
5609 continue;
5610 }
5611 // Nothing past this point can reach the output.
5612 literal(pos, brace_start - pos);
5613 emit(format_op::kind::unmatched, 0, 0, 0);
5614 break;
5615 }
5616
5617 literal(pos, brace_start - pos);
5618
5619 // Find this field's closing brace. The spec may itself contain
5620 // replacement fields, for a dynamic width or precision
5621 // ("{:{}.{}f}"), so the first '}' is not necessarily the one that
5622 // ends the field; step over a nested field rather than stopping
5623 // inside it. A nested field cannot nest any further, so one level
5624 // is all the grammar allows for.
5625 //
5626 // Only a '{' inside the format spec starts one: everything before
5627 // the ':' is the argument index, which is digits alone. Reading a
5628 // '{' there as nested would change what a malformed string like
5629 // "{unclosed and {}" means, and it is not a nested field anyway.
5630 size_t brace_end = brace_start + 1;
5631 bool in_spec = false;
5632 while (brace_end < fmt.length() && fmt[brace_end] != '}') {
5633 if (fmt[brace_end] == ':') {
5634 in_spec = true;
5635 } else if (in_spec && fmt[brace_end] == '{') {
5636 const size_t nested_end = fmt.find('}', brace_end + 1);
5637 if (nested_end == std::string_view::npos) {
5638 break;
5639 }
5640 brace_end = nested_end + 1;
5641 continue;
5642 }
5643 ++brace_end;
5644 }
5645 if (brace_end >= fmt.length() || fmt[brace_end] != '}') {
5646 // Malformed format string: the rest goes out as it is.
5647 literal(brace_start, fmt.length() - brace_start);
5648 break;
5649 }
5650 pos = brace_end + 1;
5651
5652 // A placeholder may carry an explicit argument index ({0}, {1}, ...)
5653 // in front of the optional ':' format spec, so the parser has to
5654 // resolve the index itself: each argument is formatted against its
5655 // own single-argument spec.
5656 //
5657 // std::format rejects a format string that mixes explicit indices
5658 // with bare {} automatic placeholders. This parser tolerates the
5659 // mix (the two counters are independent) rather than losing the
5660 // whole log line to a format error.
5661 uint8_t resolved_index = 0;
5662 size_t spec_prefix_len = 0; // leading digits consumed from the placeholder
5663 if (brace_start + 1 < brace_end &&
5664 fmt[brace_start + 1] >= '0' && fmt[brace_start + 1] <= '9') {
5665 uint32_t id = 0;
5666 while (brace_start + 1 + spec_prefix_len < brace_end &&
5667 fmt[brace_start + 1 + spec_prefix_len] >= '0' &&
5668 fmt[brace_start + 1 + spec_prefix_len] <= '9') {
5669 if (id < arg_count) {
5670 // Once id reaches arg_count it is already out of range,
5671 // and further digits can only push it further out, so
5672 // stop accumulating there. Multiplying through a long
5673 // digit run would overflow uint32_t and could wrap a
5674 // huge index back onto a valid argument: "{4294967296}"
5675 // would otherwise select argument 0.
5676 id = id * 10 + static_cast<uint32_t>(fmt[brace_start + 1 + spec_prefix_len] - '0');
5677 }
5678 ++spec_prefix_len;
5679 }
5680 if (id >= arg_count) {
5681 // Not enough arguments. A manual index: the automatic
5682 // counter stays untouched.
5683 emit(format_op::kind::missing, 0, 0, 0);
5684 continue;
5685 }
5686 resolved_index = static_cast<uint8_t>(id);
5687 } else {
5688 if (arg_index >= arg_count) {
5689 // Not enough arguments
5690 emit(format_op::kind::missing, 0, 0, 0);
5691 continue;
5692 }
5693 // Claimed here rather than at the end of the iteration: a nested
5694 // width or precision field takes the *next* automatic argument,
5695 // so this field's own has to be spoken for before the spec below
5696 // is walked.
5697 resolved_index = arg_index++;
5698 }
5699
5700 // Rebuild the spec as a single-argument one. The explicit index is
5701 // dropped ({1:>8} -> {:>8}, {1} -> {}), and a nested width or
5702 // precision field is cut out, to be replaced on each line by the
5703 // decimal value of the argument it names ({0:{1}} over (x, 8) ->
5704 // {:8}). Substituting the value rather than forwarding the nested
5705 // field is what keeps every argument formatting against a
5706 // one-argument spec, which is what lets each ArgType hand
5707 // std::format its own union member.
5708 const size_t spec_off = specs_.size();
5709 const size_t pieces_begin = pieces_.size();
5710 size_t piece_off = spec_off;
5711 specs_ += '{';
5712 bool nested_arg_missing = false;
5713 bool spec_started = false; // same rule the scan above applied
5714 for (size_t i = brace_start + 1 + spec_prefix_len; i < brace_end; ) {
5715 const char ch = fmt[i];
5716 if (ch != '{' || !spec_started) {
5717 spec_started = spec_started || ch == ':';
5718 specs_ += ch;
5719 ++i;
5720 continue;
5721 }
5722
5723 ++i; // step past the nested field's '{'
5724 uint32_t nested_id = 0;
5725 bool nested_explicit = false;
5726 while (i < brace_end && fmt[i] >= '0' && fmt[i] <= '9') {
5727 if (nested_id < arg_count) {
5728 nested_id = nested_id * 10 + static_cast<uint32_t>(fmt[i] - '0');
5729 }
5730 nested_explicit = true;
5731 ++i;
5732 }
5733 if (i < brace_end && fmt[i] == '}') {
5734 ++i; // step past the nested field's '}'
5735 }
5736
5737 if (!nested_explicit) {
5738 nested_id = arg_index;
5739 if (arg_index < arg_count) {
5740 ++arg_index; // as above, never past the end
5741 }
5742 }
5743 if (nested_id >= arg_count) {
5744 nested_arg_missing = true;
5745 break;
5746 }
5747 pieces_.push_back(spec_piece{static_cast<uint32_t>(piece_off),
5748 static_cast<uint32_t>(specs_.size() - piece_off),
5749 static_cast<uint8_t>(nested_id)});
5750 piece_off = specs_.size();
5751 }
5752
5753 const size_t piece_count = pieces_.size() - pieces_begin;
5754 if (nested_arg_missing) {
5755 // The width or precision names an argument that was never
5756 // passed, so there is no spec to format against. Reported as a
5757 // missing argument like any other, rather than as a format
5758 // error, which would cost the whole line. The fields before it
5759 // are still evaluated on each line, as they were read before
5760 // the missing one was found and may themselves be in error.
5761 if (piece_count == 0) {
5762 specs_.resize(spec_off);
5763 emit(format_op::kind::missing, 0, 0, 0);
5764 } else {
5765 emit(format_op::kind::nested_missing, 0, pieces_begin, piece_count);
5766 }
5767 continue;
5768 }
5769 specs_ += '}';
5770
5771 if (piece_count == 0 && specs_.size() - spec_off == 2) {
5772 // "{}", or "{1}" once its index is dropped: no spec to hand on.
5773 specs_.resize(spec_off);
5774 emit(format_op::kind::plain, resolved_index, 0, 0);
5775 } else if (piece_count == 0) {
5776 emit(format_op::kind::arg, resolved_index, spec_off, specs_.size() - spec_off);
5777 } else {
5778 pieces_.push_back(spec_piece{static_cast<uint32_t>(piece_off),
5779 static_cast<uint32_t>(specs_.size() - piece_off),
5780 spec_piece::kNoNested});
5781 emit(format_op::kind::nested, resolved_index, pieces_begin, piece_count + 1);
5782 }
5783 }
5784
5785 return {static_cast<uint32_t>(begin), static_cast<uint32_t>(ops_.size())};
5786 }
5787
5790 void build_nested_spec(const LogEntry& entry, const format_op& op) {
5791 nested_spec_.clear();
5792 for (uint32_t p = op.off; p < op.off + op.len; ++p) {
5793 const spec_piece& piece = pieces_[p];
5794 nested_spec_.append(specs_.data() + piece.off, piece.len);
5795 if (piece.nested == spec_piece::kNoNested) {
5796 continue;
5797 }
5798 // A zero width is dropped rather than written out. A literal 0
5799 // in the width position is the zero-padding flag and not a
5800 // width at all ("{:0}" pads a number, and is rejected outright
5801 // for a text argument), whereas a width of zero just means no
5802 // minimum width, which is what leaving it out says.
5803 // Zero is a meaningful precision ("{:.0f}"), so only the width
5804 // case is dropped; the '.' that introduces a precision is
5805 // already in the spec by the time we get here.
5806 const uint64_t value = dynamic_spec_value(entry.args[piece.nested]);
5807 if (value != 0 || nested_spec_.back() == '.') {
5808 append_uint(nested_spec_, value);
5809 }
5810 }
5811 }
5812
5813 void render(std::string& out, std::string_view fmt, const LogEntry& entry, op_range ops) {
5814 for (uint32_t i = ops.begin; i < ops.end; ++i) {
5815 const format_op& op = ops_[i];
5816 switch (op.type) {
5817 case format_op::kind::literal:
5818 out.append(fmt.data() + op.off, op.len);
5819 break;
5820 case format_op::kind::missing:
5821 out += "<MISSING_ARG>";
5822 break;
5823 case format_op::kind::plain:
5824 append_plain_argument(out, entry.args[op.index]);
5825 break;
5826 case format_op::kind::arg:
5827 append_log_argument(out, std::string_view{specs_.data() + op.off, op.len},
5828 entry.args[op.index]);
5829 break;
5830 case format_op::kind::nested:
5831 build_nested_spec(entry, op);
5832 append_log_argument(out, nested_spec_, entry.args[op.index]);
5833 break;
5834 case format_op::kind::nested_missing:
5835 build_nested_spec(entry, op);
5836 out += "<MISSING_ARG>";
5837 break;
5838 case format_op::kind::unmatched:
5839 throw std::format_error("unmatched '}' in format string");
5840 }
5841 }
5842 }
5843
5844 std::vector<slot> slots_; // open addressing, power-of-two sized
5845 size_t used_ = 0;
5846 std::vector<format_op> ops_; // every cached format's ops, back to back
5847 std::vector<spec_piece> pieces_; // nested specs' pieces
5848 std::string specs_; // spec text the ops and pieces point into
5849 std::string texts_; // a copy of each cached format's text
5850 std::string nested_spec_; // a nested spec, rebuilt per field
5851};
5852
5853} // namespace detail
5854
5865inline bool append_formatted_message(std::string& out, const LogEntry& entry) {
5866 const std::string_view fmt = view_string_ref(entry.format);
5867 if (entry.arg_count == 0) {
5868 out += fmt;
5869 return true;
5870 }
5871
5872 // Everything appended past here is rolled back if formatting fails, so the
5873 // error text replaces the partial message instead of trailing it.
5874 const size_t base = out.size();
5875
5876 // std::make_format_args doesn't work with custom types on MSVC, so the format
5877 // specifiers are parsed by hand and applied to each argument, which keeps
5878 // std::format's behavior.
5879 try {
5880 out.reserve(base + fmt.size() + 256); // Reserve some space for formatting
5881 detail::message_formats::local().append(out, fmt, entry);
5882 return true;
5883 } catch (const std::format_error& e) {
5884 out.resize(base);
5885 out += "[FORMAT_ERROR: ";
5886 out += e.what();
5887 out += ']';
5888 return false;
5889 } catch (...) {
5890 out.resize(base);
5891 out += "[FORMAT_ERROR: Unknown format error]";
5892 return false;
5893 }
5894}
5895
5896inline std::pair<std::string_view, bool> ISink::formatted_message(const LogEntry& entry) {
5897 detail::dispatch_message* const current = detail::current_dispatch();
5898 if (current && current->entry == &entry) {
5899 if (!current->formatted) {
5900 current->text.clear();
5901 current->good = append_formatted_message(current->text, entry);
5902 current->formatted = true;
5903 }
5904 return {current->text, current->good};
5905 }
5906 message_buffer_.clear();
5907 const bool good = append_formatted_message(message_buffer_, entry);
5908 return {message_buffer_, good};
5909}
5910
5911inline std::pair<std::string, bool> ISink::format_log_message(const LogEntry& entry) {
5912 const auto [message, good] = formatted_message(entry);
5913 return {std::string(message), good};
5914}
5915
5916inline void write_source_location(detail::line_writer& out, const LogEntry& entry) noexcept {
5917 if (!has_source_location(entry)) {
5918 return;
5919 }
5920 out.put(" [", 2);
5921 out.put(view_string_ref(entry.file));
5922 out.put(':');
5923 out.put_uint(entry.line);
5924 out.put(']');
5925}
5926
5928inline constexpr size_t source_location_bound(size_t file_length) noexcept {
5929 return file_length + detail::kMaxUint32Digits + 4; // " [", ':', ']'
5930}
5931
5937inline void write_process_id(detail::line_writer& out, const LogEntry& entry) noexcept {
5938 if (entry.pid == 0) {
5939 return;
5940 }
5941 out.put(" [", 2);
5942 out.put_uint(entry.pid);
5943 if (entry.tag[0] != '\0') {
5944 out.put(':');
5945 out.put(entry.tag, detail::tag_length(entry.tag));
5946 }
5947 out.put(']');
5948}
5949
5952inline constexpr size_t kProcessIdBound = detail::kMaxUint32Digits + SLICK_LOGGER_TAG_SIZE + 4;
5953
5958inline size_t default_layout_bound(const LogEntry& entry, const TimestampFormatter& timestamp_formatter,
5959 std::string_view level_name, std::string_view message,
5960 size_t file_length) noexcept {
5961 return timestamp_formatter.write_bound() + level_name.size() + message.size() + 4 // " [", "] "
5962 + (entry.pid ? kProcessIdBound : 0)
5963 + (has_source_location(entry) ? source_location_bound(file_length) : 0);
5964}
5965
5967inline size_t source_file_length(const LogEntry& entry) noexcept {
5968 return has_source_location(entry) ? view_string_ref(entry.file).size() : 0;
5969}
5970
5979inline void write_default_layout(detail::line_writer& out, const LogEntry& entry,
5980 const TimestampFormatter& timestamp_formatter,
5981 std::string_view level_name, std::string_view message) {
5982 timestamp_formatter.write(out, entry.timestamp);
5983 out.put(" [", 2);
5984 out.put(level_name);
5985 out.put(']');
5986 write_process_id(out, entry);
5987 write_source_location(out, entry);
5988 out.put(' ');
5989 out.put(message);
5990}
5991
5993inline void append_default_layout(std::string& out, const LogEntry& entry,
5994 const TimestampFormatter& timestamp_formatter,
5995 std::string_view level_name, std::string_view message) {
5996 detail::line_writer writer(out, default_layout_bound(entry, timestamp_formatter, level_name,
5997 message, source_file_length(entry)));
5998 write_default_layout(writer, entry, timestamp_formatter, level_name, message);
5999 writer.finish();
6000}
6001
6002inline PatternFormatter::Flag PatternFormatter::flag_for(char c, std::string_view pattern) {
6003 switch (c) {
6004 case 'v': return Flag::kMessage;
6005 case 'l': return Flag::kLevel;
6006 case 'L': return Flag::kLevelShort;
6007 case 'P': return Flag::kProcessId;
6008 case 'k': return Flag::kTag;
6009 case 'n': return Flag::kSinkName;
6010 case 's': return Flag::kSourceFile;
6011 case '#': return Flag::kSourceLine;
6012 case '@': return Flag::kSourceLoc;
6013 case 'Y': return Flag::kYear4;
6014 case 'y': return Flag::kYear2;
6015 case 'm': return Flag::kMonth;
6016 case 'd': return Flag::kDay;
6017 case 'H': return Flag::kHour24;
6018 case 'I': return Flag::kHour12;
6019 case 'p': return Flag::kAmPm;
6020 case 'M': return Flag::kMinute;
6021 case 'S': return Flag::kSecond;
6022 case 'e': return Flag::kMillis;
6023 case 'f': return Flag::kMicros;
6024 case 'F': return Flag::kNanos;
6025 case 'T': return Flag::kTimeHMS;
6026 case 'D': return Flag::kDateMDY;
6027 case 'c': return Flag::kDateTimeFull;
6028 case 'E': return Flag::kEpochSeconds;
6029 case 'a': return Flag::kWeekdayShort;
6030 case 'A': return Flag::kWeekdayLong;
6031 case 'b': return Flag::kMonthShort;
6032 case 'B': return Flag::kMonthLong;
6033 case '^': return Flag::kColorBegin;
6034 case '$': return Flag::kColorEnd;
6035 case '+': return Flag::kDefaultHeader;
6036 case 'q': return Flag::kConfiguredTimestamp;
6037 case 't':
6038 #if SLICK_LOGGER_ENABLE_THREAD_ID
6039 return Flag::kThreadId;
6040 #else
6041 throw std::invalid_argument(
6042 "slick-logger: pattern flag '%t' needs SLICK_LOGGER_ENABLE_THREAD_ID, which "
6043 "this build switched off, so every entry would render a thread id of 0. "
6044 "Pattern: " + std::string(pattern));
6045 #endif
6046
6047 // spdlog flags this logger has no data for. Named apart from the unknown
6048 // case so the message can say why rather than just "unrecognized".
6049 case '!': case 'g': case 'o': case 'i': case 'u': case 'O': case 'z':
6050 throw std::invalid_argument(
6051 std::string("slick-logger: pattern flag '%") + c + "' is not supported. See "
6052 "PatternFormatter for the flags that are. Pattern: " + std::string(pattern));
6053
6054 default:
6055 throw std::invalid_argument(
6056 std::string("slick-logger: unknown pattern flag '%") + c + "' in pattern: "
6057 + std::string(pattern));
6058 }
6059}
6060
6061inline void PatternFormatter::compile(std::string_view pattern) {
6062 ops_.clear();
6063 literals_.clear();
6064 pattern_.assign(pattern);
6065 has_color_range_ = false;
6066 needs_cache_ = false;
6067 needs_subsecond_ = false;
6068
6069 // Literal runs are accumulated and flushed as one op each, so "a%lb%vc" costs
6070 // three literal ops rather than one per character.
6071 std::string literal;
6072 auto flush_literal = [&]() {
6073 if (literal.empty()) {
6074 return;
6075 }
6076 Op op;
6077 op.flag = Flag::kLiteral;
6078 op.literal_off = static_cast<uint32_t>(literals_.size());
6079 op.literal_len = static_cast<uint32_t>(literal.size());
6080 literals_ += literal;
6081 literal.clear();
6082 ops_.push_back(op);
6083 };
6084
6085 for (size_t i = 0; i < pattern.size(); ++i) {
6086 if (pattern[i] != '%') {
6087 literal += pattern[i];
6088 continue;
6089 }
6090
6091 // "%[-][width]<flag>"
6092 size_t j = i + 1;
6093 bool left_align = false;
6094 uint32_t width = 0;
6095 if (j < pattern.size() && pattern[j] == '-') {
6096 left_align = true;
6097 ++j;
6098 }
6099 while (j < pattern.size() && pattern[j] >= '0' && pattern[j] <= '9') {
6100 width = std::min(width * 10 + static_cast<uint32_t>(pattern[j] - '0'), kMaxFieldWidth);
6101 ++j;
6102 }
6103 if (j >= pattern.size()) {
6104 throw std::invalid_argument(
6105 "slick-logger: pattern ends with a dangling '%': " + std::string(pattern));
6106 }
6107 if (pattern[j] == '%') {
6108 // "%-5%" would silently drop the -5. A width on an escaped percent is
6109 // meaningless, so it is far more likely a mistyped flag than intent.
6110 if (left_align || width != 0) {
6111 throw std::invalid_argument(
6112 "slick-logger: '%%' takes no width or alignment; did you mean a flag "
6113 "letter? Pattern: " + std::string(pattern));
6114 }
6115 literal += '%';
6116 i = j;
6117 continue;
6118 }
6119
6120 // Resolved before the literal is flushed so an invalid flag throws with
6121 // the formatter still untouched.
6122 const Flag flag = flag_for(pattern[j], pattern);
6123 flush_literal();
6124
6125 Op op;
6126 op.flag = flag;
6127 op.left_align = left_align;
6128 op.width = static_cast<uint8_t>(width);
6129 ops_.push_back(op);
6130
6131 if (flag == Flag::kColorBegin) {
6132 has_color_range_ = true;
6133 }
6134 if (flag_needs_cache(flag)) {
6135 needs_cache_ = true;
6136 } else if (flag == Flag::kMillis || flag == Flag::kMicros || flag == Flag::kNanos) {
6137 needs_subsecond_ = true;
6138 }
6139 // %+ renders the message itself, and the level flags need to know whether
6140 // formatting the message failed, so all four force the format pass.
6141 if (flag == Flag::kMessage || flag == Flag::kDefaultHeader ||
6142 flag == Flag::kLevel || flag == Flag::kLevelShort) {
6143 needs_message_ = true;
6144 }
6145 i = j;
6146 }
6147 flush_literal();
6148
6149 // Whether the last %^ was ever closed. Fixed by the op list, so it is settled
6150 // here rather than tracked per line.
6151 color_left_open_ = false;
6152 for (const Op& op : ops_) {
6153 if (op.flag == Flag::kColorBegin) {
6154 color_left_open_ = true;
6155 } else if (op.flag == Flag::kColorEnd) {
6156 color_left_open_ = false;
6157 }
6158 }
6159
6160 fuse_cached_slices();
6161 fuse_literal_prefixes();
6162
6163 // Tallied from the fused ops, whose slices are what actually gets written.
6164 fixed_bound_ = 0;
6165 message_count_ = level_name_count_ = sink_name_count_ = source_file_count_ = 0;
6166 color_begin_count_ = color_end_count_ = timestamp_count_ = default_layout_count_ = 0;
6167 for (const Op& op : ops_) {
6168 fixed_bound_ += op.prefix_len + fixed_length(op) + op.width;
6169 switch (op.flag) {
6170 case Flag::kMessage: ++message_count_; break;
6171 case Flag::kLevel: ++level_name_count_; break;
6172 case Flag::kSinkName: ++sink_name_count_; break;
6173 case Flag::kSourceFile:
6174 case Flag::kSourceLoc: ++source_file_count_; break;
6175 case Flag::kColorBegin: ++color_begin_count_; break;
6176 case Flag::kColorEnd: ++color_end_count_; break;
6177 case Flag::kConfiguredTimestamp: ++timestamp_count_; break;
6178 case Flag::kDefaultHeader: ++default_layout_count_; break;
6179 default: break;
6180 }
6181 }
6182}
6183
6184inline size_t PatternFormatter::fixed_length(const Op& op) noexcept {
6185 using namespace detail;
6186 switch (op.flag) {
6187 case Flag::kCachedSlice: return op.literal_len + (op.frac_digits ? 1 + op.frac_digits : 0);
6188 case Flag::kLiteral: return op.literal_len;
6189 case Flag::kLevelShort: return 1;
6190 case Flag::kThreadId:
6191 case Flag::kProcessId:
6192 case Flag::kSourceLine: return kMaxUint32Digits;
6193 case Flag::kSourceLoc: return kMaxUint32Digits + 1; // the file is counted per line
6194 case Flag::kTag: return SLICK_LOGGER_TAG_SIZE;
6195 case Flag::kYear4: return 4;
6196 case Flag::kYear2: case Flag::kMonth: case Flag::kDay:
6197 case Flag::kHour24: case Flag::kHour12: case Flag::kAmPm:
6198 case Flag::kMinute: case Flag::kSecond: return 2;
6199 case Flag::kMillis:
6200 case Flag::kMicros:
6201 case Flag::kNanos: return subsecond_digits(op.flag);
6202 case Flag::kTimeHMS: return kTimeLen;
6203 case Flag::kDateMDY: return 8;
6204 case Flag::kDateTimeFull: return 24;
6205 case Flag::kEpochSeconds: return kMaxUint64Digits;
6206 case Flag::kWeekdayShort:
6207 case Flag::kMonthShort: return 3;
6208 case Flag::kWeekdayLong:
6209 case Flag::kMonthLong: return kMaxDayOrMonthName;
6210 // Supplied by the line; see line_bound().
6211 case Flag::kMessage: case Flag::kLevel: case Flag::kSinkName: case Flag::kSourceFile:
6212 case Flag::kColorBegin: case Flag::kColorEnd:
6213 case Flag::kDefaultHeader: case Flag::kConfiguredTimestamp:
6214 return 0;
6215 }
6216 return 0;
6217}
6218
6219SLICK_LOGGER_FORCE_INLINE size_t PatternFormatter::line_bound(const LogEntry& entry,
6220 const Context& ctx) const noexcept {
6221 size_t bound = fixed_bound_ + message_count_ * ctx.message.size()
6222 + level_name_count_ * ctx.level_name.size()
6223 + sink_name_count_ * ctx.sink_name.size()
6224 // One more of each for the escapes format() wraps a line in
6225 // itself, or closes a range left open with.
6226 + (color_begin_count_ + 1) * ctx.color_start.size()
6227 + (color_end_count_ + 1) * ctx.color_end.size();
6228 const size_t file_length =
6229 (source_file_count_ || default_layout_count_) ? source_file_length(entry) : 0;
6230 bound += source_file_count_ * file_length;
6231 if (ctx.timestamp) {
6232 bound += timestamp_count_ * ctx.timestamp->write_bound();
6233 if (default_layout_count_) {
6234 bound += default_layout_count_ * default_layout_bound(entry, *ctx.timestamp,
6235 ctx.level_name, ctx.message,
6236 file_length);
6237 }
6238 }
6239 return bound;
6240}
6241
6242inline bool PatternFormatter::flag_needs_cache(Flag flag) noexcept {
6243 switch (flag) {
6244 // A fused run is only ever built out of the calendar flags below, so it
6245 // belongs here with them.
6246 case Flag::kCachedSlice:
6247 case Flag::kYear4: case Flag::kYear2: case Flag::kMonth: case Flag::kDay:
6248 case Flag::kHour24: case Flag::kHour12: case Flag::kAmPm:
6249 case Flag::kMinute: case Flag::kSecond:
6250 case Flag::kTimeHMS: case Flag::kDateMDY: case Flag::kDateTimeFull:
6251 case Flag::kWeekdayShort: case Flag::kWeekdayLong:
6252 case Flag::kMonthShort: case Flag::kMonthLong:
6253 return true;
6254 // %+ and %q render a timestamp of their own through TimestampFormatter,
6255 // which keeps its own cache lookup, so they do not need one here either.
6256 default:
6257 return false;
6258 }
6259}
6260
6261inline bool PatternFormatter::cached_slice_for(Flag flag, size_t& offset, size_t& length) noexcept {
6262 switch (flag) {
6263 case Flag::kYear4: offset = 0; length = 4; return true;
6264 case Flag::kYear2: offset = 2; length = 2; return true;
6265 case Flag::kMonth: offset = 5; length = 2; return true;
6266 case Flag::kDay: offset = 8; length = 2; return true;
6267 case Flag::kHour24: offset = 11; length = 2; return true;
6268 case Flag::kMinute: offset = 14; length = 2; return true;
6269 case Flag::kSecond: offset = 17; length = 2; return true;
6270 case Flag::kTimeHMS: offset = detail::kTimeOffset; length = detail::kTimeLen; return true;
6271 default: return false;
6272 }
6273}
6274
6275inline bool PatternFormatter::literal_matches_cached(std::string_view literal,
6276 size_t offset) noexcept {
6277 if (offset + literal.size() > detail::kDateTimeLen) {
6278 return false;
6279 }
6280 for (size_t i = 0; i < literal.size(); ++i) {
6281 // Only separators can match: a digit position varies per timestamp, so a
6282 // literal digit there would be a coincidence this must not act on.
6283 if (literal[i] != cached_separator_at(offset + i)) {
6284 return false;
6285 }
6286 }
6287 return true;
6288}
6289
6290inline void PatternFormatter::fuse_cached_slices() {
6291 std::vector<Op> fused;
6292 fused.reserve(ops_.size());
6293
6294 for (const Op& op : ops_) {
6295 size_t offset = 0;
6296 size_t length = 0;
6297
6298 // "<slice>.%f": the separator is the literal just fused past the slice.
6299 // Checked before anything else touches fused.back(), which is that literal.
6300 const uint32_t frac_digits = subsecond_digits(op.flag);
6301 if (frac_digits && op.width == 0 && fused.size() >= 2 &&
6302 fused.back().flag == Flag::kLiteral && fused.back().literal_len == 1 &&
6303 fused[fused.size() - 2].flag == Flag::kCachedSlice &&
6304 fused[fused.size() - 2].frac_digits == 0) {
6305 const char separator = literals_[fused.back().literal_off];
6306 fused.pop_back();
6307 fused.back().frac_sep = separator;
6308 fused.back().frac_digits = static_cast<uint8_t>(frac_digits);
6309 continue;
6310 }
6311
6312 // A padded field has to stay its own op: the padding is measured against
6313 // that field alone, not against whatever it would be fused with. Nor can
6314 // a slice grow once it has a fraction, which it writes last.
6315 if (op.width == 0 && !fused.empty() && fused.back().flag == Flag::kCachedSlice &&
6316 fused.back().frac_digits == 0) {
6317 Op& run = fused.back();
6318 const size_t run_end = run.literal_off + run.literal_len;
6319
6320 if (cached_slice_for(op.flag, offset, length) && offset == run_end) {
6321 run.literal_len += static_cast<uint32_t>(length);
6322 continue;
6323 }
6324 if (op.flag == Flag::kLiteral &&
6325 literal_matches_cached(std::string_view{literals_}.substr(op.literal_off, op.literal_len),
6326 run_end)) {
6327 run.literal_len += op.literal_len;
6328 continue;
6329 }
6330 }
6331
6332 if (op.width == 0 && cached_slice_for(op.flag, offset, length)) {
6333 Op slice;
6334 slice.flag = Flag::kCachedSlice;
6335 slice.literal_off = static_cast<uint32_t>(offset);
6336 slice.literal_len = static_cast<uint32_t>(length);
6337 fused.push_back(slice);
6338 continue;
6339 }
6340
6341 fused.push_back(op);
6342 }
6343
6344 ops_ = std::move(fused);
6345}
6346
6347inline void PatternFormatter::fuse_literal_prefixes() {
6348 std::vector<Op> fused;
6349 fused.reserve(ops_.size());
6350
6351 for (size_t i = 0; i < ops_.size(); ++i) {
6352 const Op& op = ops_[i];
6353 if (op.flag == Flag::kLiteral && i + 1 < ops_.size() && ops_[i + 1].flag != Flag::kLiteral) {
6354 Op next = ops_[++i];
6355 next.prefix_off = op.literal_off;
6356 next.prefix_len = op.literal_len;
6357 fused.push_back(next);
6358 continue;
6359 }
6360 fused.push_back(op);
6361 }
6362
6363 ops_ = std::move(fused);
6364}
6365
6366// Forced inline: this is the body of format()'s loop, and a call per op cost
6367// more than most ops' own work.
6368SLICK_LOGGER_FORCE_INLINE void PatternFormatter::write_op(detail::line_writer& out, const Op& op,
6369 const LogEntry& entry, const Context& ctx,
6370 const detail::second_cache* cache,
6371 uint32_t subsecond_ns) const {
6372 using namespace detail;
6373
6374 // Every date and time flag slices the "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" text that
6375 // cached_second() renders once per whole second, so none of them convert a
6376 // time_t or touch the locale. The caller supplies a cache for exactly the
6377 // flags that read one, the epoch placeholder standing in when localtime
6378 // fails, so a flag missing from flag_needs_cache() is a bug in that list
6379 // rather than a null this should quietly render around.
6380 assert(!flag_needs_cache(op.flag) || cache != nullptr);
6381
6382 switch (op.flag) {
6383 case Flag::kCachedSlice:
6384 out.put(cache->date_time + op.literal_off, op.literal_len);
6385 if (op.frac_digits) {
6386 out.put(op.frac_sep);
6387 write_subsecond(out.cursor(), subsecond_ns, op.frac_digits);
6388 out.advance(op.frac_digits);
6389 }
6390 break;
6391 case Flag::kLiteral:
6392 out.put(literals_.data() + op.literal_off, op.literal_len);
6393 break;
6394 case Flag::kMessage:
6395 out.put(ctx.message);
6396 break;
6397 case Flag::kLevel:
6398 out.put(ctx.level_name);
6399 break;
6400 case Flag::kLevelShort:
6401 out.put(to_short_string(ctx.level)[0]);
6402 break;
6403 case Flag::kThreadId:
6404 out.put_uint(entry.thread_id);
6405 break;
6406 case Flag::kProcessId:
6407 // A Local-mode entry carries no pid, but it was produced right here,
6408 // so print this process rather than a bare zero.
6409 out.put_uint(entry.pid ? entry.pid : current_process_id());
6410 break;
6411 case Flag::kTag:
6412 out.put(entry.tag, detail::tag_length(entry.tag));
6413 break;
6414 case Flag::kSinkName:
6415 out.put(ctx.sink_name);
6416 break;
6417 case Flag::kSourceFile:
6418 if (has_source_location(entry)) {
6419 out.put(view_string_ref(entry.file));
6420 }
6421 break;
6422 case Flag::kSourceLine:
6423 if (has_source_location(entry)) {
6424 out.put_uint(entry.line);
6425 }
6426 break;
6427 case Flag::kSourceLoc:
6428 if (has_source_location(entry)) {
6429 out.put(view_string_ref(entry.file));
6430 out.put(':');
6431 out.put_uint(entry.line);
6432 }
6433 break;
6434 case Flag::kYear4: out.put(cache->date_time, 4); break;
6435 case Flag::kYear2: out.put(cache->date_time + 2, 2); break;
6436 case Flag::kMonth: out.put(cache->date_time + 5, 2); break;
6437 case Flag::kDay: out.put(cache->date_time + 8, 2); break;
6438 case Flag::kHour24: out.put(cache->date_time + 11, 2); break;
6439 case Flag::kMinute: out.put(cache->date_time + 14, 2); break;
6440 case Flag::kSecond: out.put(cache->date_time + 17, 2); break;
6441 case Flag::kTimeHMS: out.put(cache->date_time + kTimeOffset, kTimeLen); break;
6442 case Flag::kHour12: {
6443 int hour = cache->tm.tm_hour % 12;
6444 if (hour == 0) {
6445 hour = 12;
6446 }
6447 write_2_digits(out.cursor(), static_cast<uint32_t>(hour));
6448 out.advance(2);
6449 break;
6450 }
6451 case Flag::kAmPm:
6452 out.put((cache->tm.tm_hour < 12) ? "AM" : "PM", 2);
6453 break;
6454 // Fixed-width digits are rendered in place: the writer's budget already
6455 // holds fixed_length() for them.
6456 case Flag::kMillis:
6457 case Flag::kMicros:
6458 case Flag::kNanos: {
6459 const uint32_t digits = subsecond_digits(op.flag);
6460 write_subsecond(out.cursor(), subsecond_ns, digits);
6461 out.advance(digits);
6462 break;
6463 }
6464 case Flag::kDateMDY: {
6465 char* p = out.cursor();
6466 std::memcpy(p, cache->date_time + 5, 2); // MM
6467 p[2] = '/';
6468 std::memcpy(p + 3, cache->date_time + 8, 2); // DD
6469 p[5] = '/';
6470 std::memcpy(p + 6, cache->date_time + 2, 2); // YY
6471 out.advance(8);
6472 break;
6473 }
6474 case Flag::kDateTimeFull:
6475 // "Www Mmm DD HH:MM:SS YYYY", the shape std::asctime produces.
6476 out.put(weekday_short(cache->tm.tm_wday));
6477 out.put(' ');
6478 out.put(month_short(cache->tm.tm_mon));
6479 out.put(' ');
6480 out.put(cache->date_time + 8, 2);
6481 out.put(' ');
6482 out.put(cache->date_time + kTimeOffset, kTimeLen);
6483 out.put(' ');
6484 out.put(cache->date_time, 4);
6485 break;
6486 case Flag::kEpochSeconds:
6487 out.put_uint(entry.timestamp / 1000000000ULL);
6488 break;
6489 case Flag::kWeekdayShort: out.put(weekday_short(cache->tm.tm_wday)); break;
6490 case Flag::kWeekdayLong: out.put(weekday_long(cache->tm.tm_wday)); break;
6491 case Flag::kMonthShort: out.put(month_short(cache->tm.tm_mon)); break;
6492 case Flag::kMonthLong: out.put(month_long(cache->tm.tm_mon)); break;
6493 case Flag::kColorBegin: out.put(ctx.color_start); break;
6494 case Flag::kColorEnd: out.put(ctx.color_end); break;
6495 case Flag::kDefaultHeader:
6496 if (ctx.timestamp) {
6497 write_default_layout(out, entry, *ctx.timestamp, ctx.level_name, ctx.message);
6498 }
6499 break;
6500 case Flag::kConfiguredTimestamp:
6501 if (ctx.timestamp) {
6502 ctx.timestamp->write(out, entry.timestamp);
6503 }
6504 break;
6505 }
6506}
6507
6508inline void PatternFormatter::format(std::string& out, const LogEntry& entry,
6509 const Context& ctx) const {
6510 // Null exactly when the pattern renders no calendar field, which is the only
6511 // case in which nothing reads it: every op that does is a flag_needs_cache()
6512 // flag, and those are what set needs_cache_. When one is present the pointer
6513 // is never null: a localtime failure renders the same 1970 placeholder the
6514 // built-in layout uses, which keeps every date op free of a null check.
6515 const detail::second_cache* cache = nullptr;
6516 if (needs_cache_) {
6517 cache = detail::cached_second(static_cast<int64_t>(entry.timestamp / 1000000000ULL));
6518 if (!cache) [[unlikely]] {
6519 cache = &detail::epoch_fallback_cache();
6520 }
6521 }
6522 uint32_t subsecond_ns = 0;
6523 if (needs_subsecond_) {
6524 subsecond_ns = static_cast<uint32_t>(entry.timestamp % 1000000000ULL);
6525 }
6526
6527 // Sized once for the whole line, so no op below checks capacity or grows.
6528 detail::line_writer writer(out, line_bound(entry, ctx));
6529
6530 // A pattern that does not mark its own range colors the whole line, which is
6531 // what the built-in layout does.
6532 const bool wrap_color = !ctx.color_start.empty() && !has_color_range_;
6533 if (wrap_color) {
6534 writer.put(ctx.color_start);
6535 }
6536
6537 // write_op() is forced inline, so it appears here exactly once: a second
6538 // copy for padded fields would double the loop and crowd the inliner out of
6539 // everything the op bodies call.
6540 for (const Op& op : ops_) {
6541 // Most ops carry no prefix. One test skips copy_bytes()' whole size ladder.
6542 if (op.prefix_len != 0) {
6543 writer.put(literals_.data() + op.prefix_off, op.prefix_len);
6544 }
6545 const size_t start = writer.offset();
6546 write_op(writer, op, entry, ctx, cache, subsecond_ns);
6547 if (op.width != 0) {
6548 writer.pad_from(start, op.width, op.left_align);
6549 }
6550 }
6551
6552 if (wrap_color) {
6553 writer.put(ctx.color_end);
6554 } else if (color_left_open_) {
6555 // "%^" with no "%$" means "color from here to the end of the line", not
6556 // "leave the terminal tinted for everything printed afterwards".
6557 writer.put(ctx.color_end);
6558 }
6559 writer.finish();
6560}

6596inline std::string_view ISink::format_log_entry(const LogEntry& entry,
6597 ColorFn color_for,
6598 std::string_view color_end) {
6599 format_buffer_.clear();
6600 append_log_entry(format_buffer_, entry, color_for, color_end);
6601 return format_buffer_;
6602}
6603
6604inline void ISink::append_log_entry(std::string& out, const LogEntry& entry,
6605 ColorFn color_for, std::string_view color_end) {
6606 const PatternFormatter* active = active_pattern_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
6607
6608 // The message comes first because a format error overrides the level that
6609 // gets printed, so neither the level nor its color can be resolved until the
6610 // message has been built. A pattern that renders neither skips the whole
6611 // std::format pass; needs_message() is what says so. When it is needed, the
6612 // logger formats it once per entry however many sinks render it.
6613 std::string_view message;
6614 bool good = true;
6615 if (!active || active->needs_message()) {
6616 std::tie(message, good) = formatted_message(entry);
6617 }
6618 // A message that could not be formatted is reported at ERROR whatever it was
6619 // logged at. Derived once here so every level-rendering flag, and the color,
6620 // agree on what the line says.
6621 const LogLevel level = good ? entry.level : LogLevel::L_ERROR;
6622 const std::string_view level_name = to_string(level);
6623 const std::string_view color_start = color_for ? color_for(level) : std::string_view{};
6624
6625 if (active) {
6626 PatternFormatter::Context ctx;
6627 ctx.message = message;
6628 ctx.level = level;
6629 ctx.level_name = level_name;
6630 ctx.sink_name = name_;
6631 ctx.timestamp = &timestamp_formatter_;
6632 ctx.color_start = color_start;
6633 ctx.color_end = color_end;
6634 active->format(out, entry, ctx);
6635 } else {
6636 detail::line_writer writer(out,
6637 color_start.size() + color_end.size()
6638 + default_layout_bound(entry, timestamp_formatter_, level_name,
6639 message, source_file_length(entry)));
6640 writer.put(color_start);
6641 write_default_layout(writer, entry, timestamp_formatter_, level_name, message);
6642 writer.put(color_end);
6643 writer.finish();
6644 }
6645}

6725inline void FileSinkBase::write_cached() {
6726 if (!write_cache_.empty()) {
6727 // A failed stream drops the batch, as it would have dropped each line.
6728 file_stream_.write(write_cache_.data(), static_cast<std::streamsize>(write_cache_.size()));
6729 write_cache_.clear();
6730 }
6731}
6732
6733inline size_t FileSinkBase::write_line(const LogEntry& entry) {
6734 if (write_cache_.capacity() < write_cache_size_) [[unlikely]] {
6735 // Once, with room for the line that crosses the threshold, so filling
6736 // the cache never reallocates it.
6737 write_cache_.reserve(write_cache_size_ + write_cache_size_ / 8 + 4096);
6738 }
6739 const size_t start = write_cache_.size();
6740 try {
6741 append_log_entry(write_cache_, entry);
6742 } catch (...) {
6743 write_cache_.resize(start); // never let half a line reach the file
6744 throw;
6745 }
6746 if constexpr (detail::kLineEnding.size() > 1) {
6747 // What text mode did to a message with newlines in it.
6748 if (std::memchr(write_cache_.data() + start, '\n', write_cache_.size() - start)) [[unlikely]] {
6749 const std::string line = write_cache_.substr(start);
6750 write_cache_.resize(start);
6751 for (const char c : line) {
6752 if (c == '\n') {
6753 write_cache_.append(detail::kLineEnding);
6754 } else {
6755 write_cache_.push_back(c);
6756 }
6757 }
6758 }
6759 }
6760 write_cache_.append(detail::kLineEnding);
6761 const size_t added = write_cache_.size() - start;
6762 if (write_cache_.size() >= write_cache_size_) {
6763 write_cached();
6764 }
6765 return added;
6766}

6791inline size_t existing_file_size(const std::filesystem::path& path) noexcept {
6792 std::error_code ec;

6796
6798inline std::string local_date(time_t time) {
6799 std::tm tm;
6800 if (!to_local_tm(time, tm)) {
6801 return {};
6802 }
6803 char date[11];
6804 std::strftime(date, sizeof(date), "%Y-%m-%d", &tm);
6805 return date;
6806}
6807
6809inline std::string file_write_date(const std::filesystem::path& path) {
6810 std::error_code ec;
6811 const auto written = std::filesystem::last_write_time(path, ec);
6812 if (ec) {
6813 return {};
6814 }
6815 const auto system_time = std::chrono::time_point_cast<std::chrono::system_clock::duration>(
6816 written - std::filesystem::file_time_type::clock::now() + std::chrono::system_clock::now());
6817 return local_date(std::chrono::system_clock::to_time_t(system_time));
6818}
6819
6821inline std::filesystem::path suffixed_path(const std::filesystem::path& base, const std::string& suffix) {
6822 return base.parent_path() / (base.stem().string() + "_" + suffix + base.extension().string());
6823}
6824
6826inline std::filesystem::path dated_indexed_path(const std::filesystem::path& base, const std::string& date,
6827 size_t index) {
6828 char number[24];
6829 std::snprintf(number, sizeof(number), "%03zu", index);
6830 return suffixed_path(base, date + "_" + number);
6831}
6832
6834inline void move_file(const std::filesystem::path& from, const std::filesystem::path& to) {
6835 std::error_code ec;
6836 std::filesystem::rename(from, to, ec);
6837 if (ec) {
6838 std::filesystem::copy_file(from, to, ec);
6839 if (!ec) {
6840 std::filesystem::remove(from, ec);
6841 }
6842 }
6843}
6844
6847inline void shift_rotated_files(const std::filesystem::path& base, size_t max_files) {
6848 const auto rotated = [&](size_t index) { return suffixed_path(base, std::to_string(index)); };
6849 std::error_code ec;
6850 std::filesystem::remove(rotated(max_files - 1), ec);
6851 for (size_t i = max_files - 1; i > 0; --i) {
6852 const auto from = i == 1 ? base : rotated(i - 1);
6853 if (std::filesystem::exists(from, ec)) {
6854 move_file(from, rotated(i));
6855 }
6856 }
6857}
6858
6861inline void shift_dated_files(const std::filesystem::path& base, const std::string& date, size_t max_files) {
6862 const auto dated = suffixed_path(base, date);
6863 std::error_code ec;
6864 if (max_files == 1) {
6865 std::filesystem::remove(dated, ec); // only the dated file is kept, so the new one replaces it
6866 return;
6867 }
6868 if (max_files == 0) {
6869 return;
6870 }
6871 std::filesystem::remove(dated_indexed_path(base, date, max_files - 1), ec);
6872 for (size_t i = max_files - 1; i >= 2; --i) {
6873 const auto from = dated_indexed_path(base, date, i - 1);
6874 if (std::filesystem::exists(from, ec)) {
6875 move_file(from, dated_indexed_path(base, date, i));
6876 }
6877 }
6878 if (std::filesystem::exists(dated, ec)) {
6879 move_file(dated, dated_indexed_path(base, date, 1));
6880 }
6881}
6882
6886inline void retire_daily_file(const std::filesystem::path& base, const std::string& date, size_t max_files) {
6887 std::error_code ec;
6888 if (std::filesystem::exists(suffixed_path(base, date), ec)) {
6889 shift_dated_files(base, date, max_files);
6890 }
6891 if (std::filesystem::exists(base, ec)) {
6892 move_file(base, suffixed_path(base, date));
6893 }
6894}
6895
6898inline const std::filesystem::path& retire_stale_daily_file(const std::filesystem::path& base, size_t max_files) {
6899 const std::string written = file_write_date(base);
6900 if (!written.empty() && written != local_date(std::time(nullptr))) {
6901 retire_daily_file(base, written, max_files);
6902 }
6903 return base;
6904}

7008inline BinarySink::BinarySink(const std::filesystem::path& file_path, std::string&& name)
7009 // std::ios::binary is what keeps Windows from expanding a 0x0A byte in the
7010 // payload into CR LF, which would corrupt every record after it.
7011 : FileSinkBase(file_path, std::ios::binary | std::ios::app, std::move(name)) {
7012 // A binary sink can only write binary payloads, so broadcast text entries
7013 // would be dropped anyway. Opt out with set_dedicated(false).
7014 set_dedicated(true);
7015}
7016
7017inline void BinarySink::write(const LogEntry& entry) {
7018 if (!file_stream_) {
7019 return;
7020 }
7021 for (uint8_t i = 0; i < entry.arg_count; ++i) {
7022 const LogArgument& arg = entry.args[i];
7023 if (arg.type != ArgType::BLOB) {
7024 continue;
7025 }
7026 const auto payload = view_binary(arg.value.dynamic_str);
7027 if (!payload.empty()) {
7028 write_payload(payload.data(), payload.size());
7029 }
7030 }
7031}
7032
7033inline void BinarySink::write_payload(const std::byte* data, size_t size) {
7034 file_stream_.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(data), static_cast<std::streamsize>(size));
7035 bytes_written_.fetch_add(size, std::memory_order_relaxed);
7036}

7038namespace detail {
7039
7040inline uint64_t text_table::hash(std::string_view text) noexcept {
7041 uint64_t h = 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ull ^ text.size();
7042 const char* p = text.data();
7043 size_t n = text.size();
7044 for (; n >= 8; p += 8, n -= 8) {
7045 uint64_t word;
7046 std::memcpy(&word, p, 8);
7047 h = (h ^ word) * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9ull;
7048 h ^= h >> 29;
7049 }
7050 if (n != 0) {
7051 uint64_t tail = 0;
7052 std::memcpy(&tail, p, n);
7053 h = (h ^ tail) * 0x94D049BB133111EBull;
7054 }
7055 return h ^ (h >> 32);
7056}
7057
7058SLICK_LOGGER_NOINLINE inline uint32_t text_table::intern_slow(const char* data, size_t size, hint& h, bool& added) {
7059 const std::string_view text{data, size};
7060 added = false;
7061 const uint64_t key = hash(text);
7062 if (!slots_.empty()) {
7063 const size_t mask = slots_.size() - 1;
7064 for (size_t i = key & mask; slots_[i].id != 0; i = (i + 1) & mask) {
7065 const slot& s = slots_[i];
7066 if (s.hash == key && s.size == text.size() && same(s.copy, text)) {
7067 h = {text.data(), s.copy, s.size, s.id};
7068 return s.id;
7069 }
7070 }
7071 }
7072 if (used_ + text.size() + kOverheadPerText > limit_) {
7073 return 0; // full: inline
7074 }
7075 if ((count_ + 1) * 2 > slots_.size()) {
7076 std::vector<slot> old(std::max<size_t>(slots_.size() * 2, 256));
7077 old.swap(slots_);
7078 for (const slot& s : old) {
7079 if (s.id != 0) {
7080 insert(s);
7081 }
7082 }
7083 }
7084 const slot s{key, store(text), static_cast<uint32_t>(text.size()), next_id_++};
7085 insert(s);
7086 ++count_;
7087 used_ += text.size() + kOverheadPerText;
7088 h = {text.data(), s.copy, s.size, s.id};
7089 added = true;
7090 return s.id;
7091}
7092
7093inline const char* text_table::store(std::string_view text) {
7094 if (text.size() > block_left_) {
7095 const size_t size = std::max(text.size(), kBlockSize);
7096 blocks_.push_back(std::make_unique_for_overwrite<char[]>(size));
7097 block_at_ = blocks_.back().get();
7098 block_left_ = size;
7099 }
7100 char* const copy = block_at_;
7101 if (!text.empty()) {
7102 std::memcpy(copy, text.data(), text.size());
7103 }
7104 block_at_ += text.size();
7105 block_left_ -= text.size();
7106 return copy;
7107}
7108
7109inline void text_table::insert(const slot& s) noexcept {
7110 const size_t mask = slots_.size() - 1;
7111 size_t i = s.hash & mask;
7112 while (slots_[i].id != 0) {
7113 i = (i + 1) & mask;
7114 }
7115 slots_[i] = s;
7116}
7117
7119struct record_cursor {
7120 char* at;
7121
7122 template<typename T>
7123 SLICK_LOGGER_FORCE_INLINE void put(T value) noexcept {
7124 std::memcpy(at, &value, sizeof(T));
7125 at += sizeof(T);
7126 }
7127 SLICK_LOGGER_FORCE_INLINE void put_bytes(const char* data, size_t size) noexcept {
7128 if (size != 0) {
7129 std::memcpy(at, data, size);
7130 }
7131 at += size;
7132 }
7133};
7134
7136inline std::string_view encoded_text_arg(const LogArgument& arg) noexcept {
7137 if (arg.type == ArgType::STRING_LITERAL) {
7138 const char* const text = arg.value.literal_ptr;
7139 return text ? std::string_view{text} : std::string_view{};
7140 }
7141 if (arg.type == ArgType::STRING_DYNAMIC) {
7142 return view_string_ref(arg.value.dynamic_str);
7143 }
7144 if (arg.type == ArgType::BLOB) {
7145 const auto bytes = view_binary(arg.value.dynamic_str);
7146 return {reinterpret_cast<const char*>(bytes.data()), bytes.size()};
7147 }
7148 return {};
7149}
7150
7151} // namespace detail

7153inline EncodedFileSink::EncodedFileSink(const std::filesystem::path& file_path, std::string&& name)
7154 // Binary, or Windows would expand every 0x0A byte into CR LF.
7155 : FileSinkBase(file_path, std::ios::binary | std::ios::app, std::move(name)),
7156 file_bytes_(detail::existing_file_size(file_path)) {
7157 write_header();
7158}
7159
7160inline void EncodedFileSink::write_header() {
7161 detail::record_cursor out{reserve(detail::kEncodedHeaderSize)};
7162 out.put(detail::kEncodedHeader);
7163 out.put_bytes(detail::kEncodedMagic, sizeof(detail::kEncodedMagic));
7164 out.put(detail::kEncodedVersion);
7165 out.put(uint16_t{0});
7166 out.put(detail::kEncodedByteOrder);
7167 used_ = static_cast<size_t>(out.at - buffer_.data());
7168}
7169
7170inline EncodedFileSink::~EncodedFileSink() {
7171 drain();
7172}
7173
7174inline void EncodedFileSink::flush() {
7175 drain();
7176 FileSinkBase::flush();
7177}
7178
7179SLICK_LOGGER_NOINLINE inline void EncodedFileSink::drain() {
7180 if (used_ != 0) {
7181 // A failed stream drops the batch, as FileSinkBase::write_cached() does.
7182 file_stream_.write(buffer_.data(), static_cast<std::streamsize>(used_));
7183 file_bytes_ += used_;
7184 used_ = 0;
7185 }
7186}
7187
7188SLICK_LOGGER_NOINLINE inline void EncodedFileSink::grow(size_t size) {
7189 // A full cache and the record that crosses it, zero-filled once.
7190 buffer_.resize(std::max({buffer_.size() * 2, used_ + size, write_cache_size_ + 4096}));
7191}
7192
7193SLICK_LOGGER_NOINLINE inline void EncodedFileSink::write_text(uint32_t id, const char* data, size_t size) {
7194 detail::record_cursor out{reserve(1 + 4 + 4 + size)};
7195 out.put(detail::kEncodedText);
7196 out.put(id);
7197 out.put(static_cast<uint32_t>(size));
7198 out.put_bytes(data, size);
7199 used_ = static_cast<size_t>(out.at - buffer_.data());
7200}
7201
7202inline void EncodedFileSink::write(const LogEntry& entry) {
7203 // No check of the stream here: a failed one drops the buffer in drain(), and
7204 // reaching its state through ofstream's virtual base costs every entry.
7205 // Texts first: an entry refers only to ids defined ahead of it.
7206 const std::string_view format = view_string_ref(entry.format);
7207 const uint32_t format_id = text_id(format);
7208 const bool located = has_source_location(entry);
7209 const std::string_view file = located ? view_string_ref(entry.file) : std::string_view{};
7210 const uint32_t file_id = located ? text_id(file) : 0;
7211 // Local mode has no tag: skip the scan when its first byte says so.
7212 const size_t tag_size = entry.tag[0] != '\0' ? detail::tag_length(entry.tag) : 0;
7213 const uint32_t pid = entry.pid;
7214 const bool process = pid != 0 || tag_size != 0;
7215 const uint8_t arg_count = std::min<uint8_t>(entry.arg_count, SLICK_LOGGER_MAX_ARGS);
7216
7217 // The most the entry takes: per argument its type and 8 bytes (a scalar is
7218 // copied whole and trimmed to its size), plus a string's bytes. The sizes
7219 // are summed, not kept: a local array costs MSVC a stack cookie check.
7220 size_t bound = 1 + 3 + 8 + 4 + 4 + (format_id ? 0 : 4 + format.size()) +
7221 (located ? 8 + (file_id ? 0 : 4 + file.size()) : 0) + (process ? 5 + tag_size : 0) +
7222 size_t{arg_count} * (1 + 8);
7223 for (uint8_t i = 0; i < arg_count; ++i) {
7224 const LogArgument& arg = entry.args[i];
7225 if (detail::encoded_arg_bytes(arg.type) == 0) {
7226 bound += detail::encoded_text_arg(arg).size(); // its u32 size is inside the 8 counted
7227 }
7228 }
7229
7230 detail::record_cursor out{reserve(bound)};
7231 out.put(detail::kEncodedEntry);
7232 out.put(static_cast<uint8_t>(entry.level));
7233 out.put(static_cast<uint8_t>((located ? detail::kEncodedLocated : 0) | (process ? detail::kEncodedProcess : 0)));
7234 out.put(arg_count);
7235 out.put(entry.timestamp);
7236 out.put(entry.thread_id);
7237 const auto put_text = [&](uint32_t id, std::string_view text) {
7238 out.put(id);
7239 if (id == 0) {
7240 out.put(static_cast<uint32_t>(text.size()));
7241 out.put_bytes(text.data(), text.size());
7242 }
7243 };
7244 put_text(format_id, format);
7245 if (located) {
7246 put_text(file_id, file);
7247 out.put(entry.line);
7248 }
7249 if (process) {
7250 out.put(pid);
7251 out.put(static_cast<uint8_t>(tag_size));
7252 out.put_bytes(entry.tag, tag_size);
7253 }
7254 for (uint8_t i = 0; i < arg_count; ++i) {
7255 const LogArgument& arg = entry.args[i];
7256 out.put(static_cast<uint8_t>(arg.type));
7257 if (const uint8_t bytes = detail::encoded_arg_bytes(arg.type)) [[likely]] {
7258 std::memcpy(out.at, &arg.value, 8); // one move whatever the size
7259 out.at += bytes;
7260 continue;
7261 }
7262 if (arg.type == ArgType::WCHAR) { // 2 bytes on Windows, 4 elsewhere
7263 out.put(static_cast<uint32_t>(arg.value.wc));
7264 } else if (arg.type == ArgType::PTR) {
7265 out.put(static_cast<uint64_t>(reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(arg.value.ptr)));
7266 } else {
7267 const std::string_view text = detail::encoded_text_arg(arg);
7268 out.put(static_cast<uint32_t>(text.size()));
7269 out.put_bytes(text.data(), text.size());
7270 }
7271 }
7272 used_ = static_cast<size_t>(out.at - buffer_.data());
7273 if (used_ >= write_cache_size_) {
7274 drain();
7275 }
7276}
7277
7278inline RotatingEncodedFileSink::RotatingEncodedFileSink(const std::filesystem::path& base_path,
7279 const RotationConfig& config, std::string&& name)
7280 : EncodedFileSink(base_path, std::move(name)), config_(config) {}
7281
7282inline void RotatingEncodedFileSink::write(const LogEntry& entry) {
7283 if (file_size() >= config_.max_file_size) [[unlikely]] {
7284 restart_file([this] { detail::shift_rotated_files(file_path_, config_.max_files); });
7285 }
7286 EncodedFileSink::write(entry);
7287}
7288
7289// Retire a file left from an earlier date before the base class opens the
7290// path, so the sink always starts on today's file.
7291inline DailyEncodedFileSink::DailyEncodedFileSink(const std::filesystem::path& base_path,
7292 const RotationConfig& config, std::string&& name)
7293 : EncodedFileSink(detail::retire_stale_daily_file(base_path, config.max_files), std::move(name)),
7294 config_(config) {
7295 start_date(static_cast<uint64_t>(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(
7296 std::chrono::system_clock::now().time_since_epoch())
7297 .count()));
7298}
7299
7300inline void DailyEncodedFileSink::start_date(uint64_t timestamp) {
7301 const auto seconds = static_cast<time_t>(timestamp / 1'000'000'000);
7302 date_ = detail::local_date(seconds);
7303 std::tm tm;
7304 if (date_.empty() || !detail::to_local_tm(seconds, tm)) {
7305 date_ = "1970-01-01";
7306 next_day_ = UINT64_MAX; // date unknown, so never switch files
7307 return;
7308 }
7309 tm.tm_mday += 1; // mktime() normalizes this to the next local midnight, DST included
7310 tm.tm_hour = 0;
7311 tm.tm_min = 0;
7312 tm.tm_sec = 0;
7313 tm.tm_isdst = -1;
7314 const time_t next = std::mktime(&tm);
7315 next_day_ = next < 0 ? UINT64_MAX : static_cast<uint64_t>(next) * 1'000'000'000;
7316}
7317
7318inline void DailyEncodedFileSink::write(const LogEntry& entry) {
7319 const uint64_t timestamp = entry.timestamp;
7320 if (timestamp >= next_day_ || (config_.max_file_size && file_size() >= config_.max_file_size)) [[unlikely]] {
7321 rotate(timestamp);
7322 }
7323 EncodedFileSink::write(entry);
7324}
7325
7326inline void DailyEncodedFileSink::rotate(uint64_t timestamp) {
7327 // Like DailyFileSink, retire the file under the date it was written on.
7328 restart_file([this] { detail::retire_daily_file(file_path_, date_, config_.max_files); });
7329 if (timestamp >= next_day_) {
7330 start_date(timestamp);
7331 }
7332}
