7334inline EncodedLogReader::EncodedLogReader(const std::filesystem::path& path)
7335 : file_(path, std::ios::binary), buffer_(size_t{1} << 20) {
7336 if (!file_) {
7337 throw std::runtime_error("Failed to open encoded log: " + path.string());
7338 }
7339 char kind = 0;
7340 if (!read(kind)) {
7341 return; // empty: no entries
7342 }
7343 if (kind != detail::kEncodedHeader || !read_header()) {
7344 throw std::runtime_error(path.string() + ": " +
7345 (error_.empty() ? std::string("not a file written by EncodedFileSink") : error_));
7346 }
7347}
7348
7349inline bool EncodedLogReader::fill(size_t size) {
7350 if (end_ - pos_ >= size) [[likely]] {
7351 return true;
7352 }
7353 std::memmove(buffer_.data(), buffer_.data() + pos_, end_ - pos_);
7354 end_ -= pos_;
7355 pos_ = 0;
7356 if (buffer_.size() < size) {
7357 buffer_.resize(std::max(size, buffer_.size() * 2));
7358 }
7359 while (end_ < size && file_) {
7360 file_.read(buffer_.data() + end_, static_cast<std::streamsize>(buffer_.size() - end_));
7361 end_ += static_cast<size_t>(file_.gcount());
7362 }
7363 return end_ >= size;
7364}
7365
7366template<typename T>
7367inline bool EncodedLogReader::read(T& value) {
7368 if (!fill(sizeof(T))) {
7369 return false;
7370 }
7371 std::memcpy(&value, buffer_.data() + pos_, sizeof(T));
7372 pos_ += sizeof(T);
7373 consumed_ += sizeof(T);
7374 return true;
7375}
7376
7377inline bool EncodedLogReader::read_text(std::string& out) {
7378 static constexpr uint32_t kMaxText = uint32_t{1} << 26; // past this the file is corrupt
7379 uint32_t size = 0;
7380 if (!read(size)) {
7381 return false;
7382 }
7383 if (size > kMaxText) {
7384 return fail("a text of " + std::to_string(size) + " bytes at offset " + std::to_string(consumed_ - 4));
7385 }
7386 if (!fill(size)) {
7387 return false;
7388 }
7389 out.append(buffer_.data() + pos_, size);
7390 pos_ += size;
7391 consumed_ += size;
7392 return true;
7393}
7394
7395inline bool EncodedLogReader::fail(std::string why) {
7396 if (error_.empty()) {
7397 error_ = std::move(why);
7398 }
7399 return false;
7400}
7401
7402inline bool EncodedLogReader::read_header() {
7403 char magic[sizeof(detail::kEncodedMagic)];
7404 uint16_t version = 0;
7405 uint16_t reserved = 0;
7406 uint32_t byte_order = 0;
7407 if (!read(magic) || !read(version) || !read(reserved) || !read(byte_order)) {
7408 return false;
7409 }
7410 if (std::memcmp(magic, detail::kEncodedMagic, sizeof(magic)) != 0) {
7411 return fail("not a file written by EncodedFileSink");
7412 }
7413 if (byte_order != detail::kEncodedByteOrder) {
7414 return fail("written on a machine of the other byte order");
7415 }
7416 if (version == 0 || version > detail::kEncodedVersion) {
7417 return fail("format version " + std::to_string(version) + ", this build reads up to " +
7418 std::to_string(detail::kEncodedVersion));
7419 }
7420 texts_.clear(); // a new session numbers its texts from 1 again
7421 return true;
7422}
7423
7424inline bool EncodedLogReader::read_definition() {
7425 uint32_t id = 0;
7426 if (!read(id)) {
7427 return false;
7428 }
7429 if (id != texts_.size() + 1) {
7430 return fail("text " + std::to_string(id) + " out of order at offset " + std::to_string(consumed_ - 4));
7431 }
7432 texts_.emplace_back();
7433 return read_text(texts_.back());
7434}
7435
7436inline bool EncodedLogReader::read_entry() {
7437 uint8_t level = 0;
7438 uint8_t bits = 0;
7439 uint8_t arg_count = 0;
7440 uint64_t timestamp = 0;
7441 uint32_t thread_id = 0;
7442 if (!read(level) || !read(bits) || !read(arg_count) || !read(timestamp) || !read(thread_id)) {
7443 return false;
7444 }
7445 if (level >= static_cast<uint8_t>(LogLevel::L_OFF)) {
7446 return fail("an entry at level " + std::to_string(level));
7447 }
7448 if (arg_count > SLICK_LOGGER_MAX_ARGS) {
7449 return fail("an entry with " + std::to_string(arg_count) + " arguments, past SLICK_LOGGER_MAX_ARGS (" +
7450 std::to_string(SLICK_LOGGER_MAX_ARGS) + ") in this build");
7451 }
7452 LogEntry& e = entry_;
7453 e = LogEntry{};
7454 e.timestamp = timestamp;
7455 e.thread_id = thread_id;
7456 e.level = static_cast<LogLevel>(level);
7457 e.arg_count = arg_count;
7458
7459 // Inline texts and arguments go to strings_, which may move as it grows,
7460 // so their addresses are set once the whole entry is in.
7461 struct pending {
7462 int target; // -2 format, -1 file, else the argument
7463 size_t offset;
7464 uint32_t size;
7465 };
7466 pending pendings[SLICK_LOGGER_MAX_ARGS + 2];
7467 size_t pending_count = 0;
7468 strings_.clear();
7469 const auto read_inline = [&](int target) {
7470 const size_t offset = strings_.size();
7471 if (!read_text(strings_)) {
7472 return false;
7473 }
7474 pendings[pending_count++] = {target, offset, static_cast<uint32_t>(strings_.size() - offset)};
7475 strings_.push_back('\0'); // a literal is read up to its NUL
7476 return true;
7477 };
7478 const auto read_ref = [&](StringRef& ref, int target, bool& interned) {
7479 uint32_t id = 0;
7480 if (!read(id)) {
7481 return false;
7482 }
7483 interned = id != 0;
7484 if (id == 0) {
7485 return read_inline(target);
7486 }
7487 if (id > texts_.size()) {
7488 return fail("an unknown text " + std::to_string(id) + " at offset " + std::to_string(consumed_ - 4));
7489 }
7490 const std::string& text = texts_[id - 1];
7491 ref = StringRef{text.c_str(), static_cast<uint32_t>(text.size())};
7492 return true;
7493 };
7494
7495 bool interned = false;
7496 if (!read_ref(e.format, -2, interned)) {
7497 return false;
7498 }
7499 if (interned) {
7500 // Fixed while this reader lives, so its parse can be kept: see message_formats.
7501 e.flags |= kEntryStaticFormat;
7502 }
7503 if (bits & detail::kEncodedLocated) {
7504 bool unused = false;
7505 uint32_t line = 0;
7506 if (!read_ref(e.file, -1, unused) || !read(line)) {
7507 return false;
7508 }
7509 e.line = line;
7510 e.flags |= kEntryHasSourceLocation;
7511 }
7512 if (bits & detail::kEncodedProcess) {
7513 uint32_t pid = 0;
7514 uint8_t tag_size = 0;
7515 if (!read(pid) || !read(tag_size)) {
7516 return false;
7517 }
7518 if (tag_size > SLICK_LOGGER_TAG_SIZE) {
7519 return fail("a process tag of " + std::to_string(tag_size) + " bytes");
7520 }
7521 if (!fill(tag_size)) {
7522 return false;
7523 }
7524 std::memcpy(e.tag, buffer_.data() + pos_, tag_size);
7525 pos_ += tag_size;
7526 consumed_ += tag_size;
7527 e.pid = pid;
7528 }
7529 for (uint8_t i = 0; i < arg_count; ++i) {
7530 uint8_t type = 0;
7531 if (!read(type)) {
7532 return false;
7533 }
7534 if (type > static_cast<uint8_t>(ArgType::BLOB)) {
7535 return fail("an argument of unknown type " + std::to_string(type));
7536 }
7537 LogArgument& arg = e.args[i];
7538 arg.type = static_cast<ArgType>(type);
7539 if (const uint8_t size = detail::encoded_arg_bytes(arg.type)) {
7540 if (!fill(size)) {
7541 return false;
7542 }
7543 std::memcpy(reinterpret_cast<char*>(&arg.value), buffer_.data() + pos_, size);
7544 pos_ += size;
7545 consumed_ += size;
7546 continue;
7547 }
7548 switch (arg.type) {
7549 case ArgType::WCHAR: {
7550 uint32_t wc = 0;
7551 if (!read(wc)) {
7552 return false;
7553 }
7554 arg.value.wc = static_cast<wchar_t>(wc);
7555 continue;
7556 }
7557 case ArgType::PTR: {
7558 uint64_t ptr = 0;
7559 if (!read(ptr)) {
7560 return false;
7561 }
7562 arg.value.ptr = reinterpret_cast<void*>(static_cast<uintptr_t>(ptr));
7563 continue;
7564 }
7565 default: // STRING_LITERAL, STRING_DYNAMIC, BLOB
7566 if (!read_inline(i)) {
7567 return false;
7568 }
7569 continue;
7570 }
7571 }
7572 for (size_t i = 0; i < pending_count; ++i) {
7573 const pending& p = pendings[i];
7574 const StringRef ref{strings_.data() + p.offset, p.size};
7575 if (p.target == -2) {
7576 e.format = ref;
7577 } else if (p.target == -1) {
7578 e.file = ref;
7579 } else if (e.args[p.target].type == ArgType::STRING_LITERAL) {
7580 e.args[p.target].value.literal_ptr = ref.ptr;
7581 } else {
7582 e.args[p.target].value.dynamic_str = ref;
7583 }
7584 }
7585 return true;
7586}
7587
7588inline const LogEntry* EncodedLogReader::next() {
7589 while (error_.empty()) {
7590 const uint64_t start = consumed_;
7591 char kind = 0;
7592 if (!read(kind)) {
7593 return nullptr; // the end, between records
7594 }
7595 bool complete = false;
7596 if (kind == detail::kEncodedEntry) {
7597 if (read_entry()) {
7598 return &entry_;
7599 }
7600 } else if (kind == detail::kEncodedText) {
7601 complete = read_definition();
7602 } else if (kind == detail::kEncodedHeader) {
7603 complete = read_header();
7604 } else {
7605 fail("an unknown record at offset " + std::to_string(start));
7606 }
7607 if (!complete) {
7608 fail("the record at offset " + std::to_string(start) + " is cut short");
7609 }
7610 }
7611 return nullptr;
7612}
7613
7614inline Logger& Logger::instance() {
7615 return *override_instance_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
7616}
7617
7618inline Logger Logger::instance_;
7619inline std::atomic<Logger*> Logger::override_instance_{&Logger::instance_};
7620
7621inline void Logger::set_instance(Logger* logger) noexcept {
7622 override_instance_.store(logger, std::memory_order_release);
7623}
7624
7625inline void Logger::clear_instance_override() noexcept {
7626 override_instance_.store(&instance_, std::memory_order_release);
7627}
7628
7629inline LogStats Logger::stats_snapshot() const noexcept {
7630 const std::shared_ptr<const LogStats> latest =
7631 stats_latest_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
7632 return latest ? *latest : LogStats{};
7633}
7634
7635inline void Logger::publish_stats(const LogStats& stats) noexcept {
7636 // Each report publishes a fresh, immutable LogStats and swaps the pointer, so
7637 // a reader is never looking at storage the statistics thread is writing.
7638 //
7639 // A seqlock over a shared LogStats would be cheaper, but by the letter of the
7640 // memory model it is a data race: the reader copies the payload while the
7641 // writer assigns it, and only afterwards learns the generation moved. That is
7642 // undefined behavior no fence can repair. One allocation per reporting
7643 // interval (once a second by default), off the logging path, is a small
7644 // price for a snapshot with no race at all.
7645 try {
7646 stats_latest_.store(std::make_shared<const LogStats>(stats),
7647 std::memory_order_release);
7648 } catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
7649 // Keep the previous snapshot rather than terminating a background thread.
7650 }
7651}
7652
7653inline void Logger::accumulate_stats_sample() noexcept {
7654 if (!log_queue_) {
7655 return;
7656 }
7657 // Consumed first: the two loads are not atomic together, and loading the
7658 // producer cursor second makes it the fresher of the pair, so the common case
7659 // needs no clamp. The clamp below still covers the reverse ordering.
7660 uint64_t consumed = read_index_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
7661 uint64_t produced = log_queue_->initial_reading_index();
7662 if (thread_rings_ || registry_) {
7663 const ring_totals rings = thread_ring_totals();
7664 consumed += rings.consumed;
7665 produced += rings.produced;
7666 }
7667 const uint64_t depth = produced > consumed ? produced - consumed : 0;
7668
7669 if (depth > stats_depth_max_) {
7670 stats_depth_max_ = depth;
7671 }
7672 stats_depth_sum_ += depth;
7673 ++stats_sample_count_;
7674
7675 // The string ring is a gauge too, and is invisible to a once-per-report read
7676 // for the same reason the depth is: by the time a report lands, the burst
7677 // that backed the ring up has usually drained. Sampling it costs three
7678 // relaxed loads (the writer's read cursor and the two ring cursors), so it is
7679 // cheap enough to run on the tick.
7680 if (mode_ == QueueMode::SharedProducer) {
7681 return; // no local reader, so there is no frontier to measure against
7682 }
7683 LogStats probe;
7684 if (sample_string_occupancy(probe)) {
7685 stats_string_seen_ = true;
7686 stats_string_last_ = probe.string_inflight_bytes;
7687 if (probe.string_inflight_bytes > stats_string_inflight_max_) {
7688 stats_string_inflight_max_ = probe.string_inflight_bytes;
7689 }
7690 }
7691}
7692
7693inline void Logger::advance_string_frontier() noexcept {
7694 // Called by the writer once per drained batch, with the batch already
7695 // dispatched. Implements the cursor-pair rule described at
7696 // stats_string_frontier_: hold one (entry cursor, string cursor) snapshot and
7697 // promote the string half only once the read cursor has passed the entry half.
7698 if (!stats_gen_open_) {
7699 // The read order is the proof. R is read first: every entry with a slot
7700 // below R had already taken that slot, and a producer reserves its string
7701 // before it takes a slot, so every one of those strings was reserved
7702 // before R was read, and therefore before S, which is read after it. So
7703 // "all slots below R drained" means "everything below S consumed".
7704 // Reading S first would let a slot below R reserve a string above S in
7705 // between, and the promotion would free bytes still in use.
7706 stats_gen_entry_ = log_queue_->initial_reading_index();
7707 stats_gen_string_ = string_queue_->initial_reading_index();
7708 // A thread ring's record holding strings below S raised its ring's mark
7709 // and the epoch before reserving them, then fenced: with S read, this
7710 // fence makes both visible. The marks are scanned only when it moved.
7711 std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_acquire);
7712 const uint64_t epoch = string_epoch_->load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
7713 if (epoch != stats_seen_epoch_) {
7714 try {
7715 if (remote_) {
7716 attach_new_producers(); // the mark may be a producer's not attached yet
7717 }
7718 stats_gen_rings_.clear();
7719 const auto note = [this](const detail::producer_ring* ring) {
7720 const uint64_t end = ring->shared_strings_end();
7721 if (end > ring->released()) {
7722 stats_gen_rings_.emplace_back(ring, end);
7723 }
7724 };
7725 const uint32_t used = ring_slots_used_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
7726 for (uint32_t i = 0; i < used; ++i) {
7727 if (const detail::producer_ring* ring = ring_slots_[i].ring.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
7728 note(ring);
7729 }
7730 }
7731 for (const detail::ring_view* view : remote_views_) {
7732 note(view->ring);
7733 }
7734 stats_seen_epoch_ = epoch;
7735 } catch (...) {
7736 return; // no snapshot, so the frontier holds: the safe direction
7737 }
7738 }
7739 stats_gen_open_ = true;
7740 }
7741 // Noted rings the writer has drained past their mark. A producer may lower a
7742 // mark it overestimated, so the current one counts too.
7743 while (!stats_gen_rings_.empty()) {
7744 const auto& [ring, end] = stats_gen_rings_.back();
7745 if (ring->released() < std::min(end, ring->shared_strings_end())) {
7746 break;
7747 }
7748 stats_gen_rings_.pop_back();
7749 }
7750 // read_index_ is this thread's own cursor, already advanced past the batch
7751 // just written, so a relaxed load sees the writer's own last store.
7752 if (stats_gen_rings_.empty() && read_index_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) >= stats_gen_entry_) {
7753 stats_string_frontier_.store(stats_gen_string_, std::memory_order_relaxed);
7754 stats_gen_open_ = false;
7755 }
7756}
7757
7758inline bool Logger::sample_string_occupancy(LogStats& stats) noexcept {
7759 if (!log_queue_ || !string_queue_) {
7760 return false;
7761 }
7762 const uint64_t capacity = string_queue_->size();
7763 if (capacity == 0) {
7764 return false;
7765 }
7766
7767 // The entry ring's reservation cursor is not a publication boundary: a producer
7768 // reserves a slot, then fills it, then publishes. Reading a slot off that
7769 // cursor would race the fill and yield torn data, so the statistics thread
7770 // never touches the entry ring directly. The writer thread instead publishes
7771 // the frontier below, taken from an entry read() has already handed it.
7772 const auto rings_drained = [this]() noexcept {
7773 if (registry_) {
7774 // A collector cannot see a producer it has not attached, and its ring
7775 // totals are a scan old: only its frontier knows. See advance_string_frontier().
7776 return false;
7777 }
7778 if (!thread_rings_) {
7779 return true;
7780 }
7781 const ring_totals rings = thread_ring_totals(); // a ring record may hold strings here too
7782 return rings.consumed >= rings.produced;
7783 };
7784 if (read_index_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) >= log_queue_->initial_reading_index() && rings_drained()) {
7785 // Nothing outstanding, so nothing in the string ring is still needed.
7786 // This zero is a measurement, and reporting it as invalid would hide the
7787 // healthiest state the pipeline has.
7788 stats.string_inflight_bytes = 0;
7789 stats.string_pct = 0.0;
7790 stats.string_pct_valid = true;
7791 return true;
7792 }
7793
7794 // Everything from the frontier to the write cursor is still outstanding. The
7795 // frontier starts life at the ring cursor start() saw, so there is always a
7796 // floor to measure from: before the writer has confirmed a single drain,
7797 // nothing has been consumed, and the whole span since start is in flight.
7798 // Reporting it as unknown would blank the row exactly while a startup burst
7799 // was filling the ring.
7800 const uint64_t watermark = stats_string_frontier_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
7801 const uint64_t write_cursor = string_queue_->initial_reading_index();
7802 // An absolute reserve index in both modes, so the span is a plain
7803 // subtraction. Keeping it absolute is what lets an exactly full ring read as
7804 // capacity instead of aliasing to zero, and makes an overrun visible as a
7805 // distance past capacity rather than silently folding back into range.
7806 uint64_t behind = write_cursor > watermark ? write_cursor - watermark : 0;
7807 if (behind > capacity) {
7808 behind = capacity;
7809 }
7810
7811 stats.string_inflight_bytes = behind;
7812 stats.string_pct = std::min(
7813 100.0, static_cast<double>(behind) * 100.0 / static_cast<double>(capacity));
7814 stats.string_pct_valid = true;
7815 return true;
7816}
7817inline LogStats Logger::sample_stats() noexcept {
7818 LogStats stats;
7819 // The entries' own clock, so a sample lines up with the lines it describes.
7820 stats.timestamp_ns = current_timestamp();
7821 stats.sample_count = stats_sample_count_;
7822
7823 if (!log_queue_ || !string_queue_) {
7824 return stats;
7825 }
7826
7827 uint64_t consumed = read_index_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
7828 uint64_t produced = log_queue_->initial_reading_index();
7829 ring_totals rings;
7830 if (thread_rings_ || registry_) {
7831 rings = thread_ring_totals();
7832 consumed += rings.consumed;
7833 produced += rings.produced;
7834 }
7835 stats.thread_ring_count = rings.rings;
7836 const uint64_t depth = produced > consumed ? produced - consumed : 0;
7837 const uint64_t entry_capacity = log_queue_->size();
7838 // A shared-memory producer has no writer thread, so read_index_ never advances
7839 // and anything derived from it would be meaningless. Report those as zero, the
7840 // same reasoning flush() uses to return early in that mode.
7841 const bool has_reader = (mode_ != QueueMode::SharedProducer);
7842
7843 stats.entries_produced = produced;
7844 stats.entries_consumed = has_reader ? consumed : 0;
7845 stats.entry_queue_depth = has_reader ? depth : 0;
7846 // The report-time reading is a sample too, and is taken after the last tick,
7847 // so fold it in. Otherwise the "peak" could come out below the value in the
7848 // same row.
7849 stats.entry_queue_depth_max = has_reader ? std::max(stats_depth_max_, depth) : 0;
7850 stats.entry_queue_capacity = static_cast<uint32_t>(entry_capacity);
7851 if (has_reader && stats_sample_count_ != 0) {
7852 stats.entry_queue_depth_mean =
7853 static_cast<double>(stats_depth_sum_) / static_cast<double>(stats_sample_count_);
7854 }
7855 if (has_reader && entry_capacity != 0) {
7856 const double capacity_d = static_cast<double>(entry_capacity);
7857 stats.entry_queue_pct =
7858 std::min(100.0, static_cast<double>(depth) * 100.0 / capacity_d);
7859 stats.entry_queue_pct_max = std::min(
7860 100.0, static_cast<double>(stats.entry_queue_depth_max) * 100.0 / capacity_d);
7861 }
7862
7863 const uint64_t string_capacity = string_queue_->size();
7864 stats.string_bytes_written = string_queue_->initial_reading_index();
7865 stats.string_buffer_capacity = static_cast<uint32_t>(string_capacity);
7866 // Plus the entries the writer read but discarded as torn: they too were
7867 // overwritten before it could use them, just mid-read rather than before it.
7868 stats.entry_loss_count =
7869 log_queue_->loss_count() + torn_entry_count_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) +
7870 rings.dropped; // counted whatever kLossDetectionEnabled says: it costs the drop path only
7871 stats.string_loss_count = string_queue_->loss_count();
7872
7873 if (has_reader) {
7874 // string_pct_valid covers the whole row, point value and peak alike. A row
7875 // whose ticks never resolved a frontier reports unknown rather than a
7876 // confident zero: a zero peak would read as "no pressure" at exactly the
7877 // moment the ring might be filling unobserved.
7878 if (sample_string_occupancy(stats)) {
7879 stats_string_seen_ = true;
7880 stats_string_last_ = stats.string_inflight_bytes;
7881 } else if (stats_string_seen_) {
7882 // This read found nothing, but a tick in this interval did. Report
7883 // that rather than the previous interval's, which is staler.
7884 stats.string_inflight_bytes = stats_string_last_;
7885 stats.string_pct_valid = true;
7886 } else {
7887 // Nothing seen at all this interval; carry the last known value so a
7888 // consumer sees the previous reading rather than a spurious zero.
7889 stats.string_inflight_bytes = stats_previous_.string_inflight_bytes;
7890 stats.string_pct_valid = false;
7891 }
7892
7893 if (stats.string_pct_valid) {
7894 // The peak comes from the oversampling ticks, which catch the bursts a
7895 // single point sample misses.
7896 stats.string_inflight_bytes_max =
7897 std::max(stats_string_inflight_max_, stats.string_inflight_bytes);
7898 }
7899 if (string_capacity != 0) {
7900 const double capacity_d = static_cast<double>(string_capacity);
7901 stats.string_pct = std::min(
7902 100.0, static_cast<double>(stats.string_inflight_bytes) * 100.0 / capacity_d);
7903 stats.string_pct_max = std::min(
7904 100.0,
7905 static_cast<double>(stats.string_inflight_bytes_max) * 100.0 / capacity_d);
7906 }
7907 }
7908
7909 if (stats_has_previous_) {
7910 const double elapsed = std::chrono::duration<double>(
7911 std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - stats_last_report_).count();
7912 stats.interval_sec = elapsed;
7913 if (elapsed > 0.0) {
7914 // Deltas over the measured elapsed time, so a late wake-up shifts when
7915 // a sample lands but never distorts the rate it reports.
7916 const auto delta = [](uint64_t now_v, uint64_t then_v) noexcept -> double {
7917 return now_v > then_v ? static_cast<double>(now_v - then_v) : 0.0;
7918 };
7919 const double bytes =
7920 delta(stats.string_bytes_written, stats_previous_.string_bytes_written);
7921 stats.produced_per_sec =
7922 delta(stats.entries_produced, stats_previous_.entries_produced) / elapsed;
7923 stats.consumed_per_sec =
7924 delta(stats.entries_consumed, stats_previous_.entries_consumed) / elapsed;
7925 stats.string_bytes_per_sec = bytes / elapsed;
7926 if (string_capacity != 0) {
7927 const double capacity_d = static_cast<double>(string_capacity);
7928 stats.string_turnover_pct = bytes * 100.0 / capacity_d;
7929 stats.string_wraps_per_sec = bytes / capacity_d / elapsed;
7930 }
7931 }
7932 }
7933 return stats;
7934}
7935
7936inline void Logger::stats_thread_func() {
7937 using clock = std::chrono::steady_clock;
7938 const auto tick = std::chrono::milliseconds(stats_sample_interval_ms_);
7939 const auto report_every = std::chrono::milliseconds(stats_interval_ms_);
7940
7941 stats_last_report_ = clock::now();
7942 auto next_report = stats_last_report_ + report_every;
7943
7944 while (running_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
7945 // Sleeping one tick at a time is what keeps shutdown prompt: atomic::wait
7946 // has no timeout in C++20, and a condition variable would need a mutex the
7947 // rest of this logger does without. The tick doubles as the oversampling
7948 // rate, so shutdown latency and gauge fidelity come from one knob.
7949 std::this_thread::sleep_for(tick);
7950 if (!running_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
7951 break;
7952 }
7953 accumulate_stats_sample();
7954
7955 const auto now = clock::now();
7956 if (now < next_report) {
7957 continue;
7958 }
7959 const LogStats stats = sample_stats();
7960 publish_stats(stats);
7961 write_stats_row(stats);
7962
7963 stats_previous_ = stats;
7964 stats_has_previous_ = true;
7965 stats_last_report_ = now;
7966 stats_depth_max_ = 0;
7967 stats_depth_sum_ = 0;
7968 stats_sample_count_ = 0;
7969 stats_string_inflight_max_ = 0;
7970 stats_string_last_ = 0;
7971 stats_string_seen_ = false;
7972 // Advance from the previous boundary rather than from now, so a late tick
7973 // does not push every later report further and further out.
7974 next_report += report_every;
7975 if (next_report <= now) {
7976 next_report = now + report_every;
7977 }
7978 }
7979
7980 // A last report, so both the file and the snapshot capture the end state.
7981 accumulate_stats_sample();
7982 const LogStats final_stats = sample_stats();
7983 publish_stats(final_stats);
7984 write_stats_row(final_stats);
7985}
7986
7987inline void Logger::write_stats_header() {
7988 static constexpr std::string_view kHeader =
7989 "timestamp,interval_sec,sample_count,"
7990 "entries_produced,entries_consumed,produced_per_sec,consumed_per_sec,"
7991 "entry_queue_depth,entry_queue_depth_max,entry_queue_depth_mean,"
7992 "entry_queue_capacity,entry_queue_pct,entry_queue_pct_max,"
7993 "string_inflight_bytes,string_inflight_bytes_max,string_buffer_capacity,"
7994 "string_pct,string_pct_max,string_pct_valid,"
7995 "string_bytes_written,string_bytes_per_sec,string_turnover_pct,"
7996 "string_wraps_per_sec,entry_loss_count,string_loss_count,thread_ring_count\n";
7997 stats_stream_ << kHeader;
7998 stats_bytes_written_ = kHeader.size();
7999}
8000
8001inline void Logger::open_stats_csv() {
8002 if (stats_file_.empty()) {
8003 return; // snapshots only; nothing to write
8004 }
8005 detail::open_buffered_stream(stats_stream_, stats_stream_buffer_, stats_file_,
8006 std::ios::out | std::ios::trunc,
8007 detail::kStreamBufferSize);
8008 if (!stats_stream_) {
8009 throw std::runtime_error("Failed to open statistics file: " + stats_file_.string());
8010 }
8011 write_stats_header();
8012}
8013
8014inline void Logger::roll_stats_csv() {
8015 stats_stream_.flush();
8016 stats_stream_.close();
8017
8018 std::filesystem::path backup = stats_file_;
8019 backup.replace_extension();
8020 backup += ".1.csv";
8021
8022 std::error_code ec;
8023 std::filesystem::remove(backup, ec);
8024 std::filesystem::rename(stats_file_, backup, ec);
8025 if (ec) {
8026 // Same fallback the daily sink uses: a rename across devices fails, a
8027 // copy does not.
8028 std::filesystem::copy_file(stats_file_, backup,
8029 std::filesystem::copy_options::overwrite_existing, ec);
8030 if (!ec) {
8031 std::filesystem::remove(stats_file_, ec);
8032 }
8033 }
8034
8035 detail::open_buffered_stream(stats_stream_, stats_stream_buffer_, stats_file_,
8036 std::ios::out | std::ios::trunc,
8037 detail::kStreamBufferSize);
8038 if (stats_stream_) {
8039 write_stats_header();
8040 }
8041}
8042
8043inline void Logger::write_stats_row(const LogStats& stats) {
8044 if (stats_file_.empty() || !stats_stream_.is_open()) {
8045 return;
8046 }
8047 if (stats_max_file_size_ != 0 && stats_bytes_written_ >= stats_max_file_size_) {
8048 roll_stats_csv();
8049 if (!stats_stream_.is_open()) {
8050 return;
8051 }
8052 }
8053
8054 std::string row;
8055 row.reserve(256);
8056 TimestampFormatter{TimestampFormatter::Format::WITH_MICROSECONDS}
8057 .append_timestamp(row, stats.timestamp_ns);
8058 // No field can contain a comma, so the rows need no quoting.
8059 std::format_to(std::back_inserter(row),
8060 ",{:.6f},{},{},{},{:.3f},{:.3f},{},{},{:.2f},{},{:.2f},{:.2f},"
8061 "{},{},{},{:.2f},{:.2f},{},{},{:.3f},{:.3f},{:.3f},{},{},{}\n",
8062 stats.interval_sec, stats.sample_count,
8063 stats.entries_produced, stats.entries_consumed,
8064 stats.produced_per_sec, stats.consumed_per_sec,
8065 stats.entry_queue_depth, stats.entry_queue_depth_max,
8066 stats.entry_queue_depth_mean, stats.entry_queue_capacity,
8067 stats.entry_queue_pct, stats.entry_queue_pct_max,
8068 stats.string_inflight_bytes, stats.string_inflight_bytes_max,
8069 stats.string_buffer_capacity,
8070 stats.string_pct, stats.string_pct_max,
8071 stats.string_pct_valid ? 1 : 0,
8072 stats.string_bytes_written, stats.string_bytes_per_sec,
8073 stats.string_turnover_pct, stats.string_wraps_per_sec,
8074 stats.entry_loss_count, stats.string_loss_count, stats.thread_ring_count);
8075
8076 stats_stream_ << row;
8077 stats_stream_.flush(); // a crash is exactly when these rows matter most
8078 stats_bytes_written_ += row.size();
8079
8080 if (!stats_stream_ && !stats_write_failed_) {
8081 // Never throw here: this runs on a background thread, and a failed CSV must
8082 // not take the process down or stop stats_snapshot() from working. Say so
8083 // once rather than on every interval.
8084 stats_write_failed_ = true;
8085 std::fprintf(stderr, "SlickLogger: failed writing statistics to %s\n",
8086 stats_file_.string().c_str());
8087 }
8088}
8089
8090inline void Logger::set_source_location_options(bool enabled) noexcept {
8091 source_location_options_.store(enabled ? kSourceLocationEnabled : 0, std::memory_order_release);
8092}
8093
8094inline void Logger::init(const std::filesystem::path& log_file, size_t log_queue_size, size_t string_buffer_size) {
8095 shutdown(); // make sure the logger is stopped
8096 add_sink(std::make_shared<FileSink>(log_file));
8097
8098 // Ensure queue_size is power of 2
8099 create_local_queues(round_up_to_power_of_2(log_queue_size),
8100 round_up_to_power_of_2(string_buffer_size), kDefaultStringItemsPerSlot);
8101 log_file_ = log_file;
8102 configure_thread_rings(LogConfig{});
8103 start();
8104}
8105
8106inline void Logger::configure_thread_rings(const LogConfig& config) noexcept {
8107 const bool producer = config.mode == QueueMode::SharedProducer;
8108 thread_rings_ = config.thread_rings && (config.mode == QueueMode::Local || producer);
8109 const size_t ring_size = producer ? config.shared_thread_ring_size : config.thread_ring_size;
8110 thread_ring_size_ = std::clamp<size_t>(round_up_to_power_of_2(ring_size), 4096, size_t{1} << 30);
8111 max_thread_rings_ = producer ? std::clamp<uint32_t>(config.shared_thread_rings, 1, detail::shm_ring_segment::kMaxRings)
8112 : std::clamp<uint32_t>(config.max_thread_rings, 1, 4096);
8113 ring_poll_interval_ns_ = int64_t{config.writer_poll_interval_us} * 1000;
8114 ring_full_drops_ = config.thread_ring_full == RingFullPolicy::Drop;
8115}
8116
8117inline std::string Logger::create_thread_rings() {
8118 ring_slots_ = std::make_unique<detail::thread_ring_slot[]>(max_thread_rings_);
8119 ring_slots_used_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
8120 thread_ring_max_payload_ = static_cast<uint32_t>(std::min<size_t>(thread_ring_size_ / 2, UINT32_MAX)) -
8121 detail::producer_ring::kRecordHeader;
8122 if (mode_ != QueueMode::SharedProducer) {
8123 ring_views_ = std::make_unique<detail::ring_view[]>(max_thread_rings_);
8124 ring_fence_ = !detail::writer_barrier_available();
8125 local_rings_ = true;
8126 return {};
8127 }
8128 // A producer process: its rings are in its own segment, and it has no writer to wake.
8129 std::string why;
8130 if (!claim_registry_slot(why)) {
8131 ring_slots_.reset();
8132 thread_rings_ = false;
8133 return why;
8134 }
8135 auto* const segment = static_cast<detail::shm_ring_segment*>(ring_shm_.data());
8136 for (uint32_t i = 0; i < max_thread_rings_; ++i) {
8137 ring_slots_[i].ring.store(segment->ring(i), std::memory_order_relaxed);
8138 }
8139 ring_fence_ = false;
8140 ring_in_shm_ = true;
8141 spill_route_base_ = ((registry_generation_ & detail::kRouteGenerationMask)
8142 << (detail::kRouteSlotBits + detail::kRouteRingBits)) | registry_slot_;
8143 spill_route_shift_ = detail::kRouteSlotBits;
8144 spill_progress_ = &registry_->read_index;
8145 string_epoch_ = &registry_->string_epoch;
8146 return {};
8147}
8148
8149inline void Logger::start() {
8150 // Every init() builds fresh queues and then comes here, so the writer's view
8151 // of the entry ring starts over here too. 64 pages per ring for
8152 // entry_page_cursor_, or a page per slot in rings smaller than that: more pages
8153 // drop fewer entries early, fewer mean producers raise the cursor less often.
8154 torn_entry_count_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
8155 entry_page_cursor_.page.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
8156 const uint32_t ring_shift = static_cast<uint32_t>(std::countr_zero(log_queue_->size()));
8157 entry_page_shift_ = ring_shift > 6 ? ring_shift - 6 : 0;
8158
8159 // Before running_ and before any thread: open_stats_csv() throws on a file it
8160 // cannot create, and a throw from here must leave the logger untouched rather
8161 // than half-started with a live writer thread the failed caller never expects.
8162 if (stats_enabled_) {
8163 stats_depth_max_ = 0;
8164 stats_depth_sum_ = 0;
8165 stats_sample_count_ = 0;
8166 stats_string_inflight_max_ = 0;
8167 stats_string_last_ = 0;
8168 stats_string_seen_ = false;
8169 stats_bytes_written_ = 0;
8170 stats_has_previous_ = false;
8171 stats_write_failed_ = false;
8172 // Seeded with the ring cursor as it stands now, not with a "nothing known
8173 // yet" sentinel. Nothing this run reserves can end at or below it, so it
8174 // is a true floor, and until the first promotion it is also the exact
8175 // answer: the writer has confirmed no drain, so everything reserved since
8176 // start is still in flight. A fresh local ring starts at zero; a shared
8177 // segment starts wherever it was attached, which is why this is read
8178 // rather than assumed.
8179 stats_gen_entry_ = 0;
8180 stats_gen_string_ = 0;
8181 stats_gen_open_ = false;
8182 stats_gen_rings_.clear();
8183 stats_seen_epoch_ = UINT64_MAX;
8184 uint64_t string_floor =
8185 string_queue_ ? string_queue_->initial_reading_index() : 0;
8186 if (mode_ == QueueMode::SharedCollector && collect_backlog_) {
8187 // A collector replaying a backlog is the one case where the attach
8188 // point is not a floor. It rewinds its entry reader below that point
8189 // (see below), so the entries it is about to drain own strings that
8190 // producers reserved before it attached. The attach cursor would
8191 // declare those strings free from the first sample and report an
8192 // idle ring throughout the replay. Rewind the floor the same way the
8193 // reader is rewound, to the oldest position the ring can still hold:
8194 // anything older has been overwritten anyway, and what is left is in
8195 // flight until the replay has drained it.
8196 const uint64_t capacity = string_queue_ ? string_queue_->size() : 0;
8197 string_floor = string_floor > capacity ? string_floor - capacity : 0;
8198 }
8199 stats_string_frontier_.store(string_floor, std::memory_order_relaxed);
8200 open_stats_csv();
8201 }
8202
8203 shared_head_ready_ = false;
8204 shared_gate_ring_ = nullptr;
8205 shared_gate_view_ = nullptr;
8206 std::string ring_warning;
8207 if (thread_rings_) {
8208 ring_warning = create_thread_rings();
8209 }
8210 running_ = true;
8211
8212 // A shared-memory producer has no sinks and no writer thread: the collector
8213 // process owns both and drains the shared queue on everyone's behalf.
8214 if (mode_ != QueueMode::SharedProducer) {
8215 // Initialize read_index_ before starting the thread
8216 read_index_.store(log_queue_->initial_reading_index(), std::memory_order_relaxed);
8217 if (mode_ == QueueMode::SharedCollector && collect_backlog_) {
8218 // Producers may already have published into this segment before the
8219 // collector attached. Rewind to the oldest slot the ring can still
8220 // hold so nothing buffered is dropped; anything older than that has
8221 // been overwritten already.
8222 const uint64_t capacity = log_queue_->size();
8223 const uint64_t attached_at = read_index_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
8224 read_index_.store(attached_at > capacity ? attached_at - capacity : 0,
8225 std::memory_order_relaxed);
8226 }
8227 shared_cursor_ = read_index_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
8228 if (registry_) {
8229 publish_shared_cursor();
8230 // Producers already running: their rings are backlog too.
8231 scan_registry(true);
8232 }
8233
8234 // No wait for the thread to come up: running_ is already true, and the
8235 // queue is lock-free, so entries logged before the thread is scheduled
8236 // simply wait in the ring for it to drain them. A sleep here would not
8237 // be a handshake anyway, and on Windows it would add ~15.6ms to every
8238 // init().
8239 writer_thread_ = std::thread([this]() { writer_thread_func(); });
8240 }
8241 // init() is no hot path, and the thread calling it often logs the most: its
8242 // ring is faulted in here rather than one page at a time on later calls.
8243 prepare_thread();
8244 log(LogLevel::L_INFO, "SlickLogger v{}", SLICK_LOGGER_VERSION);
8245 if (!ring_warning.empty()) {
8246 log(LogLevel::L_WARN, "SlickLogger: no thread rings in shared memory ({}), logging through the shared rings",
8247 ring_warning);
8248 }
8249
8250 // Spawned last, so the banner above is already in the queue rather than
8251 // racing the first sample. The CSV is already open by this point.
8252 if (stats_enabled_) {
8253 stats_thread_ = std::thread([this]() { stats_thread_func(); });
8254 }
8255}
8256
8257inline void Logger::init(const LogConfig& config) {
8258 shutdown(); // make sure the logger is stopped
8259
8260 if (config.mode == QueueMode::SharedProducer) {
8261 // The collector process owns the sinks; a producer that also held sinks
8262 // would write the same entry twice and defeat the point of centralizing.
8263 if (!config.sinks.empty()) {
8264 throw std::runtime_error(
8265 "SharedProducer mode must not define sinks. The collector process owns the sinks.");
8266 }
8267 }
8268 else if (config.sinks.empty()) {
8269 throw std::runtime_error("No sink. Sinks should be added in the config.");
8270 }
8271
8272 // Before the sinks are registered, so add_sink() hands each one the default.
8273 // An empty config.pattern leaves any earlier set_pattern() alone rather than
8274 // silently clearing it.
8275 if (!config.pattern.empty()) {
8276 set_pattern(config.pattern);
8277 }
8278 // Before start(), so even its version banner carries the configured time.
8279 // Null leaves an earlier set_timestamper() alone, as with the pattern above.
8280 if (config.timestamper) {
8281 set_timestamper(config.timestamper);
8282 }
8283
8284 for (auto& sink : config.sinks) {
8285 add_sink(sink);
8286 }
8287
8288 set_level(config.min_level);
8289 set_source_location_options(config.include_source_location);
8290
8291 // Written before start() spawns the statistics thread, which is the only
8292 // reader of these afterwards, so they need no synchronization.
8293 stats_enabled_ = config.enable_stats;
8294 stats_file_ = config.stats_file;
8295 stats_interval_ms_ = std::max(1u, config.stats_interval_ms);
8296 // Oversampling faster than the reporting interval is the point; slower than it
8297 // would starve the reports, so clamp rather than honour it.
8298 stats_sample_interval_ms_ =
8299 std::clamp(config.stats_sample_interval_ms, 1u, stats_interval_ms_);
8300 stats_max_file_size_ = config.stats_max_file_size;
8301
8302 // Ensure queue_size is power of 2
8303 size_t log_queue_size = round_up_to_power_of_2(config.log_queue_size);
8304 size_t string_buffer_size = round_up_to_power_of_2(config.string_buffer_size);
8305
8306 if (config.mode == QueueMode::Local) {
8307 create_local_queues(log_queue_size, string_buffer_size, config.string_items_per_slot);
8308 }
8309 else {
8310 setup_shared_queues(config, static_cast<uint32_t>(log_queue_size),
8311 static_cast<uint32_t>(string_buffer_size),
8312 normalize_items_per_slot(config.string_items_per_slot, string_buffer_size));
8313 }
8314 configure_thread_rings(config);
8315 if (mode_ != QueueMode::Local) {
8316 try {
8317 setup_registry(config);
8318 } catch (...) {
8319 close_registry();
8320 log_queue_.reset();
8321 string_queue_.reset();
8322 mode_ = QueueMode::Local;
8323 shm_name_.clear();
8324 entry_flags_ = 0;
8325 pid_ = 0;
8326 thread_rings_ = false;
8327 throw;
8328 }
8329 }
8330 start();
8331}
8332
8333inline void Logger::validate_shared_memory_name(const std::string& name) {
8334 // The string ring lives in a companion segment named "<name>_str", and macOS
8335 // caps shm_open names at 31 characters, so the base name has to leave room.
8336 constexpr size_t kMaxNameLength = 24;
8337
8338 if (name.empty()) {
8339 throw std::runtime_error("shared_memory_name is required when mode is not QueueMode::Local.");
8340 }
8341 if (name.size() > kMaxNameLength) {
8342 throw std::runtime_error("shared_memory_name '" + name + "' is longer than "
8343 + std::to_string(kMaxNameLength) + " characters.");
8344 }
8345 for (char c : name) {
8346 const bool allowed = (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z')
8347 || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c == '_';
8348 if (!allowed) {
8349 throw std::runtime_error("shared_memory_name '" + name +
8350 "' may only contain characters in [A-Za-z0-9_].");
8351 }
8352 }
8353}
8354
8355inline size_t Logger::truncated_tag_length(std::string_view tag) noexcept {
8356 constexpr size_t kMaxTagBytes = SLICK_LOGGER_TAG_SIZE - 1; // leave room for the NUL
8357 if (tag.size() <= kMaxTagBytes) {
8358 return tag.size(); // fits whole, nothing to cut
8359 }
8360 // Never cut in the middle of a UTF-8 sequence: walk back from the cut point
8361 // over continuation bytes (0b10xxxxxx) so the stored tag stays printable.
8362 // tag[length] is in range here because tag.size() > kMaxTagBytes.
8363 size_t length = kMaxTagBytes;
8364 while (length > 0 && (static_cast<unsigned char>(tag[length]) & 0xC0) == 0x80) {
8365 --length;
8366 }
8367 return length;
8368}
8369
8370template<typename T>
8371inline std::unique_ptr<slick::queue<T, Logger::logger_queue_traits>> Logger::open_shared_queue(const std::string& name, uint32_t size,
8372 uint32_t items_per_slot) {
8373 std::string attach_error;
8374 try {
8375 // Attach to a segment somebody else already created. Sizing then comes
8376 // from its header, so a producer automatically matches the collector.
8377 return std::make_unique<slick::queue<T, logger_queue_traits>>(name.c_str());
8378 }
8379 catch (const std::exception& e) {
8380 // Usually just "nothing there yet". Keep the reason: if creating fails too,
8381 // reporting only the second error hides why the attach did not work, which
8382 // matters when the real cause was a creator still initializing rather than
8383 // a missing segment.
8384 attach_error = e.what();
8385 }
8386
8387 try {
8388 // Create it. Still create-or-attach, so a process that loses the race to
8389 // another creator simply attaches instead, and throws if that creator
8390 // chose a different items_per_slot.
8391 return std::make_unique<slick::queue<T, logger_queue_traits>>(size, items_per_slot, name.c_str());
8392 }
8393 catch (const std::exception& e) {
8394 throw std::runtime_error(std::string(e.what())
8395 + " (attaching to the existing segment first failed with: "
8396 + attach_error + ")");
8397 }
8398}
8399
8400inline void Logger::setup_shared_queues(const LogConfig& config, uint32_t queue_size, uint32_t string_buffer_size,
8401 uint32_t string_items_per_slot) {
8402 validate_shared_memory_name(config.shared_memory_name);
8403
8404 shm_name_ = config.shared_memory_name;
8405 mode_ = config.mode;
8406 collect_backlog_ = config.collect_backlog;
8407 stalled_entry_timeout_ms_ = config.stalled_entry_timeout_ms;
8408
8409 try {
8410 log_queue_ = open_shared_queue<LogEntry>(shm_name_, queue_size);
8411 string_queue_ = open_shared_queue<char>(shm_name_ + "_str", string_buffer_size, string_items_per_slot);
8412 }
8413 catch (const std::exception& e) {
8414 log_queue_.reset();
8415 string_queue_.reset();
8416 mode_ = QueueMode::Local;
8417 shm_name_.clear();
8418 // A size or element-size mismatch means another process attached to the
8419 // same name with different settings or a different build of the header.
8420 throw std::runtime_error("Failed to attach shared log queue '" + config.shared_memory_name
8421 + "': " + e.what()
8422 + ". All processes must agree on slick-logger version, "
8423 "SLICK_LOGGER_MAX_ARGS, log_queue_size, string_buffer_size and "
8424 "string_items_per_slot.");
8425 }
8426
8427 // String references become ring indices so the collector can resolve them
8428 // against its own mapping of the segment.
8429 entry_flags_ = kEntryOffsets;
8430#ifdef _WIN32
8431 pid_ = static_cast<uint32_t>(::_getpid());
8432#else
8433 pid_ = static_cast<uint32_t>(::getpid());
8434#endif
8435 std::memset(tag_, 0, sizeof(tag_));
8436 std::memcpy(tag_, config.process_tag.data(), truncated_tag_length(config.process_tag));
8437}
8438
8439inline std::string Logger::producer_segment_name(uint32_t slot) const {
8440 // '.' is not allowed in shared_memory_name, so no other name can collide.
8441 return shm_name_ + ".r" + std::to_string(slot);
8442}
8443
8444inline void Logger::setup_registry(const LogConfig& config) {
8445 using registry_t = detail::shm_registry;
8446 const bool collector = mode_ == QueueMode::SharedCollector;
8447 if (!collector && !thread_rings_) {
8448 return; // a producer on the shared rings never needs it
8449 }
8450 // The creator writes the header, then sets ready. Opening can race it, so
8451 // keep trying for a while rather than read a half-built header.
8452 const std::string name = shm_name_ + ".reg";
8453 const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(2);
8454 for (;;) {
8455 slick::shm::shared_memory shm(name.c_str(), sizeof(registry_t), slick::shm::open_or_create);
8456 auto* const registry = static_cast<registry_t*>(shm.data());
8457 if (registry && shm.is_creator()) {
8458 registry->magic = registry_t::kMagic;
8459 registry->layout_version = registry_t::kLayoutVersion;
8460 registry->slot_count = registry_t::kSlotCount;
8461 registry->ready.store(1, std::memory_order_release);
8462 }
8463 if (registry && shm.size() >= sizeof(registry_t) && registry->ready.load(std::memory_order_acquire) == 1) {
8464 if (registry->magic != registry_t::kMagic || registry->layout_version != registry_t::kLayoutVersion ||
8465 registry->slot_count != registry_t::kSlotCount) {
8466 throw std::runtime_error("shared memory registry '" + name + "' has layout version " +
8467 std::to_string(registry->layout_version) + ", this build uses " +
8468 std::to_string(registry_t::kLayoutVersion) +
8469 ". All processes must run the same slick-logger version.");
8470 }
8471 registry_shm_ = std::move(shm);
8472 registry_ = registry;
8473 break;
8474 }
8475 if (std::chrono::steady_clock::now() >= deadline) {
8476 throw std::runtime_error("shared memory registry '" + name +
8477 "' is not initialized: a stale or foreign segment, remove it");
8478 }
8479 std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
8480 }
8481 if (!collector) {
8482 return;
8483 }
8484 // One collector at a time: two would both hand ring space back to producers.
8485 const uint64_t lease = detail::collector_lease(detail::current_process_id());
8486 uint64_t holder = registry_->collector.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
8487 for (;;) {
8488 if (holder != 0 && holder != lease && detail::collector_lease_running(holder)) {
8489 throw std::runtime_error("another collector (pid " + std::to_string(holder >> 32) +
8490 ") is attached to '" + shm_name_ + "'");
8491 }
8492 if (registry_->collector.compare_exchange_weak(holder, lease, std::memory_order_acq_rel,
8493 std::memory_order_acquire)) {
8494 break;
8495 }
8496 }
8497 collector_lease_ = lease;
8498 string_epoch_ = &registry_->string_epoch;
8499 registry_backlog_ = config.collect_backlog;
8500 remote_ = std::make_unique<detail::remote_producer[]>(registry_t::kSlotCount);
8501 remote_views_.clear();
8502 registry_changes_seen_ = registry_->changes.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
8503 next_registry_scan_ns_ = 0;
8504 remote_flush_targets_.clear();
8505 remote_flush_generation_ = 0;
8506}
8507
8508inline bool Logger::claim_registry_slot(std::string& why) noexcept {
8509 using slot_t = detail::shm_registry_slot;
8510 try {
8511 const uint32_t pid = detail::current_process_id();
8512 const uint64_t start_time = detail::process_start_time(pid);
8513 const size_t bytes = detail::shm_ring_segment::bytes(max_thread_rings_, thread_ring_size_);
8514 // A free slot first. Failing that, one whose owner closed or died and whose
8515 // segment went with it, so nothing in it can still be read.
8516 for (int pass = 0; pass < 2; ++pass) {
8517 for (uint32_t i = 0; i < detail::shm_registry::kSlotCount; ++i) {
8518 slot_t& slot = registry_->slots[i];
8519 uint64_t control = slot.control.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
8520 const uint32_t state = slot_t::state_of(control);
8521 const std::string name = producer_segment_name(i);
8522 if (pass == 0 ? state != slot_t::kFree
8523 : !(state == slot_t::kClosing ||
8524 (state == slot_t::kActive &&
8525 !detail::process_running(slot.pid.load(std::memory_order_relaxed),
8526 slot.start_time.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)))) ||
8527 slick::shm::shared_memory::exists(name.c_str())) {
8528 continue;
8529 }
8530 // A new generation on claiming, so a claim taken over never passes for the new one.
8531 const uint32_t generation = slot_t::generation_of(control) + 1;
8532 const uint64_t claiming = slot_t::make(slot_t::kClaiming, generation);
8533 if (!slot.control.compare_exchange_strong(control, claiming, std::memory_order_acq_rel,
8534 std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
8535 continue;
8536 }
8537 slot.pid.store(pid, std::memory_order_relaxed);
8538 slot.start_time.store(start_time, std::memory_order_relaxed);
8539 try {
8540 slick::shm::shared_memory::remove(name.c_str()); // a stale segment: the slot is ours now
8541 slick::shm::shared_memory segment(name.c_str(), bytes, slick::shm::create_only);
8542 auto* const header = static_cast<detail::shm_ring_segment*>(segment.data());
8543 header->magic = detail::shm_ring_segment::kMagic;
8544 header->layout_version = detail::shm_ring_segment::kLayoutVersion;
8545 header->ring_layout_version = detail::producer_ring::kLayoutVersion;
8546 header->generation = generation;
8547 header->ring_count = max_thread_rings_;
8548 header->ring_capacity = thread_ring_size_;
8549 header->producer_base = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(header);
8550 header->record_layout = detail::shm_ring_segment::record_layout_of();
8551 for (uint32_t r = 0; r < max_thread_rings_; ++r) {
8552 detail::producer_ring::create(header->ring(r), thread_ring_size_);
8553 }
8554 uint64_t expected = claiming;
8555 if (!slot.control.compare_exchange_strong(expected, slot_t::make(slot_t::kActive, generation),
8556 std::memory_order_acq_rel, std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
8557 continue; // freed under us as a dead claim: leave it to its next owner
8558 }
8559 registry_->changes.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_release);
8560 ring_shm_ = std::move(segment);
8561 registry_slot_ = i;
8562 registry_generation_ = generation;
8563 return true;
8564 } catch (const std::exception& e) {
8565 why = e.what();
8566 uint64_t expected = claiming;
8567 slot.control.compare_exchange_strong(expected, slot_t::make(slot_t::kFree, generation),
8568 std::memory_order_release, std::memory_order_relaxed);
8569 }
8570 }
8571 }
8572 if (why.empty()) {
8573 why = "all " + std::to_string(detail::shm_registry::kSlotCount) + " registry slots are taken";
8574 }
8575 } catch (const std::exception& e) {
8576 why = e.what();
8577 }
8578 return false;
8579}
8580
8581inline void Logger::close_registry() noexcept {
8582 using slot_t = detail::shm_registry_slot;
8583 if (!registry_) {
8584 return;
8585 }
8586 if (remote_) {
8587 // Collector: a closing producer drained by now is freed; the rest stay
8588 // registered for the next collector.
8589 for (uint32_t i = 0; i < detail::shm_registry::kSlotCount; ++i) {
8590 detail::remote_producer& producer = remote_[i];
8591 if (producer.views) {
8592 detach_producer(i, producer.closing && producer.owns_slot && producer_drained(producer));
8593 }
8594 }
8595 uint64_t lease = collector_lease_;
8596 if (lease != 0) {
8597 registry_->collector.compare_exchange_strong(lease, 0, std::memory_order_release, std::memory_order_relaxed);
8598 }
8599 remote_.reset();
8600 remote_views_.clear();
8601 remote_views_.shrink_to_fit(); // free it with remote_, so a reopened collector starts with no allocation
8602 remote_flush_targets_.clear();
8603 collector_lease_ = 0;
8604 remote_retired_produced_ = remote_retired_consumed_ = remote_retired_dropped_ = 0;
8605 remote_produced_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
8606 remote_consumed_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
8607 remote_dropped_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
8608 remote_rings_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
8609 }
8610 if (registry_slot_ != kNoSlot) {
8611 // Producer: unmapped first, so by the time the collector frees the slot no
8612 // handle of this process keeps the segment's name taken.
8613 ring_shm_ = slick::shm::shared_memory{};
8614 uint64_t expected = slot_t::make(slot_t::kActive, registry_generation_);
8615 registry_->slots[registry_slot_].control.compare_exchange_strong(
8616 expected, slot_t::make(slot_t::kClosing, registry_generation_), std::memory_order_acq_rel,
8617 std::memory_order_relaxed);
8618 registry_->changes.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_release);
8619 registry_slot_ = kNoSlot;
8620 registry_generation_ = 0;
8621 }
8622 registry_shm_ = slick::shm::shared_memory{};
8623 registry_ = nullptr;
8624}
8625
8626inline void Logger::poll_registry() {
8627 const uint64_t changes = registry_->changes.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
8628 const int64_t now_ns = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(
8629 std::chrono::steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch()).count();
8630 if (changes == registry_changes_seen_ && now_ns < next_registry_scan_ns_) {
8631 return;
8632 }
8633 registry_changes_seen_ = changes;
8634 next_registry_scan_ns_ = now_ns + kRegistryScanMs * 1000000;
8635 scan_registry(false);
8636}
8637
8638inline void Logger::scan_registry(bool initial) {
8639 using slot_t = detail::shm_registry_slot;
8640 const int64_t now_ns = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(
8641 std::chrono::steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch()).count();
8642 for (uint32_t i = 0; i < detail::shm_registry::kSlotCount; ++i) {
8643 slot_t& slot = registry_->slots[i];
8644 detail::remote_producer& producer = remote_[i];
8645 const uint64_t control = slot.control.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
8646 const uint32_t state = slot_t::state_of(control);
8647 if (producer.views) {
8648 if (slot_t::generation_of(control) != producer.generation ||
8649 (state != slot_t::kActive && state != slot_t::kClosing)) {
8650 producer.closing = true; // the slot moved on: finish this one and leave the slot be
8651 producer.owns_slot = false;
8652 } else if (state == slot_t::kClosing || !detail::process_running(producer.pid, producer.start_time)) {
8653 producer.closing = true; // closed or died: what it published is all there is
8654 }
8655 if (producer.closing && producer_drained(producer)) {
8656 detach_producer(i, producer.owns_slot);
8657 }
8658 continue;
8659 }
8660 if (state == slot_t::kActive || state == slot_t::kClosing) {
8661 // On Retry the slot keeps its segment, records and all, for the next scan.
8662 if (attach_producer(i, initial && !registry_backlog_) == AttachResult::Unreadable &&
8663 (state == slot_t::kClosing || !detail::process_running(slot.pid.load(std::memory_order_relaxed),
8664 slot.start_time.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)))) {
8665 free_registry_slot(i, control); // nothing to read, and nobody left to write it
8666 }
8667 } else if (state == slot_t::kClaiming) {
8668 // A claimer records its pid just after it claims, so give it time.
8669 if (producer.claiming_control != control) {
8670 producer.claiming_control = control;
8671 producer.claiming_since_ns = now_ns;
8672 } else if (now_ns - producer.claiming_since_ns > 1000000000 &&
8673 !detail::process_running(slot.pid.load(std::memory_order_relaxed),
8674 slot.start_time.load(std::memory_order_relaxed))) {
8675 free_registry_slot(i, control); // died building its segment
8676 }
8677 }
8678 }
8679 publish_remote_totals();
8680}
8681
8682inline Logger::AttachResult Logger::attach_producer(uint32_t index, bool skip_backlog) {
8683 using slot_t = detail::shm_registry_slot;
8684 using segment_t = detail::shm_ring_segment;
8685 const slot_t& slot = registry_->slots[index];
8686 const uint64_t control = slot.control.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
8687 const uint32_t state = slot_t::state_of(control);
8688 if (state != slot_t::kActive && state != slot_t::kClosing) {
8689 return AttachResult::Unreadable;
8690 }
8691 const uint32_t generation = slot_t::generation_of(control);
8692 try {
8693 slick::shm::shared_memory segment(producer_segment_name(index).c_str(), slick::shm::open_existing);
8694 auto* const header = static_cast<segment_t*>(segment.data());
8695 if (!header || segment.size() < sizeof(segment_t) || header->magic != segment_t::kMagic ||
8696 header->generation != generation) {
8697 return AttachResult::Unreadable; // not the segment this generation built
8698 }
8699 if (header->layout_version != segment_t::kLayoutVersion ||
8700 header->ring_layout_version != detail::producer_ring::kLayoutVersion ||
8701 header->record_layout != segment_t::record_layout_of() || header->ring_count == 0 ||
8702 header->ring_count > segment_t::kMaxRings || !detail::producer_ring::valid_capacity(header->ring_capacity) ||
8703 segment.size() < segment_t::bytes(header->ring_count, header->ring_capacity)) {
8704 detail::remote_producer& producer = remote_[index];
8705 if (producer.refused_generation != generation) {
8706 producer.refused_generation = generation;
8707 log(LogLevel::L_WARN, "SlickLogger: producer pid {} was built with another slick-logger layout "
8708 "(version or SLICK_LOGGER_TAG_SIZE); its thread rings are not read",
8709 slot.pid.load(std::memory_order_relaxed));
8710 }
8711 return AttachResult::Unreadable;
8712 }
8713 const uint32_t count = header->ring_count;
8714 auto views = std::make_unique<detail::ring_view[]>(count);
8715 const uintptr_t delta = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(header) - static_cast<uintptr_t>(header->producer_base);
8716 for (uint32_t r = 0; r < count; ++r) {
8717 detail::producer_ring* const ring = header->ring(r);
8718 if (ring->layout_version() != detail::producer_ring::kLayoutVersion ||
8719 ring->capacity() != header->ring_capacity) {
8720 return AttachResult::Unreadable;
8721 }
8722 detail::ring_view& view = views[r];
8723 view.ring = ring;
8724 view.reader = detail::ring_reader(*ring);
8725 view.remote = true;
8726 view.delta = delta;
8727 if (skip_backlog) {
8728 view.reader.skip();
8729 }
8730 }
8731 // Reserve room for every ring before committing. A push_back that threw
8732 // partway would leave the producer attached with rings nobody reads or retries.
8733 remote_views_.reserve(remote_views_.size() + count);
8734 detail::remote_producer& producer = remote_[index];
8735 producer.segment = std::move(segment);
8736 producer.views = std::move(views);
8737 producer.ring_count = count;
8738 producer.generation = generation;
8739 producer.pid = slot.pid.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
8740 producer.start_time = slot.start_time.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
8741 producer.closing = state == slot_t::kClosing;
8742 producer.owns_slot = true;
8743 for (uint32_t r = 0; r < count; ++r) {
8744 remote_views_.push_back(&producer.views[r]);
8745 }
8746 publish_remote_totals(); // attached outside a scan too: flush(), the frontier, a spill
8747 return AttachResult::Attached;
8748 } catch (const std::bad_alloc&) {
8749 return AttachResult::Retry;
8750 } catch (const std::system_error& e) {
8751 // Opening the segment failed. Not found or permission denied is final. Anything
8752 // else, such as running out of handles or address space, is retried.
8753 const std::error_code& ec = e.code();
8754 return ec == slick::shm::errc::not_found || ec == std::errc::permission_denied ? AttachResult::Unreadable
8755 : AttachResult::Retry;
8756 } catch (const std::exception&) {
8757 return AttachResult::Unreadable;
8758 }
8759}
8760
8761inline void Logger::attach_new_producers() noexcept {
8762 using slot_t = detail::shm_registry_slot;
8763 for (uint32_t i = 0; i < detail::shm_registry::kSlotCount; ++i) {
8764 if (remote_[i].views) {
8765 continue;
8766 }
8767 const uint32_t state = slot_t::state_of(registry_->slots[i].control.load(std::memory_order_acquire));
8768 if (state == slot_t::kActive || state == slot_t::kClosing) {
8769 attach_producer(i, false); // a producer logs only once active, so nothing it logged is missed
8770 }
8771 }
8772}
8773
8774inline void Logger::detach_producer(uint32_t index, bool free_slot) {
8775 using slot_t = detail::shm_registry_slot;
8776 detail::remote_producer& producer = remote_[index];
8777 const detail::ring_view* const first = producer.views.get();
8778 const detail::ring_view* const last = first + producer.ring_count;
8779 std::erase_if(remote_views_, [&](const detail::ring_view* view) {
8780 return std::less_equal<>{}(first, view) && std::less<>{}(view, last);
8781 });
8782 if (shared_gate_view_ && std::less_equal<>{}(first, shared_gate_view_) && std::less<>{}(shared_gate_view_, last)) {
8783 shared_gate_view_ = nullptr; // drained by now, so the spill waiting on it may go
8784 shared_gate_ring_ = nullptr;
8785 }
8786 // The statistics snapshot must not hold on to rings about to be unmapped.
8787 std::erase_if(stats_gen_rings_, [&](const auto& noted) {
8788 for (uint32_t r = 0; r < producer.ring_count; ++r) {
8789 if (noted.first == producer.views[r].ring) {
8790 return true;
8791 }
8792 }
8793 return false;
8794 });
8795 for (uint32_t r = 0; r < producer.ring_count; ++r) {
8796 const detail::producer_ring* const ring = producer.views[r].ring;
8797 remote_retired_produced_ += ring->records();
8798 remote_retired_consumed_ += ring->released_records();
8799 remote_retired_dropped_ += ring->drops();
8800 }
8801 const uint32_t generation = producer.generation;
8802 producer.views.reset();
8803 producer.segment = slick::shm::shared_memory{};
8804 producer.ring_count = 0;
8805 producer.closing = false;
8806 if (free_slot) {
8807 const uint64_t closing = slot_t::make(slot_t::kClosing, generation);
8808 const uint64_t active = slot_t::make(slot_t::kActive, generation);
8809 free_registry_slot(index, slot_t::state_of(registry_->slots[index].control.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) ==
8810 slot_t::kClosing ? closing : active);
8811 }
8812}
8813
8814inline void Logger::free_registry_slot(uint32_t index, uint64_t control) noexcept {
8815 using slot_t = detail::shm_registry_slot;
8816 // Remove the segment before freeing the slot, or it could be a new owner's.
8817 // Its spills carry their own pid, so the slot can be freed right away.
8818 slick::shm::shared_memory::remove(producer_segment_name(index).c_str());
8819 registry_->slots[index].control.compare_exchange_strong(
8820 control, slot_t::make(slot_t::kFree, slot_t::generation_of(control)), std::memory_order_acq_rel,
8821 std::memory_order_relaxed);
8822}
8823
8824inline bool Logger::producer_drained(const detail::remote_producer& producer) noexcept {
8825 for (uint32_t r = 0; r < producer.ring_count; ++r) {
8826 const detail::ring_view& view = producer.views[r];
8827 if (view.head || view.ring->written() != view.ring->released()) {
8828 return false;
8829 }
8830 }
8831 return true;
8832}
8833
8834inline void Logger::publish_remote_totals() noexcept {
8835 uint64_t produced = remote_retired_produced_;
8836 uint64_t consumed = remote_retired_consumed_;
8837 uint64_t dropped = remote_retired_dropped_;
8838 for (const detail::ring_view* view : remote_views_) {
8839 consumed += view->ring->released_records(); // before records(), so depth never reads negative
8840 produced += view->ring->records();
8841 dropped += view->ring->drops();
8842 }
8843 remote_consumed_.store(consumed, std::memory_order_relaxed);
8844 remote_produced_.store(produced, std::memory_order_relaxed);
8845 remote_dropped_.store(dropped, std::memory_order_relaxed);
8846 remote_rings_.store(static_cast<uint32_t>(remote_views_.size()), std::memory_order_relaxed);
8847}
8848
8849inline bool Logger::remote_flush_ready(uint64_t generation) {
8850 if (remote_flush_generation_ != generation) {
8851 // A new request: everything published by now has to be taken first,
8852 // including from producers that registered while the writer was busy.
8853 remote_flush_generation_ = generation;
8854 remote_flush_targets_.clear();
8855 attach_new_producers();
8856 for (uint32_t i = 0; i < detail::shm_registry::kSlotCount; ++i) {
8857 const detail::remote_producer& producer = remote_[i];
8858 for (uint32_t r = 0; producer.views && r < producer.ring_count; ++r) {
8859 const detail::producer_ring* const ring = producer.views[r].ring;
8860 const uint64_t written = ring->written();
8861 if (written != ring->released()) {
8862 remote_flush_targets_.push_back({i, producer.generation, r, written});
8863 }
8864 }
8865 }
8866 }
8867 std::erase_if(remote_flush_targets_, [this](const flush_target& target) {
8868 const detail::remote_producer& producer = remote_[target.producer];
8869 return !producer.views || producer.generation != target.generation ||
8870 producer.views[target.ring].ring->released() >= target.written;
8871 });
8872 return remote_flush_targets_.empty();
8873}
8874
8875inline bool Logger::collector_attached() const noexcept {
8876 const uint64_t lease = registry_ ? registry_->collector.load(std::memory_order_acquire) : 0;
8877 return lease != 0 && detail::collector_lease_running(lease);
8878}
8879
8880inline void Logger::wait_for_collector(std::chrono::milliseconds limit) {
8881 if (!collector_attached()) {
8882 return; // a later collector replays what is still here
8883 }
8884 // What this process has logged so far: its rings, and its share of the shared
8885 // queue (threads past its rings, spills), which the collector's cursor covers.
8886 const uint64_t queue_target = log_queue_->initial_reading_index();
8887 std::vector<std::pair<const detail::producer_ring*, uint64_t>> targets;
8888 const uint32_t used = ring_slots_used_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
8889 for (uint32_t i = 0; i < used; ++i) {
8890 const detail::producer_ring* const ring = ring_slots_[i].ring.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
8891 if (ring && ring->written() != ring->released()) {
8892 targets.emplace_back(ring, ring->written());
8893 }
8894 }
8895 const auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
8896 auto next_check = start + std::chrono::milliseconds(50);
8897 wait_until_ready([&] {
8898 bool done = registry_->read_index.load(std::memory_order_acquire) >= queue_target;
8899 for (const auto& [ring, target] : targets) {
8900 done = done && ring->released() >= target;
8901 }
8902 if (done) {
8903 return true;
8904 }
8905 const auto now = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
8906 if (limit.count() > 0 && now - start >= limit) {
8907 return true;
8908 }
8909 if (now >= next_check) {
8910 next_check = now + std::chrono::milliseconds(50);
8911 return !collector_attached(); // it went away mid-wait
8912 }
8913 return false;
8914 });
8915}
8916
8917inline void Logger::add_sink(std::shared_ptr<ISink> sink) {
8918 sink->set_index(static_cast<int>(sinks_.size()));
8919 // The single place every sink passes through, so applying the default here is
8920 // what lets set_pattern() be called before or after the add_*_sink() calls.
8921 // Unconditional even when there is no default, so the sink's record of what
8922 // it would inherit always matches this logger.
8923 sink->apply_default_pattern(pattern_store_, default_pattern_);
8924 sinks_.push_back(sink);
8925 if (!sink->name().empty()) {
8926 sinkname_index_map_[sink->name()] = sink->index();
8927 }
8928}
8929
8930inline void Logger::set_pattern(std::string_view pattern) {
8931 // Compiled exactly once, here. An invalid pattern throws before any sink has
8932 // been touched, so a typo cannot leave half the sinks reformatted, and the
8933 // sinks that do take it then share the one formatter rather than each
8934 // compiling the same text over again. The loop itself cannot fail, since
8935 // apply_default_pattern() is noexcept, so the compile is the only step that
8936 // can, and it happens before the first sink is reached.
8937 const PatternFormatter* compiled = pattern_store_->get(pattern);
8938 default_pattern_ = compiled;
8939 for (auto& sink : sinks_) {
8940 if (sink) {
8941 sink->apply_default_pattern(pattern_store_, compiled);
8942 }
8943 }
8944}
8945
8946inline void Logger::set_timestamper(std::shared_ptr<ITimestamper> timestamper) {
8947 if (timestamper == timestamper_) {
8948 return;
8949 }
8950 // Room first: push_back is the only step that can throw, and doing it before
8951 // the swap means a failure leaves the old timestamper fully in place.
8952 if (timestamper_) {
8953 retired_timestampers_.reserve(retired_timestampers_.size() + 1);
8954 }
8955 // Release so the new timestamper's own state is visible to every thread
8956 // that loads the pointer, see current_timestamp().
8957 active_timestamper_.store(timestamper.get(), std::memory_order_release);
8958 if (timestamper_) {
8959 retired_timestampers_.push_back(std::move(timestamper_));
8960 }
8961 timestamper_ = std::move(timestamper);
8962}
8963
8964inline void Logger::release_sinks() {
8965 // Detach before dropping. A caller can still hold a shared_ptr to a sink this
8966 // logger is releasing, and an index left pointing at a slot that a later
8967 // add_sink() reuses would silently route that stale handle's entries to an
8968 // unrelated sink. -1 makes ISink::should_log() reject it instead.
8969 for (auto& sink : sinks_) {
8970 if (sink) {
8971 sink->set_index(-1);
8972 }
8973 }
8974 // sinkname_index_map_ holds string_view keys that point into the name strings
8975 // owned by each sink object, so it must be cleared before the sink shared_ptrs
8976 // are destroyed or dangling views would remain.
8977 sinkname_index_map_.clear();
8978 sinks_.clear();
8979}
8980
8981inline void Logger::clear_sinks() {
8982 release_sinks();
8983}

8985template<typename SinkT>
8986inline std::shared_ptr<ISink> Logger::get_sink() const noexcept {
8987 for (auto &sink : sinks_) {
8988 if (dynamic_cast<SinkT*>(sink.get()) != nullptr) {
8989 return sink;
8990 }
8991 }
8992 return nullptr;
8993}
8994
8995inline std::shared_ptr<ISink> Logger::get_sink(std::string_view name) const noexcept {
8996 auto iter = sinkname_index_map_.find(name);
8997 if (iter != sinkname_index_map_.end()) {
8998 int index = iter->second;
8999 if (index >= 0 && static_cast<size_t>(index) < sinks_.size()) [[likely]] {
9000 return sinks_[index];
9001 }
9002 }
9003 return nullptr;
9004}

9006inline void Logger::init(size_t queue_size, size_t string_buffer_size) {
9007 shutdown(false); // make sure the logger is stopped
9008
9009 if (sinks_.empty()) {
9010 throw std::runtime_error("No sink. Sinks should be added first before calling this.");
9011 }
9012
9013 // Initialize the logger with sinks that were already added; add them before calling this
9014 // Ensure queue_size is power of 2
9015 create_local_queues(round_up_to_power_of_2(queue_size),
9016 round_up_to_power_of_2(string_buffer_size), kDefaultStringItemsPerSlot);
9017 configure_thread_rings(LogConfig{});
9018 start();
9019}

9147template<typename FormatT, typename... Args>
9148inline void Logger::log_to_sink_with_location(int sink_index, LogLevel level, const char* file_name, uint32_t line,
9149 bool copy_file_name,
