9154
9155template<typename FormatT, typename... Args>
9156inline void Logger::log_at_location(int sink_index, LogLevel level, const char* file_name, uint32_t file_length,
9157 uint32_t line, bool copy_file_name, FormatT&& format, Args&&... args) {
9158 if (!running_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) || !log_queue_ || level < log_level_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed))
9159 {
9160 return;
9161 }
9162
9163 const uint64_t timestamp = current_timestamp();
9164
9165 // One test for Local mode's rings; a SharedProducer's are checked only past it.
9166 if (local_rings_) {
9167 if (log_to_thread_ring<false>(sink_index, level, file_name, file_length, line, copy_file_name, timestamp,
9168 format, args...)) {
9169 return;
9170 }
9171 } else if (ring_in_shm_) [[unlikely]] {
9172 // Packed into one tuple, scalars by value. Passed one by one, or by
9173 // reference, they add a few ns per call to the Local path above, even
9174 // when this branch is not taken.
9175 const std::tuple<FormatT&&, detail::cold_arg_t<Args>...> packed(
9176 std::forward<FormatT>(format), static_cast<detail::cold_arg_t<Args>>(args)...);
9177 if (log_to_shared_thread_ring(sink_index, level, file_name, file_length, line, copy_file_name, timestamp,
9178 packed)) {
9179 return;
9180 }
9181 }
9182
9183 // In shared-memory mode every string reference must be a ring index, because
9184 // the segment maps at a different base address in each attached process.
9185 const bool use_offsets = (entry_flags_ & kEntryOffsets) != 0;
9186
9187 // Everything bound for the string ring is copied there before the entry's
9188 // slot is reserved: the statistics frontier relies on a string never being
9189 // reserved after the slot that refers to it (see advance_string_frontier()).
9190 uint8_t flags = entry_flags_;
9191 StringRef file{};
9192 if (has_source_location(file_name, line)) {
9193 // A static file name lives in the caller's read-only data, which no other
9194 // process can address, so shared mode always copies it into the ring.
9195 // A length of 0 is unknown: measured here only when copying, else by the writer.
9196 file = (copy_file_name || use_offsets)
9197 ? store_string_in_queue(file_length ? std::string_view{file_name, file_length} : std::string_view{file_name})
9198 : StringRef{file_name, file_length};
9199 flags |= kEntryHasSourceLocation;
9200 } else {
9201 line = 0;
9202 }
9203 StringRef format_ref;
9204 if constexpr (IS_STRING_LITERAL(format)) {
9205 constexpr uint32_t format_length = static_cast<uint32_t>(sizeof(format) - 1);
9206 if (use_offsets) {
9207 format_ref = store_string_in_queue(std::string_view{format, format_length});
9208 } else {
9209 format_ref = StringRef{format, format_length}; // String literal: safe to store the pointer
9210 flags |= kEntryStaticFormat;
9211 }
9212 }
9213 else {
9214 // Non-literal format strings are copied into the string queue so their
9215 // lifetime extends until the writer thread consumes the entry.
9216 static_assert(std::is_convertible_v<FormatT, std::string_view>,
9217 "Format string type must be a string literal or convertible to std::string_view.");
9218 format_ref = store_string_in_queue(
9219 std::string_view{std::forward<FormatT>(format)});
9220 }
9221
9222 // Arguments are staged in an array sized for this call, so only the ones it
9223 // carries are ever written to the slot.
9224 constexpr size_t kMaxArgCount = is_single_format_args_v<Args...> ? SLICK_LOGGER_MAX_ARGS : sizeof...(Args);
9225 static_assert(kMaxArgCount <= SLICK_LOGGER_MAX_ARGS, "Too many log arguments");
9226 std::array<LogArgument, kMaxArgCount> staged_args;
9227 uint8_t arg_count = 0;
9228 if constexpr (is_single_format_args_v<Args...>) {
9229 // Pre-built std::format_args: unpack values on the calling thread
9230 // (format_args holds non-owning references).
9231 arg_count = enqueue_format_args(staged_args.data(),
9232 std::get<0>(std::forward_as_tuple(std::forward<Args>(args)...)));
9233 } else {
9234 arg_count = static_cast<uint8_t>(sizeof...(args));
9235 size_t arg_idx = 0;
9236 (enqueue_argument(staged_args[arg_idx++], std::forward<Args>(args)), ...);
9237 }
9238#if SLICK_LOGGER_ENABLE_THREAD_ID
9239 const uint32_t thread_id = detail::current_thread_id();
9240#else
9241 const uint32_t thread_id = 0;
9242#endif
9243
9244 // The entry is written straight into its slot, field by field and only as
9245 // many arguments as it has, rather than built on the stack and copied whole:
9246 // a LogEntry is 327 bytes, most of them argument slots a call rarely fills.
9247 uint64_t index;
9248 LogEntry& entry = reserve_shared_entry(index, use_offsets);
9249 // A compile-time argument size on the usual path, so the copy is a few plain stores.
9250 write_entry(entry, format_ref, timestamp, file, thread_id, line, sink_index, level, flags, arg_count,
9251 staged_args.data(), (is_single_format_args_v<Args...> ? arg_count : kMaxArgCount) * sizeof(LogArgument));
9252 log_queue_->publish(index);
9253 wake_writer();
9254}
9255
9256SLICK_LOGGER_FORCE_INLINE LogEntry& Logger::reserve_shared_entry(uint64_t& index, bool use_offsets) noexcept {
9257 index = log_queue_->reserve();
9258 if (!use_offsets) {
9259 // Announce the page before writing into it; see entry_page_cursor_.
9260 const uint64_t page = index >> entry_page_shift_;
9261 uint64_t announced = entry_page_cursor_.page.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
9262 while (announced < page &&
9263 !entry_page_cursor_.page.compare_exchange_weak(announced, page, std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
9264 }
9265 }
9266 // Orders the reservation and the page above before every write to the slot
9267 // that follows, as seen by the writer thread's acquire fence in snapshot_entry():
9268 // a writer that copies any of those bytes also sees this slot's reuse announced,
9269 // and discards the copy.
9270 std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_release);
9271 return *(*log_queue_)[index];
9272}
9273
9274SLICK_LOGGER_FORCE_INLINE void Logger::write_entry(LogEntry& entry, StringRef format, uint64_t timestamp,
9275 StringRef file, uint32_t thread_id, uint32_t line,
9276 int sink_index, LogLevel level, uint8_t flags, uint8_t arg_count,
9277 const LogArgument* args, size_t arg_bytes) const noexcept {
9278 entry.format = format;
9279 entry.timestamp = timestamp;
9280 entry.file = file;
9281 entry.pid = pid_;
9282 entry.thread_id = thread_id;
9283 entry.line = line;
9284 entry.sink_index = sink_index;
9285 entry.level = level;
9286 entry.flags = flags;
9287 entry.arg_count = arg_count;
9288 std::memcpy(entry.tag, tag_, sizeof(entry.tag));
9289 if (arg_bytes != 0) {
9290 std::memcpy(entry.args, args, arg_bytes);
9291 }
9292}
9293
9294template<typename Packed>
9295SLICK_LOGGER_NOINLINE bool Logger::log_to_shared_thread_ring(int sink_index, LogLevel level, const char* file_name,
9296 uint32_t file_length, uint32_t line, bool copy_file_name,
9297 uint64_t timestamp, const Packed& packed) {
9298 return std::apply(
9299 [&](auto&& format, auto&&... args) {
9300 return log_to_thread_ring<true>(sink_index, level, file_name, file_length, line, copy_file_name,
9301 timestamp, format, args...);
9302 },
9303 packed);
9304}
9305
9306template<bool InShm, typename FormatT, typename... Args>
9307SLICK_LOGGER_FORCE_INLINE bool Logger::log_to_thread_ring(int sink_index, LogLevel level, const char* file_name,
9308 uint32_t file_length, uint32_t line, bool copy_file_name,
9309 uint64_t timestamp, FormatT&& format, Args&&... args) {
9310 detail::thread_ring_tls& tls = detail::tls_thread_ring;
9311 detail::producer_ring* ring = tls.ring;
9312 if (!thread_ring_current(tls)) [[unlikely]] {
9313 ring = attach_thread_ring(tls);
9314 }
9315 if (!ring) [[unlikely]] {
9316 return false; // no ring this run: the shared path, for every entry, so order holds
9317 }
9318
9319 // Pass 1: every field as stored, strings still pointing at the caller's bytes.
9320 uint8_t flags = 0;
9321 size_t string_bytes = 0;
9322 StringRef file{};
9323 bool copy_file = false;
9324 if (has_source_location(file_name, line)) {
9325 if (copy_file_name) {
9326 string_bytes += stage_bytes(file, file_name, file_length ? file_length : std::strlen(file_name), true);
9327 copy_file = true;
9328 } else {
9329 file = StringRef{file_name, file_length}; // a length of 0 is unknown: the writer measures it
9330 }
9331 flags |= kEntryHasSourceLocation;
9332 } else {
9333 line = 0;
9334 }
9335 StringRef format_ref;
9336 if constexpr (IS_STRING_LITERAL(format)) {
9337 format_ref = StringRef{format, static_cast<uint32_t>(sizeof(format) - 1)};
9338 flags |= kEntryStaticFormat;
9339 } else {
9340 static_assert(std::is_convertible_v<FormatT, std::string_view>,
9341 "Format string type must be a string literal or convertible to std::string_view.");
9342 const std::string_view text{format};
9343 string_bytes += stage_bytes(format_ref, text.data(), text.size(), true);
9344 }
9345 constexpr size_t kMaxArgCount = is_single_format_args_v<Args...> ? SLICK_LOGGER_MAX_ARGS : sizeof...(Args);
9346 static_assert(kMaxArgCount <= SLICK_LOGGER_MAX_ARGS, "Too many log arguments");
9347 // Converted by std::to_string into the shared string ring while staging, before
9348 // the record has a place: mark as far as it could end, and lower it once placed.
9349 constexpr bool kArgsUseStringRing = !is_single_format_args_v<Args...> && (detail::uses_string_ring_v<Args> || ...);
9350 if constexpr (kArgsUseStringRing) {
9351 mark_shared_strings(*ring, ring->written() + ring->capacity());
9352 }
9353 std::array<LogArgument, kMaxArgCount> staged_args;
9354 uint8_t arg_count = 0;
9355 if constexpr (is_single_format_args_v<Args...>) {
9356 arg_count = unpack_format_args(staged_args.data(), std::get<0>(std::forward_as_tuple(args...)),
9357 [&](LogArgument& arg, auto&& value) {
9358 string_bytes += stage_argument(arg, std::forward<decltype(value)>(value));
9359 });
9360 } else {
9361 arg_count = static_cast<uint8_t>(sizeof...(args));
9362 size_t arg_idx = 0;
9363 ((string_bytes += stage_argument(staged_args[arg_idx++], args)), ...);
9364 }
9365 if constexpr (InShm) {
9366 string_bytes += stage_static_strings(file, copy_file, format_ref, flags);
9367 }
9368
9369 // Copies every staged string to @p out, or to the shared string ring when null.
9370 const auto place_strings = [&](char* out) {
9371 if (string_bytes == 0) {
9372 return;
9373 }
9374 const auto place = [&](StringRef& ref, bool terminate) {
9375 if (out) [[likely]] {
9376 copy_staged(out, ref, terminate);
9377 } else if (ref.length != 0) {
9378 ref = store_bytes_in_queue(ref.ptr, ref.length, terminate);
9379 }
9380 };
9381 if (copy_file) {
9382 place(file, true);
9383 }
9384 if constexpr (InShm || !IS_STRING_LITERAL(format)) {
9385 place(format_ref, true); // in shared memory, a literal was staged too
9386 }
9387 if constexpr (is_single_format_args_v<Args...>) {
9388 for (uint8_t i = 0; i < arg_count; ++i) {
9389 LogArgument& arg = staged_args[i];
9390 if (arg.type == ArgType::STRING_DYNAMIC || arg.type == ArgType::BLOB) {
9391 place(arg.value.dynamic_str, arg.type != ArgType::BLOB);
9392 }
9393 }
9394 } else if constexpr (kMaxArgCount > 0) {
9395 // Unrolled by the compiler: which arguments are strings is known here.
9396 constexpr bool kCopied[] = {detail::is_copied_string_v<Args>...};
9397 for (size_t i = 0; i < kMaxArgCount; ++i) {
9398 if (kCopied[i]) {
9399 place(staged_args[i].value.dynamic_str, staged_args[i].type != ArgType::BLOB);
9400 }
9401 }
9402 }
9403 };
9404
9405 // Pass 2: one reservation for the whole record, strings after the arguments.
9406 // Strings too big for the ring go to the shared string ring, and the record
9407 // stays here, so the thread's entries stay in order.
9408 const size_t arg_bytes = (is_single_format_args_v<Args...> ? arg_count : kMaxArgCount) * sizeof(LogArgument);
9409 size_t payload = offsetof(LogEntry, args) + arg_bytes + string_bytes;
9410 const bool inline_strings = payload <= thread_ring_max_payload_;
9411 if (!inline_strings) [[unlikely]] {
9412 payload -= string_bytes;
9413 }
9414 // Entries this thread spilled are still in the shared queue: its ring waits,
9415 // so a new record cannot overtake them. The writer's cursor moves with every
9416 // spilled entry it dispatches, so it is read only every kSpillCheckCalls.
9417 detail::thread_ring_slot& slot = *tls.slot;
9418 if (slot.spill_end != 0 && --slot.spill_check == 0) [[unlikely]] {
9419 slot.spill_check = kSpillCheckCalls;
9420 if (spill_progress_->load(std::memory_order_acquire) >= slot.spill_end) {
9421 slot.spill_end = 0;
9422 }
9423 }
9424 uint8_t* const record = slot.spill_end == 0 ? ring->try_reserve(static_cast<uint32_t>(payload)) : nullptr;
9425 if (!record) [[unlikely]] {
9426 if (ring_full_drops_) {
9427 ring->drop(); // counted in LogStats::entry_loss_count
9428 if constexpr (kArgsUseStringRing) {
9429 ring->mark_shared_strings(ring->written());
9430 }
9431 return true;
9432 }
9433 // Full, or an earlier spill is still pending: the shared queue instead of a
9434 // drop, flagged kEntrySpilled with the ring's route in pid. The writer
9435 // holds such an entry until the ring has been drained to where the spill
9436 // began, so the thread's order holds. Written here rather than in a helper,
9437 // so the arguments are still a compile-time size, as on the shared path.
9438 place_strings(nullptr); // to the shared string ring, before the slot as on the shared path
9439 if (slot.spill_end == 0) {
9440 begin_spill(slot, *ring);
9441 }
9442 uint64_t index;
9443 LogEntry& entry = reserve_shared_entry(index, InShm);
9444 write_entry(entry, format_ref, timestamp, file, tls.thread_id, line, sink_index, level,
9445 static_cast<uint8_t>(flags | entry_flags_ | kEntrySpilled), arg_count, staged_args.data(),
9446 arg_bytes);
9447 const uint32_t route =
9448 spill_route_base_ | (static_cast<uint32_t>(tls.slot - ring_slots_.get()) << spill_route_shift_);
9449 if constexpr (InShm) {
9450 entry.format.length |= route << 16; // see kEntrySpilled
9451 entry.file.length |= route & 0xFFFF0000u;
9452 } else {
9453 entry.pid = route;
9454 }
9455 log_queue_->publish(index);
9456 slot.spill_end = index + 1;
9457 if constexpr (kArgsUseStringRing) {
9458 ring->mark_shared_strings(ring->written());
9459 }
9460 wake_writer();
9461 return true;
9462 }
9463 if (!inline_strings) [[unlikely]] {
9464 mark_shared_strings(*ring, ring->reserved_end());
9465 }
9466 place_strings(inline_strings ? reinterpret_cast<char*>(record) + offsetof(LogEntry, args) + arg_bytes : nullptr);
9467 write_entry(*reinterpret_cast<LogEntry*>(record), format_ref, timestamp, file, tls.thread_id, line, sink_index,
9468 level, flags, arg_count, staged_args.data(), arg_bytes);
9469 ring->publish();
9470 if constexpr (kArgsUseStringRing) {
9471 ring->mark_shared_strings(ring->written()); // the record's own end, now it has one
9472 }
9473 if (ring_fence_) {
9474 std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_seq_cst); // see detail::writer_barrier_available()
9475 }
9476 wake_writer();
9477 return true;
9478}
9479
9480SLICK_LOGGER_NOINLINE inline void Logger::mark_shared_strings(detail::producer_ring& ring, uint64_t end) noexcept {
9481 ring.mark_shared_strings(end);
9482 string_epoch_->fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
9483 // Before the string ring reservation that follows; pairs with the fence in
9484 // advance_string_frontier().
9485 std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_release);
9486}
9487
9488SLICK_LOGGER_NOINLINE inline void Logger::begin_spill(detail::thread_ring_slot& slot,
9489 detail::producer_ring& ring) noexcept {
9490 // Published before the entry that refers to it. A previous spill's entries
9491 // are all out by now, so nothing still waits on the old value.
9492 ring.set_spill_gate(ring.written());
9493 slot.spill_check = kSpillCheckCalls;
9494}
9495
9496inline bool Logger::prepare_thread() noexcept {
9497 if (!running_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) || !thread_rings_) {
9498 return false;
9499 }
9500 detail::thread_ring_tls& tls = detail::tls_thread_ring;
9501 if (!thread_ring_current(tls) && !attach_thread_ring(tls)) {
9502 return false;
9503 }
9504 if (!tls.ring) {
9505 return false; // every ring is taken
9506 }
9507 // A log call leaves the ring's pages to be faulted in as it fills. Fault them
9508 // all now instead, while the ring is still empty and so safe to overwrite.
9509 detail::thread_ring_slot& slot = *tls.slot;
9510 if (!slot.prefaulted && tls.ring->written() == tls.ring->released()) {
9511 tls.ring->prefault();
9512 slot.prefaulted = true;
9513 }
9514 return true;
9515}
9516
9517SLICK_LOGGER_FORCE_INLINE bool Logger::thread_ring_current(const detail::thread_ring_tls& tls) const noexcept {
9518 // In this order: the slot may be read only once owner and generation match.
9519 return tls.owner == this && tls.generation == ring_generation_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) &&
9520 (!tls.ring || tls.slot->ticket.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) == tls.ticket);
9521}
9522
9523SLICK_LOGGER_NOINLINE inline detail::producer_ring* Logger::attach_thread_ring(detail::thread_ring_tls& tls) noexcept {
9524 const uint64_t generation = ring_generation_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
9525#if SLICK_LOGGER_ENABLE_THREAD_ID
9526 const uint32_t thread_id = detail::current_thread_id();
9527#else
9528 const uint32_t thread_id = 0;
9529#endif
9530 // No ring when the registry is full: the thread then stays on the shared path
9531 // for the rest of the run, from every module, so its entries never split
9532 // across two sources.
9533 const uint32_t index = claim_thread_ring(generation);
9534 detail::thread_ring_slot* const slot = index == kNoSlot ? nullptr : &ring_slots_[index];
9535 detail::producer_ring* const ring = slot ? slot->ring.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) : nullptr;
9536 const uint64_t ticket = slot ? slot->ticket.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) : 0;
9537 tls = {this, generation, ring, slot, ticket, thread_id};
9538 return ring;
9539}
9540
9541inline uint32_t Logger::claim_thread_ring(uint64_t generation) noexcept {
9542 using slot_t = detail::thread_ring_slot;
9543 slot_t* const slots = ring_slots_.get();
9544 const uint64_t me = detail::os_thread_id();
9545 // This thread may hold a slot already, claimed from another module: the host,
9546 // or a plugin logging through this Logger. Reusing it keeps the thread's
9547 // entries in one order. If that module unloaded, its exit hook orphaned the
9548 // slot while the thread lives on: take it back unless another thread got
9549 // there first.
9550 const uint32_t used = ring_slots_used_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
9551 for (uint32_t i = 0; i < used; ++i) {
9552 if (slots[i].owner.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) != me) {
9553 continue;
9554 }
9555 uint32_t state = slots[i].state.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
9556 if (state == slot_t::kActive) {
9557 return i;
9558 }
9559 if (state == slot_t::kOrphaned &&
9560 slots[i].state.compare_exchange_strong(state, slot_t::kClaimed, std::memory_order_acquire,
9561 std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
9562 return activate_slot(i, generation, false); // spills still pending stay ordered
9563 }
9564 }
9565 // Sent to the shared rings already, maybe from another module: a ring now would
9566 // put this thread's entries in two sources, where they can come out reordered.
9567 for (const detail::ring_fallback* node = ring_fallbacks_.load(std::memory_order_acquire); node;
9568 node = node->next) {
9569 if (node->owner == me) {
9570 return kNoSlot;
9571 }
9572 }
9573 for (uint32_t i = 0; i < max_thread_rings_; ++i) {
9574 uint32_t expected = slots[i].state.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
9575 if (expected == slot_t::kOrphaned) {
9576 // Its thread exited. Take it over once drained, rather than wait for a
9577 // parked writer to notice: positions carry on, so the writer needs no reset.
9578 const detail::producer_ring* old = slots[i].ring.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
9579 if (old->written() != old->released()) {
9580 continue;
9581 }
9582 } else if (expected != slot_t::kFree) {
9583 continue;
9584 }
9585 if (!slots[i].state.compare_exchange_strong(expected, slot_t::kClaimed, std::memory_order_acquire,
9586 std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
9587 continue;
9588 }
9589 if (!slots[i].ring.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
9590 try {
9591 // Not pre-faulted: a claim on a log call must stay cheap, and a ring
9592 // only costs what it is filled to. prepare_thread() faults it in.
9593 slots[i].ring.store(detail::producer_ring::allocate(thread_ring_size_, false).release(),
9594 std::memory_order_release);
9595 } catch (...) {
9596 slots[i].state.store(slot_t::kFree, std::memory_order_release);
9597 return fall_back(me);
9598 }
9599 }
9600 slots[i].owner.store(me, std::memory_order_relaxed);
9601 uint32_t seen = ring_slots_used_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
9602 while (seen <= i && !ring_slots_used_.compare_exchange_weak(seen, i + 1, std::memory_order_release,
9603 std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
9604 }
9605 return activate_slot(i, generation, true);
9606 }
9607 return fall_back(me);
9608}
9609
9610inline uint32_t Logger::fall_back(uint64_t owner) noexcept {
9611 // Once per thread per run. A thread that later reuses the id inherits the
9612 // decision, which costs it speed, never order.
9613 if (auto* node = new (std::nothrow) detail::ring_fallback{owner, ring_fallbacks_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)}) {
9614 while (!ring_fallbacks_.compare_exchange_weak(node->next, node, std::memory_order_release,
9615 std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
9616 }
9617 }
9618 return kNoSlot;
9619}
9620
9621inline uint32_t Logger::activate_slot(uint32_t index, uint64_t generation, bool new_owner) noexcept {
9622 detail::thread_ring_slot& slot = ring_slots_[index];
9623 if (new_owner) {
9624 slot.spill_end = 0; // a previous owner's spills need not be ordered against this thread's entries
9625 }
9626 // Set up by the claiming module only, so the slot is orphaned once. The hook
9627 // holds only the latest claim: a thread that logs through two Loggers keeps
9628 // the other slot until that Logger shuts down.
9629 detail::thread_ring_exit& exit_hook = detail::tls_thread_ring_exit;
9630 exit_hook.slot = &slot;
9631 exit_hook.generation_source = &ring_generation_;
9632 exit_hook.generation = generation;
9633 slot.ticket.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed); // stale for every module that cached the old one
9634 slot.state.store(detail::thread_ring_slot::kActive, std::memory_order_release);
9635 return index;
9636}
9637
9638template<typename T>
9639inline size_t Logger::stage_argument(LogArgument& arg, T&& value) {
9640 using DecayedT = std::decay_t<T>;
9641 using BareT = std::remove_reference_t<T>;
9642 if constexpr (!detail::is_copied_string_v<T>) {
9643 enqueue_argument(arg, std::forward<T>(value)); // scalars and pointers never touch the string ring
9644 return 0;
9645 } else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<DecayedT, BinaryView>) {
9646 arg.type = ArgType::BLOB;
9647 return stage_bytes(arg.value.dynamic_str, reinterpret_cast<const char*>(value.data), value.size, false);
9648 } else if constexpr (std::is_array_v<BareT>) {
9649 const char* data = const_cast<const char*>(static_cast<const volatile char*>(value));
9650 arg.type = ArgType::STRING_DYNAMIC;
9651 return stage_bytes(arg.value.dynamic_str, data, strnlen(data, std::extent_v<BareT>), true);
9652 } else if constexpr (std::is_pointer_v<DecayedT>) {
9653 arg.type = ArgType::STRING_DYNAMIC;
9654 return stage_bytes(arg.value.dynamic_str, value, std::strlen(value), true);
9655 } else {
9656 arg.type = ArgType::STRING_DYNAMIC; // std::string, std::string_view
9657 return stage_bytes(arg.value.dynamic_str, value.data(), value.size(), true);
9658 }
9659}
9660
9661inline size_t Logger::stage_static_strings(StringRef& file, bool& copy_file, StringRef& format,
9662 uint8_t& flags) noexcept {
9663 // A static file name or literal format lives in this module's image, which
9664 // the collector process cannot read: copy them too.
9665 size_t bytes = 0;
9666 if ((flags & kEntryHasSourceLocation) && !copy_file) {
9667 bytes += stage_bytes(file, file.ptr, file.length ? file.length : std::strlen(file.ptr), true);
9668 copy_file = true;
9669 }
9670 if (flags & kEntryStaticFormat) {
9671 bytes += stage_bytes(format, format.ptr, format.length, true);
9672 flags = static_cast<uint8_t>(flags & ~kEntryStaticFormat);
9673 }
9674 return bytes;
9675}
9676
9677inline size_t Logger::stage_bytes(StringRef& ref, const char* data, size_t size, bool terminate) noexcept {
9678 // Same rules as store_bytes_in_queue(): truncated, and empty points at a literal.
9679 const uint32_t length = static_cast<uint32_t>(std::min<size_t>(size, kMaxPayloadBytes));
9680 if (length == 0) {
9681 ref = StringRef{"", 0};
9682 return 0;
9683 }
9684 ref.ptr = data;
9685 ref.length = length;
9686 return length + (terminate ? 1 : 0);
9687}
9688
9689inline void Logger::copy_staged(char*& out, StringRef& ref, bool terminate) noexcept {
9690 if (ref.length == 0) {
9691 return;
9692 }
9693 std::memcpy(out, ref.ptr, ref.length);
9694 ref.ptr = out;
9695 out += ref.length;
9696 if (terminate) {
9697 *out++ = '\0';
9698 }
9699}
9700
9701template<typename T>
9702inline void Logger::enqueue_argument(LogArgument& arg, T&& value) {
9703 using DecayedT = std::decay_t<T>;
9704 using BareT = std::remove_reference_t<T>;
9705
9706 if constexpr (std::is_same_v<DecayedT, bool>) {
9707 arg.type = ArgType::BOOL;
9708 arg.value.b = value;
9709 }
9710 else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<DecayedT, char>) {
9711 arg.type = ArgType::CHAR;
9712 arg.value.c = value;
9713 }
9714 else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<DecayedT, unsigned char>) {
9715 arg.type = ArgType::U_CHAR;
9716 arg.value.uc = value;
9717 }
9718 else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<DecayedT, wchar_t>) {
9719 arg.type = ArgType::WCHAR;
9720 arg.value.wc = value;
9721 }
9722 else if constexpr (std::is_integral_v<DecayedT>) {
9723 switch (sizeof(DecayedT)) {
9724 case sizeof(int8_t):
9725 if (std::is_signed_v<DecayedT>) {
9726 arg.type = ArgType::INT8_T;
9727 arg.value.i8 = static_cast<int8_t>(value);
9728 } else {
9729 arg.type = ArgType::UINT8_T;
9730 arg.value.u8 = static_cast<uint8_t>(value);
9731 }
9732 return;
9733 case sizeof(int16_t):
9734 if (std::is_signed_v<DecayedT>) {
9735 arg.type = ArgType::INT16_T;
9736 arg.value.i16 = static_cast<int16_t>(value);
9737 } else {
9738 arg.type = ArgType::UINT16_T;
9739 arg.value.u16 = static_cast<uint16_t>(value);
9740 }
9741 return;
9742 case sizeof(int32_t):
9743 if (std::is_signed_v<DecayedT>) {
9744 arg.type = ArgType::INT32_T;
9745 arg.value.i32 = static_cast<int32_t>(value);
9746 } else {
9747 arg.type = ArgType::UINT32_T;
9748 arg.value.u32 = static_cast<uint32_t>(value);
9749 }
9750 return;
9751 case sizeof(int64_t):
9752 if (std::is_signed_v<DecayedT>) {
9753 arg.type = ArgType::INT64_T;
9754 arg.value.i64 = static_cast<int64_t>(value);
9755 } else {
9756 arg.type = ArgType::UINT64_T;
9757 arg.value.u64 = static_cast<uint64_t>(value);
9758 }
9759 return;
9760 default:
9761 // larger integral types: convert to string
9762 arg.type = ArgType::STRING_DYNAMIC;
9763 arg.value.dynamic_str = store_string_in_queue(std::to_string(value));
9764 return;
9765 }
9766 }
9767 else if constexpr (std::is_floating_point_v<DecayedT>) {
9768 // Every floating type gets a case: long double is 16 bytes on GCC and
9769 // clang for x86, where a switch on 4 and 8 left it untyped. Wider than a
9770 // double is kept as a double, the widest a LogArgument holds, as the
9771 // std::format_args path does for __float128.
9772 if constexpr (sizeof(DecayedT) <= sizeof(float)) {
9773 arg.type = ArgType::FLOAT;
9774 arg.value.f = static_cast<float>(value);
9775 } else {
9776 arg.type = ArgType::DOUBLE;
9777 arg.value.d = static_cast<double>(value);
9778 }
9779 }
9780 else if constexpr (std::is_enum_v<DecayedT>) {
9781 enqueue_argument(arg, static_cast<std::underlying_type_t<DecayedT>>(value));
9782 }
9783 else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<DecayedT, std::chrono::system_clock::time_point>) {
9784 arg.type = ArgType::INT64_T;
9785 arg.value.i64 = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(value.time_since_epoch()).count();
9786 }
9787 else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<DecayedT, BinaryView>) {
9788 // Raw bytes: copied into the string ring like any other dynamic payload,
9789 // but without a terminator. The stored length is what makes them readable
9790 // back, since embedded NULs are legitimate payload. Stored even when empty
9791 // so shared-memory entries always carry a resolvable ring index rather
9792 // than a null pointer.
9793 arg.type = ArgType::BLOB;
9794 arg.value.dynamic_str = store_binary_in_queue(value);
9795 }
9796 else if constexpr (std::is_array_v<BareT> &&
9797 std::is_same_v<std::remove_cv_t<std::remove_extent_t<BareT>>, char>) {
9798 // value may be cv-qualified (e.g. a volatile struct member); strip
9799 // qualifiers for the read since we only need a defensive snapshot.
9800 const char* data = const_cast<const char*>(static_cast<const volatile char*>(value));
9801 constexpr size_t extent = std::extent_v<BareT>;
9802 size_t length = strnlen(data, extent);
9803 arg.type = ArgType::STRING_DYNAMIC;
9804 arg.value.dynamic_str = store_string_in_queue(std::string_view{data, length});
9805 }
9806 else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<DecayedT, const char*>) {
9807 arg.type = ArgType::STRING_DYNAMIC;
9808 arg.value.dynamic_str = store_string_in_queue(value);
9809 }
9810 else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<DecayedT, char*>) {
9811 arg.type = ArgType::STRING_DYNAMIC;
9812 arg.value.dynamic_str = store_string_in_queue(value);
9813 }
9814 else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<DecayedT, std::string>) {
9815 // Dynamic string: copy to the string queue
9816 arg.type = ArgType::STRING_DYNAMIC;
9817 arg.value.dynamic_str = store_string_in_queue(value);
9818 }
9819 else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<DecayedT, std::string_view>) {
9820 // May view a literal or a temporary, with no way to tell, so copy it
9821 arg.type = ArgType::STRING_DYNAMIC;
9822 arg.value.dynamic_str = store_string_in_queue(value);
9823 }
9824 else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<DecayedT, const void*>) {
9825 arg.type = ArgType::PTR;
9826 arg.value.ptr = const_cast<void*>(value);
9827 }
9828 else if constexpr (std::is_pointer_v<DecayedT>) {
9829 arg.type = ArgType::PTR;
9830 // Strip any cv-qualification on the pointee; we only store the
9831 // address, never dereference it, so const/volatile don't matter.
9832 arg.value.ptr = const_cast<void*>(static_cast<const volatile void*>(value));
9833 }
9834 else {
9835 // Custom type: convert to string
9836 arg.type = ArgType::STRING_DYNAMIC;
9837 arg.value.dynamic_str = store_string_in_queue(std::to_string(value));
9838 }
9839}
9840
9841inline StringRef Logger::store_bytes_in_queue(const char* data, size_t size, bool terminate) {
9842 // slick-queue packs the reservation size into 16 bits, so an over-long
9843 // reservation would corrupt the write cursor. Truncate instead.
9844 uint32_t length = static_cast<uint32_t>(std::min<size_t>(size, kMaxPayloadBytes));
9845 const bool use_offsets = (entry_flags_ & kEntryOffsets) != 0;
9846 if (length == 0 && !use_offsets) {
9847 // Nothing to copy, and a length of 0 sends view_string_ref() scanning for
9848 // the NUL, which a lapping producer can overwrite in a ring slot. A
9849 // literal's NUL cannot be overwritten.
9850 return StringRef{"", 0};
9851 }
9852 // slick-queue rejects a zero-size reservation, so in shared mode an empty
9853 // unterminated payload still claims one byte. That keeps the invariant the
9854 // collector depends on (a stored reference always resolves to a real ring
9855 // slot) at the cost of one byte in a case that carries no data anyway.
9856 uint32_t reserved = std::max(1u, length + (terminate ? 1u : 0u));
9857
9858 uint64_t start_index = string_queue_->reserve(reserved);
9859
9860 char* dest = (*string_queue_)[start_index];
9861 if (length) {
9862 std::memcpy(dest, data, length);
9863 }
9864 if (terminate) {
9865 // Copy only the payload, then terminate explicitly.
9866 dest[length] = '\0';
9867 }
9868 string_queue_->publish(start_index, reserved);
9869
9870 StringRef ref;
9871 if (use_offsets) {
9872 // Shared memory: hand out the ring index, which every attached process
9873 // can resolve against its own mapping. Tagged, so a ring record holding
9874 // it among addresses still tells it apart; the ring masks the tag off.
9875 ref.offset = start_index | detail::kStringRingRef;
9876 }
9877 else {
9878 ref.ptr = dest;
9879 }
9880 ref.length = length;
9881 return ref;
9882}
9883
9884inline StringRef Logger::store_string_in_queue(std::string_view str) {
9885 // Strings are terminated: readers reach them through view_string_ref(), where
9886 // a length of 0 means "NUL-terminated, length unknown".
9887 return store_bytes_in_queue(str.data(), str.length(), true);
9888}
9889
9890inline StringRef Logger::store_binary_in_queue(BinaryView payload) {
9891 // Binary payloads are not terminated. view_binary() treats the stored length
9892 // as authoritative (a payload can contain NUL bytes, so a terminator would
9893 // mean nothing to a reader), and skipping it saves a byte of ring space and
9894 // a store per binary argument.
9895 return store_bytes_in_queue(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(payload.data), payload.size, false);
9896}
9897
9898inline uint8_t Logger::enqueue_format_args(LogArgument* out, std::format_args fa) {
9899 return unpack_format_args(out, fa, [this](LogArgument& arg, auto&& value) {
9900 enqueue_argument(arg, std::forward<decltype(value)>(value));
9901 });
9902}
9903
9904template<typename Put>
9905inline uint8_t Logger::unpack_format_args(LogArgument* out, std::format_args fa, Put&& put) {
9906 size_t arg_idx = 0;
9907 while (arg_idx < SLICK_LOGGER_MAX_ARGS) {
9908 auto arg = fa.get(arg_idx);
9909 bool is_monostate = false;
9910 std::visit_format_arg([&]<typename T>(T&& v) {
9911 using DT = std::decay_t<T>;
9912 if constexpr (std::is_same_v<DT, std::monostate>) {
9913 is_monostate = true;
9914 } else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<DT, typename std::basic_format_arg<std::format_context>::handle>) {
9915 // Custom type via handle: std::format_context is not publicly
9916 // constructible, so store a placeholder instead.
9917 put(out[arg_idx], std::string_view{"<handle>"});
9918#ifdef __SIZEOF_INT128__
9919 } else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<DT, __int128>) {
9920 put(out[arg_idx], static_cast<long long>(v));
9921 } else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<DT, unsigned __int128>) {
9922 put(out[arg_idx], static_cast<unsigned long long>(v));
9923#endif
9924 } else if constexpr (is_float128_v<DT>) {
9925 put(out[arg_idx], static_cast<double>(v));
9926 } else {
9927 put(out[arg_idx], std::forward<T>(v));
9928 }
9929 }, arg);
9930 if (is_monostate) break;
9931 ++arg_idx;
9932 }
9933 return static_cast<uint8_t>(arg_idx);
9934}
9935
9936inline void Logger::shutdown(bool clear_sinks) {
9937 if (running_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
9938 if (registry_slot_ != kNoSlot) {
9939 // On Windows a producer's segment goes away with its last handle, so
9940 // give an attached collector a moment to take what is in it.
9941 wait_for_collector(std::chrono::milliseconds(1000));
9942 }
9943 running_.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
9944 // The writer thread may be parked. atomic::wait has no timeout, so it
9945 // only ever resumes because the token changed. Without this the join
9946 // below would block until something else happened to be logged.
9947 force_wake_writer();
9948 if (writer_thread_.joinable()) {
9949 writer_thread_.join();
9950 }
9951 // Must be joined before the queues are released below: the statistics
9952 // thread dereferences both of them on every tick. It notices running_
9953 // within one sample tick, so this never blocks for long.
9954 if (stats_thread_.joinable()) {
9955 stats_thread_.join();
9956 }
9957 }
9958 if (stats_stream_.is_open()) {
9959 stats_stream_.flush();
9960 stats_stream_.close();
9961 }
9962 stats_enabled_ = false;
9963 // Dropped here rather than only in reset(), because shutdown() is what turns
9964 // statistics off and stats_snapshot() documents a zeroed LogStats for a logger
9965 // with them disabled. Left in place, the last snapshot of a finished run would
9966 // stay readable afterwards and, since init() shuts down first, would resurface as
9967 // live-looking data after a re-init with statistics off, or after an init()
9968 // that threw out of open_stats_csv(). The statistics thread was joined above,
9969 // so nothing can publish a new snapshot over this one.
9970 stats_latest_.store(nullptr, std::memory_order_release);
9971 stats_file_.clear();
9972 stats_interval_ms_ = 0;
9973 stats_sample_interval_ms_ = 0;
9974 stats_max_file_size_ = 0;
9975
9976 if (clear_sinks) {
9977 // Release sinks to free file handles and other resources, and to detach
9978 // any handle the caller still holds. Safe here: the writer thread, the
9979 // only other user of sinks_, has been joined above.
9980 release_sinks();
9981 }
9982 // Destroying a shared queue only unmaps it: since slick-queue 2.3.0 no queue
9983 // shm_unlink()s its segment, not even the one that created it. Unlinking frees
9984 // the name while existing mappings stay valid, so a creator that unlinked on
9985 // exit would strand every process still attached: newcomers would create a
9986 // fresh segment under the same name and their entries would silently vanish.
9987 // The name therefore persists until removed (see the POSIX cleanup note in the
9988 // README), and this process's mapping is released here like any other.
9989 log_queue_.reset();
9990 string_queue_.reset();
9991 // Generation first: a thread-exit hook or a ring cached by a thread checks it
9992 // before touching the registry. The rings go with their slots.
9993 ring_generation_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_acq_rel);
9994 if (ring_in_shm_ && ring_slots_) {
9995 for (uint32_t i = 0; i < max_thread_rings_; ++i) {
9996 ring_slots_[i].ring.store(nullptr, std::memory_order_relaxed); // the segment's, not the slot's
9997 }
9998 }
9999 ring_views_.reset();
10000 ring_slots_.reset();
10001 ring_slots_used_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
10002 for (detail::ring_fallback* node = ring_fallbacks_.exchange(nullptr, std::memory_order_acq_rel); node;) {
10003 detail::ring_fallback* const next = node->next;
10004 delete node;
10005 node = next;
10006 }
10007 thread_rings_ = false;
10008 local_rings_ = false;
10009 close_registry();
10010 ring_in_shm_ = false;
10011 spill_route_base_ = 0;
10012 spill_route_shift_ = 0;
10013 spill_progress_ = &read_index_;
10014 string_epoch_ = &ring_string_epoch_;
10015 shared_head_ready_ = false;
10016 shared_gate_ring_ = nullptr;
10017 shared_gate_view_ = nullptr;
10018
10019 mode_ = QueueMode::Local;
10020 entry_flags_ = 0;
10021 pid_ = 0;
10022 std::memset(tag_, 0, sizeof(tag_));
10023 shm_name_.clear();
10024 collect_backlog_ = true;
10025 stalled_entry_timeout_ms_ = 0;
10026}
10027
10028inline Logger::~Logger() {
10029 shutdown();
10030}
10031
10032inline void Logger::flush() {
10033 if (!running_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) || !log_queue_) {
10034 return;
10035 }
10036 if (mode_ == QueueMode::SharedProducer) {
10037 // No local writer thread, and only the collector process can observe an
10038 // entry reaching a sink. With thread rings, wait for it to take
10039 // everything logged so far; without, publishing is all this process
10040 // can guarantee.
10041 if (registry_slot_ != kNoSlot) {
10042 wait_for_collector(std::chrono::milliseconds(0));
10043 }
10044 return;
10045 }
10046 // Snapshot the write cursor: any entry reserved before this point has
10047 // already been assigned an index below drain_target.
10048 const uint64_t drain_target = log_queue_->initial_reading_index();
10049 // Thread rings too: a record's space is released only once it was dispatched.
10050 std::vector<std::pair<const detail::producer_ring*, uint64_t>> ring_targets;
10051 if (thread_rings_) {
10052 const uint32_t used = ring_slots_used_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
10053 ring_targets.reserve(used);
10054 for (uint32_t i = 0; i < used; ++i) {
10055 if (const detail::producer_ring* ring = ring_slots_[i].ring.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
10056 ring_targets.emplace_back(ring, ring->written());
10057 }
10058 }
10059 }
10060 // Wait until the writer thread's read cursor reaches drain_target.
10061 force_wake_writer(); // the entries may have arrived while the writer was parked
10062 wait_until_ready([&] {
10063 for (const auto& [ring, target] : ring_targets) {
10064 if (ring->released() < target) {
10065 return false;
10066 }
10067 }
10068 return read_index_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) >= drain_target;
10069 });
10070
10071 // Consuming an entry only hands it to a sink; the sink may still be holding it
10072 // in a stream buffer. Ask the writer thread, the only thread allowed to touch
10073 // the sinks, to flush, and wait for it to acknowledge this request.
10074 const uint64_t generation = flush_request_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_acq_rel) + 1;
10075 force_wake_writer(); // it may be parked, and would not see the request otherwise
10076 wait_until_ready([&] { return flush_done_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) >= generation; });
10077}
10078
10079inline void Logger::reset() {
10080 shutdown();
10081 // Reset all state for fresh initialization
10082 log_file_.clear();
10083 read_index_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
10084 log_level_.store(LogLevel::L_TRACE);
10085 source_location_options_.store(kSourceLocationEnabled, std::memory_order_relaxed);
10086 // Cleared for the same reason as log_level_ above. init(config) treats an
10087 // empty config.pattern as "leave the current default alone", so a pattern
10088 // surviving reset() would silently reappear on sinks registered by the next
10089 // init(), which is the cross-contamination reset() exists to avoid.
10090 default_pattern_ = nullptr;
10091 // Back to system_clock, for the same reason. Only here, never in shutdown():
10092 // the retired ones may be freed now because reset(), like the rest of this
10093 // function, presumes no thread is still logging.
10094 active_timestamper_.store(nullptr, std::memory_order_relaxed);
10095 timestamper_.reset();
10096 retired_timestampers_.clear();
10097
10098 // shutdown() has joined the writer thread, so nothing else can be touching the
10099 // wake and flush state by now. None of this is required for correctness: the
10100 // counters are monotonic, the writer compares flush_request_ against
10101 // flush_done_ for inequality rather than order (so it resynchronises on its
10102 // first iteration whatever they hold), and wake_token_ is only ever compared
10103 // for change. Clearing them simply leaves a reused Logger indistinguishable
10104 // from a fresh one, which makes init()/reset() cycles easier to reason about.
10105 // Keep flush_request_ and flush_done_ together all the same, so the
10106 // flush_done_ <= flush_request_ invariant is obvious at a glance.
10107 flush_request_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
10108 flush_done_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
10109 wake_token_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
10110 writer_parked_.store(false, std::memory_order_relaxed);
10111
10112 // Same reasoning: shutdown() above joined the statistics thread, so nothing
10113 // else can be touching any of this, and clearing it leaves a reused Logger
10114 // indistinguishable from a fresh one. The published snapshot is not among
10115 // them: shutdown() drops that itself, so it is gone for every caller, not
10116 // just the ones that go on to reset().
10117 stats_previous_ = LogStats{};
10118 stats_has_previous_ = false;
10119 stats_string_frontier_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
10120 stats_gen_entry_ = 0;
10121 stats_gen_string_ = 0;
10122 stats_gen_open_ = false;
10123 stats_gen_rings_.clear();
10124 stats_seen_epoch_ = UINT64_MAX;
10125 stats_depth_max_ = 0;
10126 stats_depth_sum_ = 0;
10127 stats_sample_count_ = 0;
10128 stats_string_inflight_max_ = 0;
10129 stats_string_last_ = 0;
10130 stats_string_seen_ = false;
10131 stats_bytes_written_ = 0;
10132 stats_write_failed_ = false;
10133}
10134
10135inline Logger::DrainResult Logger::drain_pending() {
10136 if (thread_rings_ || registry_) { // a collector reads producer processes' rings
10137 return drain_sources();
10138 }
10139 // read() takes a plain uint64_t& and advances it in place. The atomic must
10140 // not be passed directly: queue also has a read(std::atomic<uint64_t>&)
10141 // overload for multiple consumers sharing one cursor, and binding that by
10142 // accident would change how slots are claimed. So the cursor is round-tripped
10143 // through a local and republished at exactly the point read() used to move it.
10144 uint64_t cursor = read_index_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
10145 auto [entry_ptr, count] = log_queue_->read(cursor);
10146 read_index_.store(cursor, std::memory_order_relaxed);
10147
10148 if (entry_ptr && count) {
10149 // read() leaves the cursor just past what it returned, and every entry is
10150 // reserved as exactly one slot.
10151 if (snapshot_entry(entry_scratch_, *entry_ptr, cursor - 1)) {
10152 dispatch_entry(entry_scratch_);
10153 }
10154
10155 if (stats_enabled_ && string_queue_) {
10156 // Placed after the dispatch: the promotion below means "the writer is
10157 // done with everything under this position", which is only true once
10158 // the batch has actually been written.
10159 advance_string_frontier();
10160 }
10161 stalled_since_ = {};
10162 return DrainResult::Wrote;
10163 }
10164
10165 // A producer process killed between reserve() and publish() leaves a hole that
10166 // read() will never return, stalling every entry behind it. Only shared queues
10167 // can be orphaned this way, so the recovery is scoped to the collector role.
10168 const bool recover_stalls = (mode_ == QueueMode::SharedCollector) && stalled_entry_timeout_ms_ > 0;
10169 if (!recover_stalls || log_queue_->initial_reading_index() <= cursor) {
10170 stalled_since_ = {};
10171 return DrainResult::Idle;
10172 }
10173
10174 // Entries are reserved ahead of us but this slot never got published.
10175 const auto now = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
10176 if (stalled_since_ == std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point{}) {
10177 stalled_since_ = now;
10178 return DrainResult::WaitingOnStall;
10179 }
10180 if (now - stalled_since_ < std::chrono::milliseconds(stalled_entry_timeout_ms_)) {
10181 return DrainResult::WaitingOnStall;
10182 }
10183
10184 read_index_.store(cursor + 1, std::memory_order_relaxed); // abandon the stalled slot
10185 stalled_since_ = {};
10186 return DrainResult::SkippedStalled;
10187}
10188
10189inline Logger::DrainResult Logger::drain_sources() {
10190 // The shared queue holds the threads past max_thread_rings and spills from
10191 // full rings. read_index_ stays on a held entry until it is dispatched, so
10192 // flush(), park_writer() and spilling threads still see it as pending.
10193 if (!shared_head_ready_) {
10194 load_shared_head();
10195 }
10196 // A spilled entry waiting on its ring is left out of the merge until then,
10197 // and whatever queued behind it waits with it. That ring skips its poll
10198 // interval meanwhile, or the writer would idle on records it is not reading.
10199 const bool shared_open = shared_head_ready_ && shared_head_released();
10200 const detail::ring_view* const urgent = shared_head_ready_ && !shared_open ? shared_gate_view_ : nullptr;
10201
10202 // Each source is in order, so the oldest entry overall is the oldest head.
10203 int64_t now_ns = INT64_MIN; // read once, only if a ring needs it
10204 bool polling = false;
10205 // A source is compared only once there is one: UINT64_MAX is a timestamp
10206 // like any other, so it cannot double as "none yet".
10207 detail::ring_view* best = nullptr;
10208 uint64_t best_ts = UINT64_MAX;
10209 uint64_t next_ts = UINT64_MAX; // the oldest head of every other source, if any
10210 const auto consider = [&](detail::ring_view& view, detail::thread_ring_slot* slot) {
10211 if (!view.head && !load_ring_head(view, slot, &view == urgent, now_ns, polling)) {
10212 return;
10213 }
10214 if (!best || view.head_timestamp < best_ts) {
10215 next_ts = best_ts;
10216 best_ts = view.head_timestamp;
10217 best = &view;
10218 } else if (view.head_timestamp < next_ts) {
10219 next_ts = view.head_timestamp;
10220 }
10221 };
10222 const uint32_t used = ring_slots_used_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
10223 for (uint32_t i = 0; i < used; ++i) {
10224 consider(ring_views_[i], &ring_slots_[i]);
10225 }
10226 for (detail::ring_view* view : remote_views_) {
10227 consider(*view, nullptr);
10228 }
10229
10230 if (shared_open) {
10231 if (!best || shared_head_.timestamp < best_ts) {
10232 // A run from the shared queue, until a ring's head is older. Under
10233 // overload most entries are spills, so this is most of the work.
10234 do {
10235 dispatch_entry(shared_head_);
10236 shared_head_ready_ = false;
10237 read_index_.store(shared_cursor_, std::memory_order_relaxed);
10238 if (stats_enabled_ && string_queue_) {
10239 advance_string_frontier();
10240 }
10241 } while (load_shared_head() && shared_head_released() && (!best || shared_head_.timestamp < best_ts));
10242 publish_shared_cursor();
10243 return DrainResult::Wrote;
10244 }
10245 const uint64_t shared_ts = shared_head_.timestamp; // LogEntry is packed: no reference to its fields
10246 next_ts = std::min(next_ts, shared_ts);
10247 }
10248 // A hole a dead producer process left in the shared queue blocks it, never the rings.
10249 const DrainResult stall = !shared_head_ready_ && mode_ == QueueMode::SharedCollector ? shared_queue_stall()
10250 : DrainResult::Idle;
10251 if (stall == DrainResult::SkippedStalled) {
10252 return stall;
10253 }
10254 if (!best) {
10255 return polling ? DrainResult::Polling : stall;
10256 }
10257 // A run from the oldest ring, until another source's head is older.
10258 do {
10259 dispatch_ring_head(*best);
10260 } while (best->head && best->head_timestamp <= next_ts);
10261 // A ring run moves the frontier only when a ring record has strings in the
10262 // string ring: a mark is pending, or one was raised since the last look.
10263 if (stats_enabled_ && string_queue_ &&
10264 (!stats_gen_rings_.empty() || string_epoch_->load(std::memory_order_relaxed) != stats_seen_epoch_)) {
10265 advance_string_frontier();
10266 }
10267 return DrainResult::Wrote;
10268}
10269
10270inline bool Logger::load_shared_head() {
10271 auto [entry_ptr, count] = log_queue_->read(shared_cursor_);
10272 if (entry_ptr && count) {
10273 shared_head_ready_ = snapshot_entry(shared_head_, *entry_ptr, shared_cursor_ - 1);
10274 stalled_since_ = {};
10275 shared_gate_ring_ = nullptr;
10276 shared_gate_view_ = nullptr;
10277 if (shared_head_ready_ && (shared_head_.flags & kEntrySpilled)) {
10278 resolve_spill();
10279 }
10280 }
10281 // Stored only when it moved: spilling threads poll this line.
10282 if (!shared_head_ready_ && read_index_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) != shared_cursor_) {
10283 read_index_.store(shared_cursor_, std::memory_order_relaxed);
10284 publish_shared_cursor();
10285 }
10286 return shared_head_ready_;
10287}
10288
10289inline void Logger::resolve_spill() {
10290 shared_head_.flags = static_cast<uint8_t>(shared_head_.flags & ~kEntrySpilled);
10291 if (!remote_) {
10292 // Local mode: the route is the thread's slot, in pid.
10293 const uint32_t route = shared_head_.pid;
10294 shared_head_.pid = 0;
10295 if (ring_slots_ && route < max_thread_rings_) {
10296 shared_gate_ring_ = ring_slots_[route].ring.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
10297 shared_gate_view_ = &ring_views_[route];
10298 }
10299 return;
10300 }
10301 // A producer process: the route holds registry slot, ring and generation.
10302 // The entry's pid is already the producer's.
10303 const uint32_t route = spilled_route_;
10304 const uint32_t index = route & (detail::shm_registry::kSlotCount - 1);
10305 const uint32_t ring = (route >> detail::kRouteSlotBits) & (detail::shm_ring_segment::kMaxRings - 1);
10306 const uint32_t generation = route >> (detail::kRouteSlotBits + detail::kRouteRingBits);
10307 detail::remote_producer& producer = remote_[index];
10308 if (!producer.views) {
10309 // Spilled before the collector's next look: its ring records come first.
10310 attach_producer(index, false);
10311 }
10312 if (producer.views && (producer.generation & detail::kRouteGenerationMask) == generation &&
10313 ring < producer.ring_count) {
10314 shared_gate_view_ = &producer.views[ring];
10315 shared_gate_ring_ = shared_gate_view_->ring;
10316 }
10317 // Otherwise the producer is gone, and it was drained before it went, so
10318 // there is nothing to wait for.
10319}
10320
10321inline Logger::DrainResult Logger::shared_queue_stall() {
10322 // A producer process killed between reserve() and publish() leaves a hole that
10323 // read() will never return, stalling every entry behind it.
10324 if (stalled_entry_timeout_ms_ == 0 || log_queue_->initial_reading_index() <= shared_cursor_) {
10325 stalled_since_ = {};
10326 return DrainResult::Idle;
10327 }
10328 const auto now = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
10329 if (stalled_since_ == std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point{}) {
10330 stalled_since_ = now;
10331 return DrainResult::WaitingOnStall;
10332 }
10333 if (now - stalled_since_ < std::chrono::milliseconds(stalled_entry_timeout_ms_)) {
10334 return DrainResult::WaitingOnStall;
10335 }
10336 read_index_.store(++shared_cursor_, std::memory_order_relaxed); // abandon the stalled slot
10337 publish_shared_cursor();
10338 stalled_since_ = {};
10339 return DrainResult::SkippedStalled;
10340}
10341
10342inline void Logger::publish_shared_cursor() noexcept {
10343 if (registry_) {
10344 registry_->read_index.store(read_index_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed), std::memory_order_release);
10345 }
10346}
10347
10348inline bool Logger::load_ring_head(detail::ring_view& view, detail::thread_ring_slot* slot, bool urgent,
10349 int64_t& now_ns, bool& polling) {
10350 using slot_t = detail::thread_ring_slot;
10351 const auto now = [&now_ns]() noexcept {
10352 if (now_ns == INT64_MIN) {
10353 now_ns = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(
10354 std::chrono::steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch()).count();
10355 }
10356 return now_ns;
10357 };
10358 if (!view.ring || view.reader.batch_done()) {
10359 uint32_t state = slot_t::kActive; // a producer process's rings are set up when attached
10360 if (slot) {
10361 state = slot->state.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
10362 if (state < slot_t::kActive) {
10363 return false; // free, or a thread is still setting it up
10364 }
10365 if (!view.ring) {
10366 // A slot keeps its ring for every later thread, so this happens once.
10367 view.ring = slot->ring.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
10368 view.reader = detail::ring_reader(*view.ring);
10369 }
10370 }
10371 // Right after a non-empty batch the producer is likely still writing:
10372 // leave its lines alone for the poll interval, unless a spill waits on it.
10373 if (view.gated && !urgent && now() - view.last_poll_ns < ring_poll_interval_ns_) {
10374 polling = true;
10375 return false;
10376 }
10377 if (!view.reader.refresh()) {
10378 view.gated = false;
10379 if (state == slot_t::kOrphaned) {
10380 // Drained: free it for the next thread, unless one already took it over.
10381 uint32_t expected = slot_t::kOrphaned;
10382 slot->state.compare_exchange_strong(expected, slot_t::kFree, std::memory_order_release,
10383 std::memory_order_relaxed);
10384 }
10385 return false;
10386 }
10387 if (ring_poll_interval_ns_ > 0) {
10388 view.gated = true;
10389 view.last_poll_ns = now();
10390 }
10391 }
10392 return view.hold_next();
10393}
10394
10395inline void Logger::dispatch_ring_head(detail::ring_view& view) {
10396 constexpr size_t kHeader = detail::kEntryHeaderBytes;
10397 if (view.head_size >= kHeader) {
10398 // Sinks get a full LogEntry they can copy, never the shorter record.
10399 uint8_t arg_count;
10400 std::memcpy(&arg_count, view.head + offsetof(LogEntry, arg_count), 1);
10401 arg_count = static_cast<uint8_t>(std::min<size_t>(
10402 {arg_count, (view.head_size - kHeader) / sizeof(LogArgument), SLICK_LOGGER_MAX_ARGS}));
10403 LogEntry& copy = entry_scratch_;
10404 std::memcpy(static_cast<void*>(&copy), view.head, kHeader + arg_count * sizeof(LogArgument));
10405 copy.arg_count = arg_count;
10406 if (view.remote) {
10407 resolve_remote_record(copy, view);
10408 }
10409 dispatch_entry(copy);
10410 }
10411 // Strings live in the record, so its space goes back only now.
10412 view.head = nullptr;
10413 view.reader.pop();
10414 view.reader.release();
10415 if (!view.reader.batch_done()) {
10416 view.hold_next();
10417 }
10418}
10419
10420inline void Logger::resolve_remote_record(LogEntry& entry, const detail::ring_view& view) const noexcept {
10421 // The producer wrote addresses in its own mapping of the segment. Shifted into
10422 // this one, each must still lie inside its record, or it is dropped unread.
10423 const uintptr_t begin = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(view.head);
10424 const uintptr_t end = begin + view.head_size;
10425 const auto resolve = [&](StringRef& ref) noexcept {
10426 if (ref.length == 0) {
10427 ref.ptr = "";
10428 return;
10429 }
10430 const uint64_t value = ref.offset;
10431 if (value & detail::kStringRingRef) {
10432 ref.ptr = (*string_queue_)[value]; // too big for the ring, so in the shared string ring
10433 return;
10434 }
10435 const uintptr_t at = static_cast<uintptr_t>(value) + view.delta;
10436 if (at < begin || at > end || end - at < ref.length) {
10437 ref.ptr = "";
10438 ref.length = 0;
10439 return;
10440 }
10441 ref.ptr = reinterpret_cast<const char*>(at);
10442 };
10443 resolve(entry.format);
10444 if (entry.flags & kEntryHasSourceLocation) {
10445 resolve(entry.file);
10446 }
10447 for (uint8_t i = 0; i < entry.arg_count; ++i) {
10448 LogArgument& arg = entry.args[i];
10449 if (arg.type == ArgType::STRING_DYNAMIC || arg.type == ArgType::STRING_LITERAL || arg.type == ArgType::BLOB) {
10450 resolve(arg.value.dynamic_str);
10451 }
10452 }
10453 entry.flags = static_cast<uint8_t>(entry.flags & ~(kEntryOffsets | kEntryStaticFormat | kEntrySpilled));
10454}
10455
10456inline bool Logger::thread_rings_pending() const noexcept {
10457 if (shared_head_ready_) {
10458 return true;
10459 }
10460 const uint32_t used = ring_slots_used_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
10461 for (uint32_t i = 0; i < used; ++i) {
10462 const detail::producer_ring* ring = ring_slots_[i].ring.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
10463 if (ring && ring->written() != ring->released()) {
10464 return true;
10465 }
10466 }
10467 return false;
10468}
10469
10470inline bool Logger::shared_head_released() const noexcept {
10471 // Not a spill, or its ring is gone: nothing to wait for.
10472 return !shared_gate_ring_ || shared_gate_ring_->released() >= shared_gate_ring_->spill_gate();
10473}
10474
10475inline Logger::ring_totals Logger::thread_ring_totals() const noexcept {
10476 ring_totals totals;
10477 const uint32_t used = ring_slots_used_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
10478 for (uint32_t i = 0; i < used; ++i) {
10479 if (const detail::producer_ring* ring = ring_slots_[i].ring.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
10480 totals.consumed += ring->released_records(); // before records(), so depth never reads negative
10481 totals.produced += ring->records();
10482 totals.dropped += ring->drops();
10483 ++totals.rings;
10484 }
10485 }
10486 if (registry_) {
10487 // A collector's view of producer processes, refreshed by its writer.
10488 totals.consumed += remote_consumed_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
10489 totals.produced += remote_produced_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
10490 totals.dropped += remote_dropped_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
10491 totals.rings += remote_rings_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
10492 }
10493 return totals;
10494}
10495
10496inline void Logger::writer_thread_func() {
10497 stalled_since_ = {};
10498
10499 // Sinks are flushed when the queue runs dry, not after every batch. Flushing
10500 // per batch would mean one fflush per entry whenever the writer thread keeps
10501 // up with the producers, which costs far more than formatting the entry.
10502 // Draining to empty and then flushing keeps what callers can observe (once
10503 // the logger is caught up, everything logged is on disk) while letting a
10504 // burst share a single flush.
10505 bool sinks_dirty = false;
10506
10507 // Idle backoff. std::this_thread::sleep_for is not used here: Windows'
10508 // default timer resolution is ~15.6ms, so a "1ms" sleep parks the thread for
10509 // ~15.6ms and puts that much latency between a log call and the entry
10510 // reaching its sink. Instead the thread stays hot for a short burst, which
10511 // covers the gaps in an active logging stream, and then parks on wake_token_
10512 // until a producer, a flush request, or shutdown releases it.
10513 static constexpr uint32_t kIdleYieldLimit = 64;
10514 uint32_t idle_yields = 0;
10515
10516 // Parking only works when the producers share this process: writer_parked_
10517 // lives in this address space, and neither WaitOnAddress nor a futex on a
10518 // private mapping can be signalled by another process. A collector therefore
10519 // keeps polling for entries that cross a process boundary. mode_ is fixed
10520 // before this thread starts and does not change while it runs.
10521 const bool can_park = (mode_ == QueueMode::Local);
10522 // A collector also watches the registry for producer processes. Under load it
10523 // looks every kScanRuns runs, so the clock read stays off the per-run cost.
10524 const bool collector = registry_ != nullptr;
10525 constexpr uint32_t kScanRuns = 256;
10526 uint32_t runs = 0;
10527
10528 while (running_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
10529 // Read the request before flushing so a request arriving mid-flush is not
10530 // mistaken for one this flush already covered.
10531 const uint64_t flush_requested = flush_request_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
10532 if (flush_requested != flush_done_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) &&
10533 (!collector || remote_flush_ready(flush_requested))) {
10534 flush_sinks();
10535 sinks_dirty = false;
10536 flush_done_.store(flush_requested, std::memory_order_release);
10537 }
10538
10539 const DrainResult result = drain_pending();
10540 if (collector && (result != DrainResult::Wrote || ++runs == kScanRuns)) {
10541 runs = 0;
10542 poll_registry();
10543 }
10544 switch (result) {
10545 case DrainResult::Wrote:
10546 sinks_dirty = true;
10547 idle_yields = 0;
10548 break;
10549 case DrainResult::SkippedStalled:
10550 log(LogLevel::L_WARN, "SlickLogger: skipped an unpublished log entry, "
10551 "a producer process likely died mid-write");
10552 idle_yields = 0;
10553 break;
10554 case DrainResult::WaitingOnStall:
10555 // A dead producer's slot clears by timeout rather than by a wake-up,
10556 // so this must keep re-checking instead of parking. It is a rare,
10557 // multi-second path where the coarse sleep does no harm.
10558 if (sinks_dirty) {
10559 flush_sinks();
10560 sinks_dirty = false;
10561 }
10562 std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
10563 break;
10564 case DrainResult::Polling:
10565 // A busy ring is due again within microseconds. Spin: a yield can give
10566 // the core away for a whole scheduler quantum while the ring fills.
10567 for (int i = 0; i < 16; ++i) {
10568 detail::cpu_pause();
10569 }
10570 break;
10571 case DrainResult::Idle:
10572 if (sinks_dirty) {
10573 flush_sinks(); // caught up: make everything written so far visible
10574 sinks_dirty = false;
10575 }
10576 if (idle_yields < kIdleYieldLimit) {
10577 ++idle_yields;
10578 std::this_thread::yield();
10579 } else if (can_park) {
10580 park_writer();
10581 idle_yields = 0;
10582 } else {
10583 std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
10584 }
10585 break;
10586 }
10587 }
10588
10589 // Drain remaining messages after running_ becomes false. A hole must be
10590 // abandoned here too, not just waited out: entries published behind it are
10591 // still valid and would otherwise be lost on shutdown. Skipping cannot loop
10592 // forever because every skip advances read_index_ toward the write cursor.
10593 // Nothing is logged about a skip during the drain, because running_ is already
10594 // false and the entry could never be consumed.
10595 stalled_since_ = {};
10596 ring_poll_interval_ns_ = 0; // nothing left to protect: drain the rings straight through
10597 if (collector) {
10598 scan_registry(false); // producers that came or went since the last look
10599 }
10600 while (true) {
10601 const DrainResult result = drain_pending();
10602 if (result == DrainResult::Idle) {
10603 break;
10604 }
10605 if (result == DrainResult::WaitingOnStall) {
10606 std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
10607 }
10608 }
10609 if (collector) {
10610 scan_registry(false); // free the closing producers drained just now
10611 }
10612
10613 // The writer thread owns the sinks, so this final flush is the last chance to
10614 // get the drained entries onto disk before shutdown() joins and returns.
10615 flush_sinks();
10616 flush_done_.store(flush_request_.load(std::memory_order_acquire), std::memory_order_release);
10617}
10618
10619inline void Logger::rebase_entry(LogEntry& entry) const noexcept {
10620 // Every ring copy carries its true length, so 0 can only be an empty string.
10621 // It is pointed at a literal rather than at its slot: view_string_ref() takes
10622 // length 0 to mean "scan for the NUL", and a producer that laps the ring can
10623 // overwrite the one the slot held.
10624 const auto resolve = [this](StringRef& ref) noexcept {
10625 ref.ptr = ref.length ? (*string_queue_)[ref.offset] : "";
10626 };
10627 resolve(entry.format);
10628 if (entry.flags & kEntryHasSourceLocation) {
10629 resolve(entry.file);
10630 }
10631 for (uint8_t i = 0; i < entry.arg_count; ++i) {
10632 LogArgument& arg = entry.args[i];
10633 if (arg.type == ArgType::STRING_DYNAMIC || arg.type == ArgType::STRING_LITERAL ||
10634 arg.type == ArgType::BLOB) {
10635 resolve(arg.value.dynamic_str);
10636 }
10637 }
10638 // The format now sits in this process's ring, whatever the producer claimed.
10639 entry.flags &= static_cast<uint8_t>(~(kEntryOffsets | kEntryStaticFormat));
10640}
10641
10642inline bool Logger::snapshot_entry(LogEntry& copy, const LogEntry& slot, uint64_t index) {
10643 // The ring never blocks a producer, so one that has lapped the writer thread
10644 // can be rewriting this slot while it is read. Formatting the slot in place
10645 // can size a line from one entry and fill it from the next, overrunning the
10646 // line buffer. So the header and the arguments it claims are copied out, and
10647 // the copy is used only if it provably predates any rewrite.
10648 //
10649 // Copying memory another thread may be writing is the formal data race every
10650 // seqlock reader has; the check below is what decides whether to trust it.
10651 // Through void*: LogEntry's member initializers make it non-trivial to GCC,
10652 // but its bytes are what the ring holds, and copying them is the point.
10653 std::memcpy(static_cast<void*>(&copy), static_cast<const void*>(&slot), offsetof(LogEntry, args));
10654 // A torn header can claim any count, and nothing may index past args[].
10655 copy.arg_count = std::min<uint8_t>(copy.arg_count, SLICK_LOGGER_MAX_ARGS);
10656 std::memcpy(copy.args, slot.args, copy.arg_count * sizeof(LogArgument));
10657
10658 // Pairs with the release fence after reserve() in log_to_sink_with_location():
10659 // had the copy read anything a later producer wrote, that producer's
10660 // announcement would be visible below. The slot is next used by reservation
10661 // index + size(), so the copy is whole while nothing has reached it. In Local
10662 // mode the page cursor answers that at page granularity (an entry within a
10663 // page of being lapped is dropped a little early) without touching the line
10664 // producers reserve on; shared mode has only the reservation cursor itself.
10665 std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_acquire);
10666 const uint64_t next_use = index + log_queue_->size();
10667 const bool rewritten = mode_ == QueueMode::Local
10668 ? entry_page_cursor_.page.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) >= (next_use >> entry_page_shift_)
10669 : log_queue_->initial_reading_index() > next_use;
10670 if (rewritten) [[unlikely]] {
10671 if constexpr (kLossDetectionEnabled) {
10672 torn_entry_count_.store(torn_entry_count_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) + 1,
10673 std::memory_order_relaxed);
10674 }
10675 return false;
10676 }
10677 if ((copy.flags & kEntrySpilled) && remote_) {
10678 // A producer process's spill: its route is in the lengths' high halves.
10679 spilled_route_ = (copy.format.length >> 16) | (copy.file.length & 0xFFFF0000u);
10680 copy.format.length &= 0xFFFFu;
10681 copy.file.length &= 0xFFFFu;
10682 }
10683 if (copy.flags & kEntryOffsets) {
10684 // Came from shared memory: turn the ring indices into addresses valid
10685 // here, so sinks always see resolved pointers.
10686 rebase_entry(copy);
10687 }
10688 return true;
10689}
10690
10691inline void Logger::flush_sinks() {
10692 for (auto& sink : sinks_) {
10693 if (sink) {
10694 sink->flush();
10695 }
10696 }
10697}
10698
10699template<typename Predicate>
10700inline void Logger::wait_until_ready(Predicate ready) {
10701 // Long enough to cover a normal drain without sleeping, short enough that a
10702 // slow wait stops burning a core.
10703 static constexpr uint32_t kCallerYieldLimit = 1024;
10704 for (uint32_t spins = 0; ; ++spins) {
10705 if (ready() || !running_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
10706 return;
10707 }
10708 if (spins < kCallerYieldLimit) {
10709 std::this_thread::yield();
10710 } else {
10711 std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
10712 }
10713 }
10714}
10715
10716inline void Logger::wake_writer() noexcept {
10717 if (writer_parked_.load(std::memory_order_seq_cst)) [[unlikely]] {
10718 force_wake_writer();
10719 }
10720}
10721
10722inline void Logger::force_wake_writer() noexcept {
10723 wake_token_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_release);
10724 wake_token_.notify_all();
10725}
10726
10727inline void Logger::park_writer() {
10728 // Read the token before announcing the park: a producer that bumps it in the
10729 // window between here and wait() leaves the value different from the one
10730 // passed in, so wait() returns immediately instead of missing the wake-up.
10731 const uint32_t token = wake_token_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
10732 writer_parked_.store(true, std::memory_order_seq_cst);
10733 if (thread_rings_) {
10734 // Ring producers publish with a plain store and then read writer_parked_;
10735 // this is the fence they skip. See detail::writer_barrier_available().
10736 if (ring_fence_) {
10737 std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_seq_cst);
10738 } else {
10739 detail::writer_barrier();
10740 }
10741 }
10742
10743 // Re-check everything the park waits for. Anything that became true before
10744 // writer_parked_ became visible would otherwise never wake us.
10745 const bool work_pending =
10746 !running_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) ||
10747 flush_request_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) != flush_done_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) ||
10748 (log_queue_ && log_queue_->initial_reading_index() !=
10749 read_index_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) ||
10750 (thread_rings_ && thread_rings_pending());
10751
10752 if (!work_pending) {
10753 wake_token_.wait(token, std::memory_order_acquire);
10754 }
10755 writer_parked_.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
10756}
10757
10758inline void Logger::dispatch_entry(const LogEntry& entry) {
10759 // Lets the sinks share one formatting of this entry's message: the first to
10760 // need it formats it, the rest reuse it, and none pays if none needs it.
10761 const detail::dispatch_scope scope(dispatch_message_, entry);
10762 if (entry.sink_index >= 0 && static_cast<size_t>(entry.sink_index) < sinks_.size()) {
10763 // Write to specific sink
10764 auto& sink = sinks_[entry.sink_index];
10765 if (entry.level < sink->min_level()) {
10766 return; // Skip if log level is below sink's minimum level
10767 }
10768 sink->write(entry);
10769 }
10770 else {
10771 // Write to all non-dedicated sinks
10772 for (auto& sink : sinks_) {
10773 if (entry.level < sink->min_level() || sink->is_dedicated()) {
10774 continue; // Skip if log level is below sink's minimum level or sink is dedicated
10775 }
10776 sink->write(entry);
10777 }
10778 }
10779}
10780
10781inline size_t Logger::round_up_to_power_of_2(size_t value) noexcept {
10782 if (value & (value - 1)) {
10783 // Round up to next power of 2
10784 size_t temp = value;
10785 temp--;
10786 temp |= temp >> 1;
10787 temp |= temp >> 2;
10788 temp |= temp >> 4;
10789 temp |= temp >> 8;
10790 temp |= temp >> 16;
10791
10792#if defined(_M_X64) || defined(__x86_64__)
10793 if constexpr (sizeof(size_t) > 4) {
10794 temp |= temp >> 32;
10795 }
10796#endif
10797 return temp + 1;
10798 }
10799 return value; // Already a power of 2
10800}
10801
10802inline uint32_t Logger::normalize_items_per_slot(size_t requested, size_t string_buffer_size) noexcept {
10803 // slick-queue throws on anything but a power of 2 no larger than the ring, and a
10804 // configuration mistake is better absorbed here than turned into a failed init.
10805 // Capped at 2^31 before rounding: the largest power of 2 a uint32_t holds, and
10806 // anything above it would round to 2^32, which is 0 once cast, or already 0 in
10807 // a 32-bit size_t.
10808 constexpr size_t kMaxItemsPerSlot = size_t{1} << 31;
10809 const size_t clamped = std::clamp<size_t>(requested, 1, kMaxItemsPerSlot);
10810 return static_cast<uint32_t>(std::min(round_up_to_power_of_2(clamped), string_buffer_size));
10811}
10812
10813inline void Logger::create_local_queues(size_t log_queue_size, size_t string_buffer_size,
10814 size_t string_items_per_slot) {
10815 log_queue_ = std::make_unique<slick::queue<LogEntry, logger_queue_traits>>(static_cast<uint32_t>(log_queue_size));
10816 string_queue_ = std::make_unique<slick::queue<char, logger_queue_traits>>(
10817 static_cast<uint32_t>(string_buffer_size),
10818 normalize_items_per_slot(string_items_per_slot, string_buffer_size));
10819}

10823// Macros for easy logging
10824#if SLICK_LOGGER_ENABLE_SOURCE_LOCATION
10825#define SLICK_LOGGER_LOG_AT_CALL_SITE(logger_instance, level, ...) \
10826 do { \
10827 static constexpr const char* slick_logger_file_name__ = SLICK_LOGGER_FILE_NAME; \
10828 (logger_instance).log_with_static_location( \
10829 level, \
10830 slick::logger::Logger::static_source_location(slick_logger_file_name__), \
10831 __LINE__, __VA_ARGS__); \
10832 } while (false)
10833#else
10834#define SLICK_LOGGER_LOG_AT_CALL_SITE(logger_instance, level, ...) \
10835 (logger_instance).log(level, __VA_ARGS__)
10836#endif
10837
10838#define SLICK_LOGGER_LOG_IF_ENABLED(level, ...) \
10839 do { \
10840 auto& slick_logger_instance__ = slick::logger::Logger::instance(); \
10841 if (slick_logger_instance__.should_log(level)) { \
10842 SLICK_LOGGER_LOG_AT_CALL_SITE(slick_logger_instance__, level, __VA_ARGS__); \
10843 } \
10844 } while (false)
10845
10846#define LOG_TRACE(...) SLICK_LOGGER_LOG_IF_ENABLED(slick::logger::LogLevel::L_TRACE, __VA_ARGS__)
10847#define LOG_DEBUG(...) SLICK_LOGGER_LOG_IF_ENABLED(slick::logger::LogLevel::L_DEBUG, __VA_ARGS__)
10848#define LOG_INFO(...) SLICK_LOGGER_LOG_IF_ENABLED(slick::logger::LogLevel::L_INFO, __VA_ARGS__)
10849#define LOG_WARN(...) SLICK_LOGGER_LOG_IF_ENABLED(slick::logger::LogLevel::L_WARN, __VA_ARGS__)
10850#define LOG_ERROR(...) SLICK_LOGGER_LOG_IF_ENABLED(slick::logger::LogLevel::L_ERROR, __VA_ARGS__)
10851#define LOG_FATAL(...) SLICK_LOGGER_LOG_IF_ENABLED(slick::logger::LogLevel::L_FATAL, __VA_ARGS__)
10852
10853// ---- Sink-targeted logging ----
10854//
10855// LOG_SINK_<LEVEL>(sink, ...) routes to one sink and, unlike sink->log_<level>(...),
10856// checks both the sink's own minimum level and the global level before the
10857// arguments appear in the expansion, so a filtered-out call evaluates nothing.
10858// It also attaches the call site, which the direct sink helpers cannot.
10859//
10860// `sink` may be an ISink reference, a raw pointer, or a smart pointer, and is
10861// evaluated exactly once.
10862
10863#if SLICK_LOGGER_ENABLE_SOURCE_LOCATION
10864#define SLICK_LOGGER_LOG_TO_SINK_AT_CALL_SITE(logger_instance, sink_index, level, ...) \
10865 do { \
10866 static constexpr const char* slick_logger_file_name__ = SLICK_LOGGER_FILE_NAME; \
10867 (logger_instance).log_to_sink_with_static_location( \
10868 sink_index, \
10869 level, \
10870 slick::logger::Logger::static_source_location(slick_logger_file_name__), \
10871 __LINE__, __VA_ARGS__); \
10872 } while (false)
10873#else
10874#define SLICK_LOGGER_LOG_TO_SINK_AT_CALL_SITE(logger_instance, sink_index, level, ...) \
10875 (logger_instance).log_to_sink(sink_index, level, __VA_ARGS__)
10876#endif
10877
10878#define SLICK_LOGGER_LOG_TO_SINK_IF_ENABLED(sink, level, ...) \
10879 do { \
10880 auto* slick_logger_sink__ = slick::logger::detail::sink_ptr(sink); \
10881 auto& slick_logger_instance__ = slick::logger::Logger::instance(); \
10882 if (slick_logger_sink__ && slick_logger_sink__->should_log(slick_logger_instance__, level)) { \
10883 SLICK_LOGGER_LOG_TO_SINK_AT_CALL_SITE(slick_logger_instance__, \
10884 slick_logger_sink__->index(), level, __VA_ARGS__); \
10885 } \
10886 } while (false)
10887
10888#define LOG_SINK_TRACE(sink, ...) SLICK_LOGGER_LOG_TO_SINK_IF_ENABLED(sink, slick::logger::LogLevel::L_TRACE, __VA_ARGS__)
10889#define LOG_SINK_DEBUG(sink, ...) SLICK_LOGGER_LOG_TO_SINK_IF_ENABLED(sink, slick::logger::LogLevel::L_DEBUG, __VA_ARGS__)
10890#define LOG_SINK_INFO(sink, ...) SLICK_LOGGER_LOG_TO_SINK_IF_ENABLED(sink, slick::logger::LogLevel::L_INFO, __VA_ARGS__)
10891#define LOG_SINK_WARN(sink, ...) SLICK_LOGGER_LOG_TO_SINK_IF_ENABLED(sink, slick::logger::LogLevel::L_WARN, __VA_ARGS__)
10892#define LOG_SINK_ERROR(sink, ...) SLICK_LOGGER_LOG_TO_SINK_IF_ENABLED(sink, slick::logger::LogLevel::L_ERROR, __VA_ARGS__)
10893#define LOG_SINK_FATAL(sink, ...) SLICK_LOGGER_LOG_TO_SINK_IF_ENABLED(sink, slick::logger::LogLevel::L_FATAL, __VA_ARGS__)
